Abstraction: This is used to hide background details or any unnecessary implementation about the data so that users only see the required information. It is one of the most important and essential features of object-oriented programming

API: Application Programming Interface. A software intermediary that allows two applications to interact with each other. Each time we use an app like Facebook, send an instant message, or check the weather on our smart device, we are using an API
Business Logic: The custom rules or algorithms that handle the exchange of information between a database and user interface

Business Rules: Business Rules provide a true abstraction level and separation from the user interface. The business rule is not actively selecting user interface elements to collect input values, which allows flexible modification of the presentation and the rule itself. The same business rule can service any number of data controller views regardless of the view types
Class: This is a blueprint that defines the variables and the methods common to all objects of a certain kind
Commit: A command that is used for storing changes performed by a transaction

Deprecated: This is the process of taking older code and marking it as no longer being useful within the codebase, usually because it has been replaced by newer code. The deprecated code is not immediately removed from the codebase because doing so may cause regression errors
Entity: An entity is a real time object that is different from others. An entity can be defined using its attributes. They are a part of an entity
Entity set: It is a collection of similar entities

Flush Current Transaction: Flushing is the process of synchronising the underlying persistent store with persistable state held in memory. It will update or insert into your tables in the running transaction, but it may not commit those changes
Getter: A getter is often associated with a setter. Together they are known as accessors. Getter returns the value of the private member variable
kloBroker: KloBroker is also known as Middleware/ MW. It is a broker in between tenants, clients, and external systems
kloTuner: It is an application used for configuration of and maintaining data under the object types. It maintains the number of users, number of roles as well as Business partners
kloIDE: It is an integrated development environment for kloBase for developing applications and websites

Lisp: Lisp is the second-oldest high-level programming language after Fortran and has changed a great deal since its early days, and a number of dialects have existed over its history. Today, the most widely known general-purpose Lisp dialects are Common Lisp and Scheme

Method: A method in object-oriented programming (OOP) is a procedure associated with a message and an object. An object consists of data and behaviour; these compose an interface, which specifies how the object may be utilised by any of its various consumers
Multi-Tenant Cloud: This is a cloud computing architecture that allows customers to share computing resources in a public or private cloud

Meta Model: A metamodel or surrogate model is a model of a model, and metamodeling is the process of generating such metamodels. Thus metamodeling or meta-modelling is the analysis, construction and development of the frames, rules, constraints, models and theories applicable and useful for modelling a predefined class of problems
Object: An entity that contains both attributes and actions is its object. It is defined by its life span, name and object identifier. Every object has two components: State and Behaviour
ORM: Object Relational Mapping is a computer programming technique for converting data between incompatible type systems (Object to Relational), using object-oriented programming language

Pagination: A storage allocation technique in which programs or data are divided into fixed length blocks called pages, main storage/memory is divided into blocks of the same length called page frames, and pages are stored in page frames, not necessarily contiguously or in logical order, and pages are transferred between main and auxiliary storage as needed
Property: A property is a special class member, intermediate in functionality between a field (or data member) and a method
Query: A query is a request for data or information from a database table or combination of tables

Query tree: It is an internal representation of an SQL statement where the single parts that it is built from are stored separately. These query trees can be shown in the server log if you set the configuration parameters debug_print_parse, debug_print_rewritten, or debug_print_plan
Rollback: A transactional control language that is used to undo the transactions that have not been saved in the database
Schema: A representation of a plan or theory in the form of an outline or model
Setter: Setter is a method to set the value of any property of a private member variable. It is accompanied by Getter

Stateless Model: In simple terms, a client program makes a request to an application server, which sends data back to the client. The server treats all client connections equally and saves no information from prior requests or sessions. A website that serves up a simple static web page is a good example of the stateless model
UTC: Coordinated United Time. Prior to 1972, this time was called Greenwich Mean Time (GMT)

Automation testing is a software testing technique that uses automated tools to execute tests, compare actual and expected results, and generate reports. Automation testing aims to increase the speed and efficiency of the testing process while improving result accuracy and reliability.

To initiate automation, whether on a private or public node server, you must replace the existing openUI5112027 within the closedmodules directory with the new openUI5112027. Additionally, ensure the sap-ui-version.json file is copied into closedmodules. Following these steps, if operating on a private node, restart the server and proceed with re-registration.

WDIO is a hugely popular E2E testing framework for Web Applications. This also includes hybrid apps. It can drive a real browser and simulate a user interacting with the app. WDIO can work with apps that use any web framework but there are certain advantages if the testing framework integrates with the web framework. If this is the case, the tests could be much simpler to write and mainly, much more reliable. Reliability is of paramount importance for E2E tests that typically struggle with flakiness so any improvement can have significant effect on the TCO of testing process

Every attempt to create, update, or delete an entity takes place in the context of a transaction. A single transaction can include any number of such operations. To maintain the consistency of the data, the transaction ensures that all of the operations it contains are applied to KloBase Datastore as a unit or, if any of the operations fails, that none of them are applied. Furthermore, all strongly-consistent reads (ancestor queries or gets) performed within the same transaction observe a consistent snapshot of the data.

documents.t: By following the above instructions, you will ensure that dialogs opened using the KloController.openDialog API are closed consistently and correctly with the KloController.closeDialog API. This approach helps avoid potential issues and improves the stability and maintainability of the application.
Screenshot
Screenshot

Dialogs opened via the KloController.openDialog API should be closed using the KloController.closeDialog API, not the sap.m.Dialog's close method. The sap.m.Dialog's close method should only be used when the dialog was opened via the sap.m.Dialog.open() method.

It has been noted that some applications are using the sap.m.Dialog's close method to close dialogs that were opened via the KloController.openDialog API. This can result in inconsistencies and potential issues. To maintain uniformity and prevent problems, it is essential that the KloController.closeDialog API is used to close dialogs opened by the KloController.openDialog API.

Notification is an alert message like SMS, email and notification in an app. Notification can be sent whenever it is required. This will work similarly to an endpoint resolver (it can send notifications to multiple receivers). The notifications sharing service is done by a third-party service (fcm) provider to clients. However, the data storage, the notification body, and the channel types are all configured by us.

The Callbacks tab is available within a notification template in the Notification Editor. It allows you to register server-side callback methods that run when the notification is being processed, enabling you to attach files dynamically to outgoing emails. Each callback method is defined by a name and a sequence number that controls the order in which it is executed.

The page refers to the single visible screen of the application. The page is the topmost layer of an application. It will be embedded with a pageLayout.

The Page area is the next level in the page hierarchy after the Page Layout. Page areas are embedded with the pagelayout. The detail of the page Area that needs to be rendered for the page area will be maintained in the Page Layout’s Layout Data section.

PageLayout is the topmost layer embedded with the page. At runtime, only one pageLayout will be picked based on the device type. The detail of which pageLayout needs to be picked is maintained in the page’s properties (screencontainerdefault, screencontainerdesktop, screencontainermobile, screenontainertab). If the property for a specific device type is not maintained then the default pageLayout will be rendered.

Row wise authorization is a security feature provided by a framework with which access to entity data can be restricted to selective row items on user level. By default, when a simple select query is fired on any entity, it returns all data that is present in the entity. But, by enabling and configuring row wise authorization on an entity, the list of records accessible to any user can be controlled using access tokens.

documents.t: "Initial sync" refers to the process of syncing data from the server to the client. When a user registers, all their relevant data is transferred from the server and stored in the client’s local database, enabling the application to function offline. The term "DeviceRegisterCall" refers to the registration process of a user in a system and after this assigned flavors can be fetched for the user. ST here, stands for Start Time, which indicates the starting timestamp of an activity/process. ET here stands for End Time, which indicates the ending timestamp of an activity/process. Here, ST and ET is stored to track how much time an activity is taking to complete. noofqueries: The total number of SQL queries that has been executed during the initialSync process of a particular flavor. noofsqlrecords: The total number of data/ records that have already been fetched after executing the queries. Eg:In this case;(shown in above screenshot) 55 SQL queries were executed. A total of 1324 records data were retrieved. "queryids" typically refers to unique identifiers associated with individual SQL queries or database queries that are executed by a system. Each queryid helps track, identify, or differentiate between specific queries that are run, making it easier to debug, analyze performance, or monitor system behavior. This contains the ids of all the initial sync queries in that particular application. “ROTdownload” stands for root download. It contains the list of applications’ zips that have been downloaded. “table generator” for storing above data in the client side tables corresponding table are required. In clientGlobalObj._log is generating table logs on the client side in opfs/ sqlite db/ etc. “Before Login”, track user input, validation, and any checks made before the user is authenticated. “After Login”, track session creation, successful login, and post-login actions. “TT” often refers to Total Time. This is the amount of time it takes to complete a particular activity or query in a system. Note:Similar for every flavor as shown in the below screenshots there are activity log details of ET,noofqueries,noofsqlrecords,STATUS,Queryids,ST,and TT.

documents.t: For the app setup, any failures during the setup process (including config updates) will be displayed in the about page. Icons are used to indicate the setup status: a green icon represents success, while a red icon indicates failure.This approach provides a user-friendly and informative method for handling only the InitialSync setup issues. Clicking on the red icon opens a popup that shows any associated error messages. From the popup, users can download the logs in a .txt file format by clicking the Download Log button, or they can reinstall the app by selecting the Reinstall button. The "Download Log" option typically refers to the ability to download a record or history of events or actions taken within a specific application or system. This log file might contain useful information such as: System actions or operations performed Errors or warnings encountered timestamps The purpose of downloading the log is usually for record-keeping for understanding the system's performance. The format of the log file can be downloaded in txt format using the download log button present in the popup.

documents.t: Date of Issue: January 2023 Target Audience: Application Developers.

The below methods are for developers. All methods take two parameters, the first parameter is the definition of the callback method and the second parameter is the context of the class where that callback method is defined. Eg: clientGlobalObj.attachShowError(this._fnShowErrorPage,this); Here fnShowErrorPage is the method definition you want to attach to an attachShowError method and this is class context or class ‘this’ where fnShowErrorPage is defined attachShowError( errFn , context ) Attach your error page to what you want to display in the UI when any error comes. Framework will internally call this method when any error comes. attachLoadComponent(loadComponentFn,context) Attach your component method using this function. Components can be seam4 components or any other SAP component. By default, the framework uses the kloTouch component to load after registration. attachOfflinePageLockMethod(offlinePageLockFn,context) Attach your offline lock method which will be called during offline login by the framework. attachForgetPasswordOffline(offlineForgetPasswordFn,context) Attach your offline forget password UI method by calling the upper method which will be internally called by the framework to display the offline forget password page. clientGlobalObj.htmlBanner.showHTMLUpgradeBanner(actionButtonEventHandler,targetContainerId,message?:string,actionButtonText?,timeLimitInMinutes?:number, timerLimitInTimestamp?) Attach your html banner on the top level of the page by calling the upper method. 5.1. Parameters - actionButtonEventHandler (mandatory) - A reference to the function that will be called when the user clicks on the action button present in the banner or after the specified time passes. targetContainerId (mandatory) - This will take the html container id. To use the banner similar to the upgrade banner, provide “html_banner_container” as the value. Message (optional)- This will take the message to be displayed in the banner. By default it takes the hardcoded Upgrade message. actionButtonText (optional)- This will take the text to be displayed in the action button. By default it takes hardcoded text ”Upgrade Now”. timeLimitInMinutes (optional)- This will take the time for which the banner will be displayed. Value must be in minutes, once the time limit is expired/once the user is clicking on the action button, the actionButtonEventHandler will be called automatically. By default, it is set to 3 minutes. timerLimitInTimestamp (optional)- This is the same as the above time limit, it can be passed in timestamp. 6.clientGlobalObj.clearAllData() - It removes data from Local Storage, Session Storage, and any cached data. After the data is cleared, the page will reload, and the user will be redirected to the registration page. For devices with QR functionality enabled, the user will be directed to the QR scanner page. Note: It is recommended to use this API only when necessary, as it may result in data loss.

ClientGlobalObj of the ClientGlobal class of ADM clients is available globally to be used by application developers. It provides the following variables and methods which help application developers to configure different aspects of client features. ADM client registration log details are also explained in this document.

Variables are recommended for changes in the index.html page after rendering of ClientGlobal class. For example, suppose the variable name is a system so in index.html it is changed as clientGlobalObj.system = “KLARION” clientGlobalObj.system = "KLARION"; system - Used to specify the system in which an application is running. Currently, there are only two values that can be used i.e. KLARION or SAP. By default the system value is Klarion. public system: "KLARION" | "SAP" = 'KLARION'; deviceType - Used to specify the device in which the application is running. Values are browser or cordova. Currently, its value is maintained automatically depending on the device type i,e if the device is a browser then the value is a browser and if it is cordova (Mobile) then its value is cordova. public deviceType: "Cordova" | "Browser"; sapUITheme - Used to set sap UI library themes. The default value is sap_belize_plus public sapUITheme: string = "sap_belize_plus"; sapUIVersion - Used to set the sap UI library version. The default value is 1.102.7 public sapUIVersion:string = "1.102.7" appName - Used to specify the name of the application. It is used to construct url SAP related URLs for seam4 type of application Eg: moast4, seam4 etc. baseRot - List of rot/app/flavor which can be mentioned at the beginning in index.html, which will be downloaded and extracted before the registration page is visible. Note: - Until the baseRot is downloaded, the user cannot perform any kind of operation. Treat it as a mandatory rot/app/flavor which is required before the user can perform any operation Structure of list: [{r_flavor:string,r_version:string,r_buildNo:number}] public baseRot:Array<{r_flavor:string,r_version:string,r_buildno:number}> = []; extendedRot - List of rot/app / flavortotally similar to baseRot with only one difference: it will get downloaded and extracted in the background. I.e User will not have to wait to begin any operation. Structure of list: [{r_flavor:string,r_version:string,r_buildNo:number}] public extendedRot:Array<{r_flavor:string,r_version:string,r_buildno:number}> = []; documentTitle - Used to specify title value in the title tag of html page. For more information refer to https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/title isLog - Boolean value to enable or disable clientGlobalObject log. The log can be accessed using clientGlobalObject._log preloadScript - List of script files with the proper path which can be mentioned in the index.html file which will get loaded in the client before the user can perform any operation. Eg: clientGlobalObj.preloadScript=["closedmodules/kloExternal/core.js"] postLoadScript - List of script files with a proper path similar to preloadScript with only one difference. Users do not have to wait for the script to load to perform any operation. enableBioMetric - its value is either true or false based on that you will view a biometric login at the offline login page. By default true is maintained is_browser_sync - value is either true or false. If true then the middleware works through the index DB of the client and if the value is false or not maintained then the middleware works through the sync adapter. oUIConfig - It is an object containing a key-value pair which is used to hide or show a particular view/div in the index.html page. Note: Developers can add more key value in this object for their usage. Key value pair listed below:
[TABLE]

documents.t: Application URLs support version-based access using the following format: https://<domain>/appservice/<landscape>/<flavor>_<version>/<api_id> where <version> follows the format: <major>-<minor>-<patch> When resolving an application version: The specified major and minor versions are honored. The system automatically resolves the request to the latest available patch version within the specified major.minor version. Example​ Available versions: 7-0-1 7-0-5 7-0-20 Request: /appservice/prod/mobile_7-0-1/api123 Resolved Version: 7-0-20 Similarly, if versions 8-1-3, 8-1-10, and 8-2-5 are available: Request: /appservice/prod/mobile_8-1-3/api123 Resolved Version: 8-1-10 This behavior ensures that consumers automatically receive the latest available patch fixes and improvements within the requested major.minor release stream without requiring URL updates.

documents.t: Add your new automation folder inside allAutomation folder. Here You’ll need to incorporate the automation files and folders you’ve created, following a standard project structure. Changes in conf.Data.js If you're running automations locally, your conf.data.js file may contain hardcoded values, as shown in the example below. However, in AWS, all configurations in conf.data.js are dynamic and sourced from master.conf.json. Add the following import statement at the top of your conf.data.js: import masterConf from '../master.conf.json' with {type: "json"}; Open master.conf.json and check whether the variables you need are already declared.If they are missing, add them manually. Replace hardcoded values in conf.data.js with references to the corresponding variables from masterConf. Refer to the example shown in the image below for guidance. Changes in KloAuWdio.js file inside kloAU folder in a automation If you're running automations locally, your kloAuWdio.js file may contain hardcoded values in the args section of config, as shown in the example below. However, in AWS, all configurations in conf.data.js are dynamic and sourced from master.conf.json. Add the following import statement at the top of your kloAuWdio.js: import masterConf from '../master.conf.json' with {type: "json"}; Then, replace all hardcoded values in conf.data.js with references to the corresponding variables from masterConf. These changes ensure that your automation setup is flexible and optimized for dynamic execution in AWS environments. Refer to the example shown in the image below for guidance. Changes in master.bat In master.bat, add the path to the newly added automation. Refer to the following code snippet for guidance: The first line navigates to the folder created with the current date. The second line navigates to the target repository inside that folder (i.e., the newly added automation). Inside that folder, a new command prompt is opened and npx wdio is executed to start the automation. The output of the automation running in the command prompt is saved to Regression.txt(change the name according to the automation created). Once the automation completes, the message "npx wdio is completed" is appended to log.txt. Changes in checkforcompletion.bat Update the count based on the number of new automations added. For example, if you’ve added 2 new automations, increase the count by 2.So, if the original count was 24, update it to 26. Changes in copyandgeneratereport.bat The copyandgeneratereport.bat script is primarily used to copy report and log files between systems and to an S3 bucket. In addition to file transfers, it also generates reports that are intended to be attached in emails. ::------ Copy of Automations report files one directory back ------- copy "Flavor_Build\reports\Flavor_Build.html" ".\ copy "Unique_Key_1\reports\Unique_Key_1.html" ".\ copy "Unique_Key_2\reports\Unique_Key_2.html" ".\ copy "Vh_Testing\reports\Vh_Testing.html" ".\ The code snippet shown above copies HTML report files from their respective automation subdirectories—such as Flavor_Build, Unique_Key_1, Unique_Key_2, and Vh_Testing—into the parent directory, which corresponds to the automation folder within the date-specific folder. This intermediate step organizes the reports in a central location, preparing them for a subsequent move to the final reports folder in later stages of the script. So if you are adding any new automation add a new line here by changing you automation folder name and report name. If you're adding a new automation, make sure to include a new line in this section by specifying the appropriate automation folder name and the corresponding report file name. ::-----------------GENERATE REPORT-------------------------------- call finalreportgenerater.bat Bol_Editor_A1 call finalreportgenerater.bat Bol_Editor_A2 call finalreportgenerater.bat Bol_Editor_A3 call finalreportgenerater.bat Bol_Editor_A4 This part of the script runs finalreportgenerater.bat for each automation module to generate a summary of its test results. The batch file reads the current date, locates the module’s HTML report, extracts key metrics like pass/fail counts and execution time, and formats them into HTML summary lines. These lines are then added to categorized report files—report_pass.txt, report_fail.txt, or report_notRun.txt—based on the outcome. Each summary includes links to the full reports stored in an S3 bucket, making it easy to access detailed results. If you're adding a new automation, be sure to add a new line in this section using the correct automation folder name—assuming the folder name matches the report file name. This part of the script copies all the log files from the date-specific folder inside the automation directory to the reports folder. From there, the files are uploaded to an S3 bucket, making them publicly accessible from anywhere. If you're adding a new automation, make sure to include a new line in this section by specifying the appropriate automation log file name. This part of the script copies all the report files from the date-specific folder inside the automation directory to the reports folder. From there, the files are uploaded to an S3 bucket, making them publicly accessible from anywhere. If you're adding a new automation, make sure to include a new line in this section by specifying the appropriate automation folder name and the corresponding report file name.

documents.t: To begin preparing your latest branch for the desired configuration, you'll first need to clone it locally using Visual Studio Code. This step ensures you have a working copy of the branch on your machine, allowing you to make the necessary changes and test them efficiently. Before cloning, make sure you're logged into Bitbucket within VS Code—this will streamline access to your repositories and avoid any authentication issues during the process. Once the branch is successfully cloned, you can proceed to update its configuration. Whether it's modifying environment variables, updating dependency files, or adjusting runtime settings, this step ensures your branch is tailored to run as intended on a specific server. Navigate to the source section of the kloAutomation repository.Click on the Clone option. Select Clone in VS Code. This will launch your VS Code editor. VS Code will open the Command Palette automatically.Choose "Clone a new copy" from the Command Palette. Select the folder where you want to save the cloned repository. When prompted, choose "Open in New Window" to view the cloned repo separately. In the bottom-left corner of VS Code, you'll see a branch icon showing the current branch—usually set to main by default. Click on the main branch label to open the Command Palette again. A list of available branches will appear. Select your newly created branch from the list. Confirm that the branch name in the bottom-left corner has changed from main to your selected branch.
documents.s: Cloning a Branch Using Visual Studio Code
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/AWS Automation/Cloning a Branch Using Visual Studio Code

documents.t: Navigate to the Branches section in the Bitbucket interface for the kloAutomation repository. Click on “Create Branch.” In the “From Branch” field, select the branch that contains the most recent commits (typically the latest stable version). Enter the desired name for your new branch. Click “Create” to generate the new branch. Your newly created branch will be an exact copy of the selected source branch and ready for further development or customization.

To run AWS automation on your local system, begin by downloading the AWS automation ZIP file from Bitbucket. Choose your preferred repository from the available options. Once selected, go to the Source section and pick the branch you want to work with. Click the three-dot menu (⋯) to reveal additional options. Select "Download Repository" to save the ZIP file locally.

documents.t: After registration in AWS, the menu wasn’t always clickable—automation was jumping ahead before it had finished loading. To further stabilize post-registration behavior—especially in AWS environments where UI components may load asynchronously—a new safeguard was introduced to ensure the ham menu expansion completes before proceeding. This was necessary because menu navigation was intermittently failing when the automation advanced before the menu system had fully initialized. Waits up to 5 times with 2-second intervals to check if the ham menu grid (__cssgrid0)(id for the whole menu ) is expanded. Uses data-menu2hbox attribute to determine expansion state (expanded-true). This checks whether the menu is expanded or not. Logs each attempt with detailed status messages for visibility and debugging. If not expanded, triggers the SAPUI5 firePress() event on the ham button (ham) to manually initiate expansion. Handles errors gracefully during both state checks and press events. Waits between retries to allow UI components time to load and respond. Provides a final summary indicating whether the menu successfully expanded or failed after all attempts. Note: To use the checkHamMenuExpansion function effectively, you must first trigger a click on the ham menu first in the data file and then using a separate function called menuSelectionLogin. This is necessary because, in the earlier approach, we used a function named menuSelection, which handled both the expansion of the hamburger menu and the selection of the menu header and its child items. However, since checkHamMenuExpansion now explicitly checks whether the hamburger menu is expanded—and expands it only if needed—we need to ensure the menu is clicked once beforehand. That initial click is handled in the data file before invoking checkHamMenuExpansion. If the menu is already expanded, the function does nothing; otherwise, it triggers the expansion. After confirming the menu state, we then call menuSelectionLogin to proceed with selecting the appropriate menu header and child. We avoid using menuSelection here because it includes its own ham menu click logic, which could interfere with the flow—causing the menu to open and then immediately close if called after checkHamMenuExpansion. At the same time, we can't remove the hamburger click from menuSelection entirely, as it's still needed in scenarios where the page is refreshed and the menu state resets. The structure of the new menu selection code in data file is illustrated below ➖

documents.t: Open Bitbucket and go to the Repositories section. From the list, select your target repository (in our case, klo_automation). Once inside the repository, navigate to the Pipelines tab Click on Run Pipeline. From the branch dropdown, choose the branch you want to run. Next, select the pipeline type from the pipeline dropdown — you’ll see two options: custom: run-public-master1 → Use this if your server is publicly accessible (e.g., our 42 and 36 servers) and you want to run Editors automation. custom: run-public-master2 → Use this if your server is publicly accessible (e.g., our 42 and 36 servers) and you want to run tools and other automation. custom: run-private-master1 → Use this if your server is not publicly accessible (e.g., server 22) and you want to run Editors automation. custom: run-private-master1 → Use this if your server is not publicly accessible (e.g., server 22) and you want to run tools and other automation.

documents.t: In Bitbucket Pipelines, you can schedule a pipeline so it runs automatically at specific times without manually triggering it. 1. Open the Repository Go to Bitbucket → Repositories → Select your repository (e.g., klo_automation). 2. Go to Pipeline Settings Navigate to Pipelines → Click on Schedules in the left-hand menu. 3. Create a New Schedule Click Add schedule (or Create schedule, depending on your Bitbucket version). 4. Configure the Schedule Branch → Choose the branch you want the pipeline to run on. Pipeline → Select which pipeline definition to run (e.g., custom: run-public-master1 or custom: run-public-master2 or custom: run-private-master1 or run-private-master2). Frequency → Choose how often it should run: Daily Weekly Custom CRON (for advanced scheduling, like every 15 mins, every Monday at 9 AM, etc.). Example CRON expressions in Bitbucket: 0 9 * * * → Every day at 9:00 AM. 0 */6 * * * → Every 6 hours. 30 2 * * 1 → Every Monday at 2:30 AM. Note :- when you schedule a pipeline in Bitbucket, all times are interpreted in UTC, not your local time. 5. Save the Schedule Click Save. Bitbucket will now automatically trigger the pipeline according to the schedule you set.

documents.t: Date of Issue: July 2025 Target Audience: Testing Team, Automation Developers Prepared by: Ankit Sen Platform Version: 7.0 A User Manual for application creation, knowledge and work reference.

The original registration script was built with a linear, pause-heavy structure. It relied on fixed browser.pause() intervals between navigation steps and form interactions, assuming that the UI and backend would be ready within those timeframes. It performed the following steps: Navigated to multiple URLs in sequence. Executed clientGlobalObj.clearAllData() to reset client-side state. Waited for login input fields using waitForDisplayed() and filled them with credentials. Click the login and accept buttons. Entered a polling loop to check if registration was completed via localStorage. However, this approach had critical limitations: It did not verify if the page was fully ready before interacting with elements. It lacked error handling and diagnostics (e.g., no screenshots or logs for debugging). It assumed that all required data (like endPointId or downloaded files) would be available immediately after navigation. In AWS environments, this led to blank screens during registration because some asynchronous calls were still in progress, and the automation moved ahead too quickly. The structure of the previous registration code are illustrated below ➖ To address the shortcomings of the earlier implementation—especially the blank screen issue observed in AWS environments—the registration script was redesigned with a more resilient, diagnostic-driven approach. The updated code introduces structured polling, conditional logic, and robust error handling to ensure the automation waits for all necessary conditions before proceeding. It now performs the following steps: Waits for endPointId to appear in sessionStorage, retrying for up to 2 minutes and logging progress with screenshots. Polls localStorage for <landscape>_FILES_DOWNLOADED status, ensuring all relevant flavors (excluding openUI5 and openUI6) report "DONE" before continuing. Navigates through multiple URLs with retry logic, waiting for the #loginHeader element to confirm page readiness. Executes clientGlobalObj.clearAllData() only when required, improving efficiency and reducing unnecessary resets. Overrides window.confirm() to auto-accept prompts, preventing modal interruptions during automation. Waits for login input fields to become visible before entering credentials, using retry loops to handle delayed rendering. Ensures the #btn_accept button is visible, enabled, and scrolled into view before clicking, improving interaction reliability. Polls for registration completion for up to 9 minutes, checking for the _IS_APP_INSTALLTION_COMPLETED flag in localStorage. Injects UI5 and captures the client version once registration is confirmed, completing the flow with contextual awareness. These changes were introduced specifically to resolve issues in AWS environments, where backend or client-side calls were taking longer to complete after navigation. The earlier code did not wait for these asynchronous operations, causing the automation to proceed prematurely and resulting in blank screens. The new implementation ensures readiness at every step, making the registration flow stable, reliable, and cloud-friendly. The structure of the new registration code are illustrated below ➖ Note: Automation running on private nodes uses a different registration flow. Please review and update your code accordingly.

Modify the privateBaseUrl, publicUi5Url, and publicBaseUrl fields in the master.conf.json file to match your server's URL settings.Ensure that all user accounts referenced in the image below are accurately set up and maintained on your server. In both startingAutomation.ps1 and endAutomation.ps1, update the email subject lines to include accurate server details.This ensures that the emails received clearly reflect the correct server environment, making them easier to identify and track. Change the Flavor names and versions in every automation conf.data.js file.

All modifications applied to public automations are equally applicable to private Node automations. However, setting up a private node is your responsibility. To do this: Place the openUI5_1_120_27 package inside the closedmodules directory, as it's required for running the automation. Update the private node URL in the master.conf.json file accordingly. Once these steps are completed, the remaining process mirrors that of public automations, and your private automation setup will be ready to run.

Now after node modules installation is completed, Navigate to your automation folder which you want to run individually and open that in any code editor to edit. documents.t: Previously, in the automation flows, whenever a busy indicator appeared, the scripts would automatically pause and wait for it to disappear before continuing. However, in recent runs—even in local environments also—the automations have stopped waiting for the busy indicator or busy dialog to fully disappear, causing them to proceed prematurely to the next steps. To address this issue, we've introduced the waitForBusyIndicator function. This asynchronous method ensures that the automation process pauses until the busy dialog has completely disappeared before continuing. Note: Our application uses two types of busy elements: sapMBusyDialog and sapMBusyIndicator. Please inspect your screen or application via the browser console to determine which one is currently in use. It repeatedly checks for the presence of the busy dialog every 2 seconds (CHECK_INTERVAL). If the dialog is visible, it continues to wait. Once the dialog is no longer detected, it waits an additional 10 seconds (WAIT_AFTER_CLOSE) to confirm it doesn't reappear. If the dialog remains gone, the loop exits and automation continues. Any errors during the check will also break the loop and log the issue. The structure of the new Wait for Busy Indicator code are illustrated below ➖

documents.t: In previous automation runs, registration occasionally failed silently—resulting in an "Oops" page without any visible error. Interestingly, re-registering often resolved the issue. To address this inconsistency, we’ve introduced a new checkRegistration() function. This function verifies whether the registration process has completed successfully. If not, it automatically re-invokes the appropriate registration function to retry the process. Important Implementation Notes: Replace the placeholder function name shown in the image with your actual registration function name. Depending on your setup, the registration function may be named register, login, or something else—ensure consistency when integrating checkRegistration().

Previously, automation processes occasionally failed due to the unexpected appearance of an upgrade popup during execution. To address this issue, we introduced the noUpgradeFunction(), which effectively suppresses the upgrade popup and ensures smoother automation flow. Important Usage Notes: The upgrade popup suppression must be re-applied after each registration and after every page refresh. This is necessary because the overridden function responsible for suppressing the popup is reset to its original state upon page reload.

documents.t: App Branching is done to create a branch of the actual app. This branch will be helpful in cases where the team wants to work on next-phase developments and at the same time provide fixes for the released application. Developers can create a new branch for the next phase of development and use this for the developments. When the developments are complete, the branch can be merged with the latest version of the app. To simplify this let's take a look at the below explanation: In the above diagram, we have an app named eam_6.0.1. Now there is a major enhancement that needs to be done for this app. This enhancement might take a long period to develop. This will automatically pause the further development progress of the app. Therefore, we will create a branch for this app. All the major developments will be done in this branch app. In the meantime, minor fixes and other changes are made to the main app and the versions are updated. Once the enhancement is complete the branch app will be exported along with the latest version and both will be merged into one major app version as the final product.

Step 1: From the menu navigate to the App Management page of the Workspace Hub. Step 2: Navigate to the App by clicking on the app link from the app list for which the branch needs to be created from the apps list section. Step 3: Create a branch for the app by clicking on the Branch action button. It will create a new branch version for the selected app. Note: Branches button will be enabled only on the released app version Note: If the app version is of type branch then the branch checkbox will be enabled. Step 4: Change the version if needed and click on the save button to save the changes. Now, our Branch app has been created. Step 5: Assign the users for this new branch in the roles & users tab(need to be manually added, will not be copied from the branched version) NOTE : Branch flavors cannot be transported or moved to any system. For doing so, create a new version, merge that branch to the new version and then move the new version to any system.
documents.s: Process to create an app branch

documents.t: It allows developers to compare two apps and prepare a newly exported (zip) file that can be imported to another app.

Step 1: Go to the export section, fill in the required fields and click on download. App ID: Flavor ID name. Version: Version of the flavor. Export: Export the flavor directly. This will create a zip in the server. Download: The download button will download the zip of the given flavor. NOTE: Export both the apps' zip for merging purposes. Step 2: Go to the compare section and upload both the zip files to Set 1 and Set 2. Set 1: App 1 zip which will compare with Set 2. Set 2: App 2 zip which will compare to Set 1. Step 3: After uploading the Zips, click on the compare action button. Compare button will list down all the differences between your apps. Child - It shows whether the relations of the root object are different. SET1 Vs SET2 - compares whether the root object( like m_entities, mu_screen, etc.) is same, different, or present only in one of the sets. Merge(O)- It will merge the whole object (like m_entities, mu_screen, etc..) Merge(O) field has a drop-down which has Vh items and a description of Vh items are mentioned below: Delete: It will delete the particular object from Merging. Set 1: After selecting SET 1, the object of set 1 will be added for Merging. Or we can say, it will pick the object from set 1 for Merging. Set 2: After selecting SET 2, the object of set 2 will be added for Merging. Or it will pick the object from set 1 for Merging. Merge(A)- It will merge the particular attribute(e.g. properties) of the object. We can also provide custom values via using Merge(A)- CUSTOM. Merge(A) field has a drop-down which has Vh items and the description of Vh items is mentioned below: Default: Contributes to the default way of merging. Custom: Custom is used to add custom values for attributes of the object. NOTE: Special care needs to be taken while merging, If you are adding property then property type also needs to be added. After clicking on any row, the difference between the two flavors for that row will be listed in another table. Properties: Properties of the object or attributes Set 1: Shows the values of properties Set 2: Shows the values of properties Custom: Used to add custom values for object attributes (e.g properties) Red dots (⬤): It specifies that the particular object or attributes have differences between the flavors Yellow Highlight will specify the exact difference of the selected object or attribute. Step 4: Click on the merge action button, A zip will be downloaded. Step 5: Create a new version of the app and import the downloaded ZIP to it. For importing, go to the import section and upload a Zip file using the Upload zip file button. Importing- app: The app id which you want to import. Importing- Version: The app ID which you want to import. Build: to build the app which you want to import. Update Schema: do updateSchema for the app which you want to import. Copy config data: copy the config data for the app which you want to import. Fill in the mandatory fields and click on the Submit button. Step 6: see the dialogue Import Status to check the status of the import. Step 7: After importing the app, the app needs to be published. This can be done via the Workspace Hub’s App Management page.

documents.t: The Status Change Process is used for segregating the version and branch hierarchy process to identify each dependent app and sequence. From Active, status can be changed to Released, Discarded. From Released, status can be changed to Deprecated. Deprecated: No users should be assigned to the App. Discarded: All the changes in the app will be discarded and not be considered in the main branch. Only from the Released version, a new version can be created. Only from Active Version, a new Branch can be created. Development can be only done in the App with Active Status. A branch can be ACTIVE, DEPRECATED, or DISCARDED.

documents.t: App Cache Settings, as the name suggests, is for developers as a helping tool while developing applications. Previously, if any offline entity was created, any metadata was updated, or any entry was made in the server-side database, it required developers to clear their cache and do registration again to get it reflected in the browser. To resolve that issue, a App Cache Settings is introduced. Now, developers can update zip, drop and create web SQL tables, update configs (eg: vh configs), and do initial sync to get server data without any middleware sync (sync of data in the background whenever the device/browser is online). Note: The App Cache Settings should be handled by developers only to avoid any inconsistency or failure in the application.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/App Cache Settings/About App Cache Settings

documents.t: The App Cache Settings looks like a table with various features. Following are the details of those features: Features Description Zip Update Update the zip of any application in the browser. It will update offline files (files which are coming from browser cache) Table Generation (web SQL) Table generation provides two options: • Drop tables and create new ones. This means the old table will be dropped and a new table will be created instead. • Delete the data from the existing table. Initial Sync Here you will be able to get data from the server database into browser web SQL tables. A Web SQL is a database at the client side (browser or device). Update Config Update application-related configs. (eg- vh config)
documents.s: Features of the App Cache Settings

documents.t: App merging is the process of merging one application branch with the current main branch (or vice versa) or merging one active branch into another active branch. It is important to note that this process merges metadata only.

Need to assign cockpit and account flavors Developer access is required to work on the targeted flavor. Deployment of the app/flavor should occur within a development environment. If you're merging into the main version, the main version must be active; if merging into a branch version, then the branch must be active. For Example: From version 1.0.2 of our app, we created a new branch, 1.0B.2, for developing a new feature. While the feature is being developed, changes may still occur in the main branch. Once the new feature is completed, we need to merge it back into the main branch. Version Type Description Example Base Version The starting version from which the branch was created. 1.0.2 Latest Main Version The most recent, stable version of the main branch. 1.0.5 Branch Version The version where the new feature has been developed. 1.0B.2
For the application merge, we need to consider three versions of the application: Target Version Source Version Base Version

The Target Version is where the changes will be applied after the merge. It is pre-filled by default based on where the user initiated the merge from. If the user navigates from a Branch, then that branch is the Target. If the user navigates from a Latest Main Version, then that main version is the Target. User Navigated From Target Version A Branch That Branch A Main Version That Main Version

The Source Version is selected by the user from a dropdown. The dropdown options depend on the type of Target: Target Type Source Options Branch Main Released Versions, Active Branches Main Version Only Branches of the App

The Base Version is automatically determined based on the selected Source and Target. It represents the common ancestor between the two — the point from which both versions diverged. You want to compare how both the Source and Target have changed since they split from the same origin — that's the Base. Usually, the Base Version is the version from which: The Branch was created, or The Main Version was forked for changes. Scenario Base Version Logic Branch → Main 🔄 Main → Branch The version from which the Branch was created The version from which the Branch was created Branch → Branch The most recent common version in both branch sequences

If there is any altered content in both the Latest Main Version and the Branch Version, it will be considered a conflict and must be resolved by the developer (user). The user will be presented with a selection option to choose either the Main Version or the Branch Version for the merge. Any further modifications can be made after the merge is imported into the version if needed. The conflicts should be resolved by the user based on their selection and any required adjustments as shown below; **Example: ** To illustrate the merge concepts discussed above, let's consider a simple scenario. **Case 1: Auto-Merge ** The title on our screen is "App Console". In the Branch Version, we are updating the title to "Workspace Hub". **Case 2: Auto-Merge **The title on our screen is "App Console". In the Main Branch Version, we are changing the title to "Workspace Hub". During the merge, the changes will be compared with the three sets, and it will be determined that the update is only in the Main Branch Version. Since this is an update exclusive to the Main Branch, it will be auto-merged into the branch without any conflicts. **Case 3: Conflict ** The title on our screen is "App Console". In the Branch Version, we are changing the title to "Workspace Hub". In the Main Version, we are changing the title to "Account Cockpit". During the merge, the changes will be compared across the three sets. It will be determined that there are changes in both the Branch Version and the Main Version when compared to the Base Version. This results in a conflict, as both versions have different updates to the title. The user will need to manually resolve this conflict by selecting the appropriate title or making adjustments as needed. Aspect Details Merge Target Only the active version (Main or Branch) can receive merged changes. Merge Concurrency Only one branch merge at a time is allowed. No support for simultaneous merges. Automatic Merge Scope Only metadata merges are handled automatically. Manual Merge Required Files like controllers, entities, queries, utils, resources require manual intervention. Unchanged Items No changes are applied if items are identical across all three versions (Base, Branch, Main). Auto-Merge Conditions Change exists only in Branch Version → Auto-merge Change exists only in Latest Main Version → Auto-merge Conflict Handling - If conflicts exist, they must be resolved manually by the user. - Compare Branch vs Base and Main vs Base to identify differences. - Then compare the resulting changes for conflicts. Default Target The Target App Version is pre-filled based on the version/branch the user navigated from. Source Options Based on Target Type If Target is a Branch, Source dropdown lists Released Main versions and Active Branches. If Target is a Main version, Source dropdown lists only Branches. Base Version Selection Automatically determined based on Source and Target versions. Supported Merge Directions ✅ Branch → Main ✅ Main → Branch ✅ Branch → Branch

A:If the build fails or the user refreshes the screen, the process will resume from the build stage, not from the merge stage. documents.s: ❓:What happens if the build fails or the page is refreshed during the process?

documents.t: **A:**If there is a conflict — such as an app merge issue or a failure in two processes — a conflict screen will appear. This screen allows the user to resolve the conflicts before continuing with the merge. Additionally, if config data is present in the flavor, and the buildconfig, or any other process fails, the conflict screen will also appear to let the user address the issue before proceeding.
documents.s: **❓:**What happens if there is a conflict during the process?

documents.t: **A:**If the process is canceled or the screen is refreshed or the browser is changed, or an error occurs, the conflict screen will not reappear if the app merge has already been completed. In this case, the process will resume from where it left off — except when copying config data. If the interruption happens during the config copy stage, the process will restart from getting the app details.

Maintaining a proper hierarchy between app versions is crucial for accurate dependency management, for this a correct approach to establish a multi-level hierarchy is required, ensuring that dependencies are calculated correctly. To maintain the hierarchy effectively, it always starts from the top-most parent and works your way down to the bottom-most child. Example: Current Versions: A-1 (Top-most Parent) B-1 C-1 D-1 (Bottom-most Child) Correct Hierarchy: A-1 -> B-1 -> C-1 -> D-1 Note: To ensure accurate dependency management; Always maintain hierarchy from the top-most parent to the bottom-most child. This method prevents errors in dependency calculations and keeps the app structure coherent.

Transport works on a pull mechanism where the target system asks for the latest update from the source system. All the below activities needed to be done on the target system. NOTE : Branch flavors cannot be transported or moved to any system. For doing so, create a new version, merge that branch to the new version and then move the new version to any system. Step 1: Go to the menu options and select App Lifecycle**.** Step 2: Transport has two screens. App Migration and Script Repository. App Migration - This screen will display all the apps in the selected source system, as well as any apps that are already installed in the current system.It allows you to see which apps are available for transport and which ones are already installed. Script Repository - In this screen, we can get all the scripts that are maintained in the current system.

When you install an app in a DEV landscape, App transport asks whether to install it As Readable or As Writable. The choice decides what is copied to the target landscape and what you can change there afterward. As Readable (Read-Only) As Writable What is moved The built application package (zip) only The app’s full metadata from the source DEV landscape Can the app be developed in the target? No Yes Can App Dependencies be maintained? No (see below) Yes Typical use Consuming an app as-is, e.g., in QA/PROD or as a parent app Continuing development in another DEV landscape Why App Dependencies can’t be maintained for a Read-Only app A Read-Only app has no metadata in the target landscape. It only has its built package. Maintaining App Dependencies writes a generated sequence to the database, and the app must be built again afterward. A Read-Only app can’t be built in the target landscape, so its dependencies can’t be changed there. Example: VP depends on OHR (VP ← OHR). If the dependency configuration has to change on the OHR side, OHR must be installed As Writable. Alternatively, make the change in the source landscape and migrate it again. Note: If you might need to change an app’s dependencies in the target landscape, install it As Writable. [Confirm] Whether a Read-Only app can be switched to Writable later, or must be reinstalled.

Transport is a tool that deploys applications from one server to another. It is mainly aimed at deploying from a dev system to QA system and from QA to PROD system but can be used across any system. Transportation of an application can be from: DEV to QA QA to PROD DEV to DEV Steps involved: DEV to QA Setup - Doing entries in tables like madm_app, madm_app_grp etc. Download- Downloading and extracting application zips from the source. Update Schema - Creating tables on the server for entities of that app. Finalizing - Making the app ACTIVE so that everyone can use it.

Maintain this configuration in target’s config file. (present in <landscape>/kloconfig/config.json) "mm_klo_online_server": { "serverUrl": "https://dev.procify38.com", "Landscape": "tools_dev6", "username": "transport", "password": "1", "realm": "cloud_app" }, Where, serverUrl is the source system’s url, landscape - source System’s landscape, username - one specific user should be there with transport flavor assigned to it. password- password for that user realm - keycloak’s realm Maintain host file entry for the source system in the target system transport_1 app should be assigned to the user.

Transport takes care of the following: Maintaining entries of applications in tables like madm_app,mf_fl,mf_fv etc., if any. Moving application zips across the system (QA or PROD system) and extracting them. Getting the metadata of the application from the source DEV system and extracting it in the target DEV system. Running automated scripts if maintained. Track manual scripts and run when required. Publishing Application. Doing an updated schema on the application.

When creating a build URL, the current klobase version (known as bol_version) must be included for the core_fw component. The bol_version indicates the version of the build running on the system and should be included in the URL to generate the correct build.

Suppose the current bol_version running in the system is 7-2-27. Previous Build URL​ Before adopting the current_bol_version, the build URL would look like this: https://dev.procifynow.com/node/EAM/core_fw_6-0/generateBuild?fv=my_test_6-0-1&buildtype= Current Build URL (7-- onwards)​ After updating to the current bol_version (7-2-27), the build URL format will be updated as follows: https://dev.procifynow.com/node/\<landscape>/core_fw_<current_bol_version>/generateBuild?fv=<flavor_name>_<flavor_version>&buildtype=<typeofBuild> For the example provided with a current_bol_version of 7-2-27, the updated URL would look like this: https://dev.procifynow.com/node/EAM/core_fw_7-2-27/generateBuild?fv=my_test_6-0-1&buildtype=devbuild **Note: ** To generate a build URL for the core_fw version: Retrieve the current bol_version from the system using clientGlobalObj._bolVersion. Update the URL with the correct core_fw version and the appropriate build type. Use the following format: https://dev.procifynow.com/node/\<landscape>/core_fw_<current_bol_version>/generateBuild?fv=<flavor_name>_<flavor_version>&buildtype=<typeofBuild> This ensures the build URL points to the correct version and build type for the system.

Url: https://maven63.com/node/mytrunk/core_fw_6-0/generateBuild?fv=app_1&buildType=checkstatus If Status is In Queue: This status indicates that your build request is waiting to be processed. The reason for the delay could be that another flavor build is currently being processed on the server. Once the server finishes the other build, your build will be processed next. In Process: This status means that your flavor build is currently being processed on the server. It’s in progress, and the system is actively working on your build. Format: <flavor>_<version> (underscore between flavor and version) Parameter values can be allFlavor or any individual flavor name or multiple flavors separated by a comma. Parameter Values Functionality allFlavor This will build all the flavors maintained in the flavor master table, excluding account and core_fw flavor.

build_type also known as task_type defines the behavior of flavor build. The build type defines the type of build being generated. The available options are below in the list ; Build type Functionality devBuild Build files will be unminified i.e., the codes and script files are not minimized. prodBuild Build files will be minified i.e., minimizing code and script files. checkStatus It will check the status of the current build process.(can also be used with an empty string to return the current status) cancelPending It will terminate the build process, if multiple flavors are in the queue it will remove those flavors from the queue. applyChange It will identify duplicates, and inconsistencies in the metadata and align them. Note: The default value of buildtype is checkStatus.

It provides all the dependent flavors' names and details for the specified flavor. Supported values : 0 / 1 When the value is 1, the mentioned fv’s dependent flavors will be built. If the value is 0 it will not include the dependent flavors.

The build process is not needed every time; it should only be used in specific scenarios. Below are the cases when you should use the build: Under prodBuild, whenever the developer needs to deploy apps to the QA server, a build is required. After entity creation, whenever we change the persists on of the entity,build is required. Whenever we maintain the Parent -child hierarchy, we need to build. Whenever we are creating vh-config, we need to build. Before doing import/export of apps, you need to build. Whenever you create new version of app, we need to build (this build is done automatically by the account console) For mobile apps, whenever you want to test app changes, you need to build. For both devBuild and prodBuild, if we are creating new env roles then we need to build. Note: When the fw_version of the application is changed, a new flavor_build must be created and re-registration will be required. The build process (both devBuild and prodBuild) should follow a parent → child order. You can trigger builds for both flavors at once. However, if the devBuild or prodBuild of a parent flavor has not been completed before building its child flavor, you will encounter an error like this:Error: Parent app(s) parent_app must be dev/prodbuilt before building child_app.

This is a screen that helps make changes in the settings and setting groups that are used in any application.

Note: If the developers want to make any changes to the Settings Definition Screen metadata then they will have to assign core_fw as a dependent app to the fw_settings1_1 app and then build the fw_settings1 flavor and reinitialize it. Only then any changes should be made. Also for save to work, assign is_external for fw_settings1 flavor as 1. To save any changes made on the Settings Definition user needs a shared, writable app.
Flavor: fw_settings1

Go to the menu App Settings. Click on the sub-menu named Settings Definition to open it. The Screen will be loaded initially with all the settings inside their respective Settings Group in a tree in ascending order based on their sequence value. Settings Group will also be in ascending order of their sequence values. Click on the Edit option in the upper right corner of the screen. On the toolbar of the screen, you will find the Create Group, Create Settings, Save, Delete and Cancel buttons. You can create the settings group by clicking the +Group button on the top right of the screen. It will ask the developer to provide the Settings Group ID in an input dialog. Click on the Create button in the input dialog. After creating a new Settings Group, users can see it updated in the Table Tree below. Users need to fill in the Sequence number, Title and Icon of that settings group and then click on the Save button to save the newly created settings group. All the settings groups will now be shown in ascending order of their sequence value. The developer then needs to create Settings inside the newly created settings group. To do that the user needs to select that settings group on the tree and then click on +Setting Button. It will ask for the Settings ID under Create Setting and the developer needs to provide the ID and click on the Create button. A new setting will be created inside the selected settings group. The developer needs to fill in the Title, Description, Sequence Number, Icon, Data Type, UI type, Vh ID, Default value, visible and modifiable_in and then click on Save to save all the changes. After successful save, all the settings in their respective groups will be in ascending order of their sequence value. Components Descriptions Title It's the name you want to put to identify the setting control. Description A short description of the setting element. Sequence Number This will put the setting elements according to the order of its sequence. Icon This implies an individual settings icon. Data Type It's the type of the setting, whether it's a number, an integer or a string etc. UI Type It is the type of Control that you want to render in the UI for those Settings such as Input, Slider, value Help, etc. Vh ID It is the value help ID created from bol editor on application flavor and it will be shown to the user as value help items in case the user has chosen UI type as VH. Default Value It's a pre-value that has been set for some particular setting. This is changeable according to your requirements. visible This implies who will be able to see the particular setting item. modifiable in This puts down conditions on who can see the setting items and so on. To update any details click on the edit button in the toolbar and after updating the details click on save to commit the changes. If you have updated any details and do not want it to commit then you can click on the reset button in the toolbar to set the details to the original state.

Our application is designed to operate with a specific Framework (FW) version. However, in certain situations, it may be necessary to downgrade the FW version to maintain compatibility, stability, or consistency across different environments. Below are the scenarios where a FW downgrade is required: **Latest FW Version Unavailable in QA and Production Environments ** Scenario: The latest FW version is deployed only in the development environment, but it has not been made available in the QA or production environments. **Reason for Downgrade: ** To ensure that the application team can move their developments to QA and production environments without facing compatibility issues. To align the development environment with the FW version currently in use in the QA and production environments. **Limited Testing of the Application with the Latest FW Version ** Scenario: The application has only been partially tested with the latest FW version, which introduces a risk that untested features or components may not perform as expected. **Reason for Downgrade: ** To provide more time for comprehensive testing and validation of the application on the latest FW version in a controlled environment before deploying it to QA or production. **Latest FW Version Exhibits Stability Concerns ** Scenario: The latest FW version has shown some performance issues or minor bugs that could affect application behavior. Reason for Downgrade: To ensure continued stability in the QA and production environments. To maintain a smooth user experience by avoiding potential disruptions in application performance.
documents.s: Framework Downgrade Scenarios in the Application
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/Applications FW Version Update/Framework Downgrade Scenarios in the Application

documents.t: If the application was initially developed using the downgraded FW version and the latest FW version becomes available in the QA and production environments, the following steps should be followed: **Upgrade the FW Version in the Development Environment: ** Update the development environment to match the latest FW version used in QA and production. **Validate Application Compatibility: ** Test the existing application, which was developed with the previous FW version, to ensure it is compatible with the latest FW version. **Make Necessary Updates: ** Update the application code or configurations as needed to support the latest FW version. **Conduct Thorough Testing: ** Perform end-to-end testing in the development environment to ensure the application functions correctly with the upgraded FW version. **Transport the Updated Application: ** After successful testing, move the updated application to the QA and production environments.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/Applications FW Version Update/Handling FW Upgrade After Downgrade

documents.t: Date of Issue: 29-OCT-2024 Target Audience: Application Development team Prepared by: Rincy Merin Robinson Platform Version: 7.0 A User Manual for application creation, knowledge and work reference.

Whenever there's a change in the major or minor versions of the FW platform, the apps that use the FW platform version need to be updated manually by the Application/Implementation team. For Example: We have an app named eam_6.0.1 that uses FW version 7_2_30. A major enhancement is required for this app due to the recent update to the FW version.Therefore, we will create a branch for this app and all the adoptions will be done in this branch, using the latest FW version 7_3_1. By reviewing the release notes for the FW update, the application team will learn about any adoptions or new features in the FW. Once the enhancement is complete, the branch app will be merged with the latest version into a single major app version, resulting in a final product, such as eam_6.0.3,FW version 7_3_1. Once all necessary fixes and updates are made to the app, it will be moved to the QA branch/environment for testing. If testing is successful, the updated app will be deployed to the production environment. Note: How to do the app branching and merging is mentioned in the UG. When the FW version is upgraded(major/minor) and is deployed,the applications that work on the FW version should be changed to the latest version.For that to achieve,create a branch and update the FW version as explained above. Once done with all the adoptions and changes, it is merged to the main branch and then the FW version is updated to transport it further to QA. Once the test is passed, the FW version will be updated in the application with the new FW version. As shown in the above diagram, if the test fails, then the app will not be taking the FW update and it will downgrade to the most recent functioning version of FW to ensure everything functions properly.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/Applications FW Version Update/Major Minor FW Version update

documents.t: Every Application / App version built on the Procify platform uses a FW/Platform version. The platform releases a new version every month with new features and bug fixes reported. It is recommended for users to stay updated with the latest version of the platform. This document serves as a guide for users on the understanding of Framework version updation(upgrade/downgrade) for applications. If an app running on the latest Framework version requires adjustments, users can use this guide to revert to an earlier version. This process involves either upgrading or downgrading the FW version. Note:Framework version can be changed only for ACTIVE Apps. App FW version cannot be changed by users when it's in QA/production.

During the patch upgrade in Framework platform, this upgrade will be automatically updated in all the applications which use the FW platform once they are released. So it's completely up to the FW team, when it comes to the patch update and there's nothing to do with the application team in the upgrading of FW version.

Important Note: All the key-value pairs listed below are case-sensitive. Any typo in the spelling will prevent the corresponding action block from being invoked. From the TestRecorder, only actions such as "click" and "sendKeys" can be automatically generated; users must manually adjust other actions to fit their requirements.
