documents.t: Essentially, this action is set up to perform a click on an element. It executes a WebDriver click command for the chosen element, typically scrolling to and then clicking the element when no additional options are specified.Please refer to the screenshot provided below for clarity. This action uses the “.press()” API of WDI5.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/Automation/Different Actions For Data file in Array Format

documents.t: Add a value to an input or textarea element found by the given selector.Send a sequence of keystrokes to an element after the input has been cleared before. Please refer to the screenshot provided below for clarity. This action uses the “.enterText()” API of WDI5. Note: For the "sendKeys" action, an additional key-value pair, "keyVal", must be included in the object. This "keyVal" will hold the text you wish to input into the selected control. You can also incorporate variables (e.g., $variable_name$) within the "keyVal" of "sendKeys". This allows for entering values stored in variables, enhancing flexibility. Please refer to the screenshot provided above for further clarification. An additional key-value pair can be included in the "sendKeys" action, namely "hitEnter": true. This will simulate pressing the Enter key from the keyboard after typing text into an input or textarea field. This feature is particularly useful in scenarios where, for instance, after filling out a search field, the Enter key needs to be pressed to initiate the search.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/Automation/Different Actions For Data file in Array Format

documents.t: Clear the value of an input or textarea element. Make sure you can interact with the element before using this command. You can't clear an input element that is disabled or in read only mode. Please refer to the screenshot provided below for clarity. This action uses the “.setValue()” API of WDIO.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/Automation/Different Actions For Data file in Array Format

documents.t: The "Function" action is utilized to execute any function that has been declared within its corresponding spec_name.spec.js file or the myUtil.js file. Note: For the "function" action, an additional key-value pair, "functionName", must be included in the object. This "functionName" will hold the name of a function declared or initialized in respective spec_name.spec.js. It's important to ensure that if a function is created in the myUtil.js file, it must be initialized in its relevant spec_name.spec.js file; otherwise, the function will not be invoked.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/Automation/Different Actions For Data file in Array Format

documents.t: The "replaceMap" action is utilized for incorporating additional variables that can be utilized across all files during runtime. This method proves beneficial for transmitting parameters within our functions, given that direct argument passing isn't feasible in array format. By employing this workaround, we simulate the behavior of passing arguments as done conventionally in regular functions. Note :- For the "replaceMap" action, an additional key-value pair, "data", must be included in the object. The "data" attribute is designed to store an array of objects, each representing a variable and its value that you wish to declare or store within the replaceMap. Upon repeated use of the same variables within replaceMap, it will overwrite the older values with the newly assigned ones. In the provided example, you'll notice the absence of "controlID" or "domElementId". This is because no actions were performed on any specific element; hence, the user needs to craft this function manually instead of generating it through a test recorder. Same will happen with many actions that are not performed on any elements.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/Automation/Different Actions For Data file in Array Format

documents.t: Save a screenshot of the current browsing context to a PNG file on your OS. Be aware that some browser drivers take screenshots of the whole document (e.g. Geckodriver with Firefox) and others only of the current viewport (e.g. Chromedriver with Chrome). This action uses the “browser.takeScreenshot()” API of WDIO.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/Automation/Different Actions For Data file in Array Format

documents.t: Get the text content from a DOM-element. Make sure the element you want to request the text from is interactable otherwise you will get an empty string as return value. If the element is disabled or not visible and you still want to receive the text content use getHTML as a workaround. This action uses the “.getText()” API of WDIO. For more reference click here. Note: For the "getText" action, an additional key-value pair, "storeAt", must be included in the object.The "storeAt" parameter will contain the name of the variable($variable_name$), where you intend to save the retrieved value from the chosen control element. getText action is only used in the places where there is only text field like sap.m.text,sap.m.label etc it will not work on input fields like klarion’s kloInput or sap.m.input.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/Automation/Different Actions For Data file in Array Format

documents.t: Get the value of a <textarea>, <select> or text <input> found by a given selector. If multiple elements are found via the given selector, an array of values is returned instead. For input with checkbox or radio type use isSelected. This action uses the “.getvalue()” API of WDIO. For more reference click here Note: For the "getValue" action, an additional key-value pair, "storeAtNew", must be included in the object.The "storeAtNew" parameter will contain the name of the variable($variable_name$), where you intend to save the retrieved value from the chosen control element. getValue action is only used in the places where there is only Input field like klarion’s kloInput or sap.m.input.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/Automation/Different Actions For Data file in Array Format

documents.t: The "ifPresent" action serves as a mechanism for verifying certain operations executed during automation. Specifically, it checks if a selected control element is indeed displayed on the screen. By utilizing its domElementId, it searches for the presence of the DOM element on the screen. Note: For the "ifPresent" action, an extra key-value pair named "type" needs to be added to the object. The "type" parameter specifies the kind of control that the action targets. This "type" should match the "controlType" found within the controlID.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/Automation/Different Actions For Data file in Array Format

documents.t: The "ifNotPresent" action functions as a counterpart to "ifPresent," serving to verify specific actions carried out during automation but in reverse. It specifically verifies whether a chosen control element is absent from the screen. Utilizing its domElementId, it searches to confirm the absence of the DOM element on the screen.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/Automation/Different Actions For Data file in Array Format

documents.t: Dispatch a series of keystrokes to the currently focused ("active") element. Activating an input element can be achieved simply by clicking on it. This approach is utilized in scenarios where the "sendKeys" action proves ineffective. Occasionally, when using "sendKeys" in an input field, the entered text may disappear immediately after being inserted, such as when specifying the control type in the UI editor while adding action. To address these issues or any other instances where "sendKeys" fails, the "Keys" action is employed. Note: For the "Keys" action, an additional key-value pair, "string", must be included in the object. This "string" will hold the text you wish to input into the selected control. You can also incorporate variables (e.g., $variable_name$) within the "string" of "Keys". This allows for entering values stored in variables, enhancing flexibility. Please refer to the screenshot provided above for further clarification. Element should be made active before using this action.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/Automation/Different Actions For Data file in Array Format

documents.t: The "keys" action is utilized to execute a range of keyboard actions within our automation processes. Note: When using the "keys" action, an extra key-value pair titled "value" must be incorporated into the object. This "value" will store the standardized key value for keyboard keys. For information on the standardized key values for specific keyboard actions, please refer to the provided link :-WebDriver Standardized Key Value .

documents.t: Within the closedmodules directory, establish a new folder titled klo_automation_1. Within this, create another folder dedicated to your automation, housing all requisite files needed to execute the automation. Note :- Adhering to this specific structure is crucial for the successful execution of the automation. The automation process attempts to access certain files, notably the klarion.json file located within the kloconfig folder, from your private node. Therefore, maintaining this structure ensures that the automation can correctly locate and utilize these files from their designated locations. Should you deviate from this structure, you will need to adjust the paths in conf.data.js accordingly to reflect the correct locations of your files. The files mentioned above are essential for running the automation. Let's examine each of these files individually.

Located within the kloAu directory, this file stands as the core component of the automation suite. It houses all necessary functions tasked with transforming array-formatted code into a conventional format. Since WDIO cannot interpret array formats directly, this conversion is imperative for compatibility.

This file will house all fundamental configurations necessary for the automation to operate, including user credentials, URLs, and the specific Chrome directory in which the execution should occur. baseUrl: Users must specify the URL to be accessed at the beginning of the automation process. userId: The User ID associated with the login or registration conducted on the previously mentioned URL. Password: The user's password, if applicable. desktopLoginID: For the desktop login ID, users need to supply the User ID used for logging in on their desktop. Profile_directory: Users must indicate the Chrome profile directory where they intend to run the automation. Specs: Within the Specs object, users must list the names of the specs they wish to execute, adhering to a sequential order. It's important to note that the names provided are case-sensitive. Ensure consistency in naming across all references to avoid discrepancies. NOTE :- The Spec and Data file names should be entered exactly as demonstrated in the preceding example. Additionally, the object name must remain consistent. Please remember that the names provided are case-sensitive. ReplaceMap :-This file includes all the application variables required for test cases. Variables must be declared within double dollar signs, like $variable_name$ How replaceMap Operates in Automation:​ In the array format data file, replaceMap searches for all variables declared either in conf.data.js or at runtime within the data file itself. Whenever it encounters a match, it substitutes the matched variable with the corresponding value from the object's key-value pair. Note: By default, two variables, $dateKey$ and $landscape$, are automatically created within replaceMap at runtime. These variables can also be utilized within your data file. $dateKey$: This variable holds the current date and time. It's particularly useful for generating unique names for entities and screens each time the automation runs. For instance, in the example provided, the $entityName$ variable is set to "d_autest_$dateKey$". During execution, %dateKey% is replaced with the current date and time, resulting in a unique identifier like d_autest_25_06_12_11. $landscape$: Contains the name of the landscape for which the private node was created. This value is derived from the klarion.json file, indicating the landscape's name.

This file encompasses all the scripts generated by the test recorder. Essentially, it stores the test script or code in array format that was produced. Observing the header section of the tsData variable, we find an object containing several key-value pairs. Let's explore these details further. Remark: This field allows you to summarize what the entire specs entails or outlines the actions performed by the specs. A point to remember is that this summary will also appear as the specs name in the HTML report. Reload and Login: These should always be set to true to ensure that the login process occurs every time the automation starts. Menu: Used to specify the navigation path to the desired menu. The structure follows the pattern of the menu group name, preceded by a forward slash, and then the menu name. For instance, to open the Procify Data Studio inside App Builder, the menu entry would be “App Builder/Procify Data Studio”. It's important to note that both the menu group and menu name are case-sensitive. Note: Test Spec/Data files generated from the Test Recorder will not include the menu key-value pair in the header object. Developers must manually add this information.

This file encompasses all the function declarations originally listed or created in the myUtil.js file. Additionally, it provides a designated space for declaring any function that is intended to be utilized exclusively within its corresponding data file. NOTE :- In the spec_name.spec.js file, towards the end, there's a highlighted segment shown in the accompanying image. Within the loadData function located at the bottom of this file, you must include your spec's name as a parameter. This name should precisely match the one listed under the specs section in the conf.data.js file. To ensure consistency across your files and facilitate the automation process, it's crucial to maintain identical naming conventions. Any discrepancy in naming, including variations in capitalization, will prevent the automation from initiating.

This file will contain all the functions that you want to use throughout your entire automation. We can create function in two formats here :- Normal Function​ Standard functions will adhere to the conventional coding practices of WDIO. We cannot incorporate any code snippets formatted as arrays in this context.These functions prove beneficial when dealing with non-UI5 pages, such as the registration or login pages of our servers. These functions are utilized in scenarios where there is no requirement for using replaceMap or variable replacement from a replaceMap.json file, as the standard functions do not support the replacement of variables denoted by $variable_name$ for ui5 pages. As demonstrated in the following example, neither replaceMap variables nor code formatted as arrays are employed, eliminating the need for runtime replacements. To grasp how we can manage non-UI5 pages or write code in a standard format, let's delve into the following: The $ command serves as a concise method to retrieve a single element from a webpage. addValue: This function allows adding a value to an input or textarea element identified by a specific selector. click: Executes a WebDriver click action on the chosen element. By default, this action involves scrolling to and clicking the targeted element unless otherwise specified. In the subsequent example, we demonstrate the process of selecting a password field element and verifying its presence on the screen using the isDisplayed() API. If the element is visible, we proceed to insert the user's password using addValue and subsequently click the login button. Array Format Function​ Array format functions in the context of writing code snippets in spec_name.data.js allow for the creation of reusable functions that can be called multiple times within the file. These functions are particularly useful for performing repetitive actions, especially when those actions need to be executed in a recursive manner. In such cases, defining a function within myUtil enables you to easily invoke it as many times as needed without duplicating code. Using new test recorder that generates actions in an array format, you would parse these actions and pass them to your function.By structuring your code in this way, you can efficiently manage complex sequences of actions, especially when dealing with arrays of elements or actions generated from automated tools like a test recorder. This approach promotes code reuse and simplifies the management of repetitive tasks within your tests. Understanding functions, we recognize that they can be invoked repeatedly, each time with varying parameters. Following this principle, we too employ a similar strategy. To explore how we pass parameters, we'll initially focus on utilizing these parameters within our array format code. Specifically, we leverage the replaceMap.json file, which stores the values of parameters passed to functions at runtime. Essentially, we're retrieving these parameter values stored in replaceMap.json through a function designed for our array format code. Our methodology involves declaring a variable and importing a utility function named getWordFromReplaceMap from the kloAuWdio file into our myUtil file. This function accepts a variable name (such as $entity$, which is declared in spec_name.data.js) as its parameter and returns the corresponding value from replaceMap.json at runtime.

For Node.js projects, the package.json file provides a simplified way to manage a project's metadata and dependencies. The file ensures a project always has current information about the libraries and tools it needs to work correctly.Every npm package and Node.js project has a package.json file with metadata for a project. The file resides in the root directory of every Node.js package .The package.json file contains descriptive and functional metadata about a project, such as a name, version, and dependencies. The file provides the npm package manager with various information to help identify the project and handle dependencies. To install the dependencies, transfer your most recent package.json file to your automation directory. Afterward, navigate to this directory using the command prompt and execute npm install.
The configuration file contains all necessary information to run your test suite. It’s a NodeJS module that exports a JSON. No changes should be made in that file by the developer.

WebdriverIO-plugin for wdi5. It provides the ui5-service to WebdriverIO, running tests in the browser.In case the very first called page is non-UI5 (think SAP CP CloudFoundry login), the config option skipInjectUI5OnStart can be set to true to postpone injecting wdi5 into the browser context. Consequently you have to do it later, as soon as the UI5 page to test is available. This can be done by calling injectUI5() on the wdio-ui5-service. So, the UI5 service will prove beneficial when encountering a stale element reference error during automation, preventing the automation from halting or performing unexpectedly. The stale element reference error is a WebDriver error that occurs because the referenced web element is no longer attached to the DOM.Every DOM element is represented in WebDriver by a unique identifying reference, known as a web element. The web element reference is a UUID used to execute commands targeting specific elements, such as getting an element's tag name and retrieving a property off an element. When an element is no longer attached to the DOM, i.e. it has been removed from the document or the document has changed, it is said to be stale. Staleness occurs for example when you have a web element reference and Upon navigation, all web element references to the previous document will be discarded along with the document. This will cause any subsequent interaction with the web element to fail with the stale element reference error. To overcome this ui5 service needs to be injected again in the page again. Refer to the screenshot above for more details.

Additionally, it's crucial to note that if the $dateKey$ variable is required in the first spec_name.spec.js file, it must be imported from conf.data.js. However, if it needs to be used starting from the second spec onwards, it should be imported from replaceMap.json.

documents.t: When using variable names in getText() and getValue() actions, they should not be reused. Although it operates similarly to replaceMap, where initializing the same variable with a different value results in replacement, this principle does not apply when storing values from the screen using getText() and getValue() actions. In these cases, repeating variable names is not allowed.

documents.t: Occasionally, due to failed automation execution or termination mid-execution, the replaceMap.json file may become empty. Consequently, attempting to run automation afterward will fail to start. To mitigate this problem, an empty object must be explicitly declared within the replaceMap.json file.

If users are conducting validations on a UI-created screen following a full preview, certain codes need to be made dynamic. Otherwise, the automation will not execute correctly if triggered again or under different conditions. As illustrated in the preceding image, there are several areas (e.g., 2-3 spots) where the code requires modification to ensure successful execution each time the automation runs. For instance, consider the scenario where the automation's flavor changes; without making the code dynamic, the automation would fail. Additionally, the page name appears in both the view ID and model ID sections of the code. If a new page is introduced with a different name, the automation will also fail unless the code is updated accordingly to reflect this change dynamically.

documents.t: Sometimes, as noticed, once the menu is opened during automation, the process halts in the browser and begins displaying errors in the console. The primary issue here is that the replaceMap, which is intended to substitute variables for viewID and modelID at runtime, fails to do so; instead, it retains the original values provided in the spec_name.data.js file. To update the page's viewID and modelID with the current ones, since these identifiers change with every screen navigation, the automation executes the getModelViewNamesForAutomation() function in the console. This function retrieves the current page's viewID and modelID, which are then stored in replaceMap. If a match is found, the existing viewID and modelID in the code, formatted as an array, are replaced with the current ones. After the menu is opened in automation, the code proceeds to the next segment. Occasionally, the screen remains partially open, still showing the loading state. At this point, even though the code execution has moved forward, the screen is not fully loaded. Consequently, when the automation runs the getModelViewNamesForAutomation() function in the console, it returns the modelID and viewID of the previously viewed page, not the current one, because the page is still in the process of rendering and is not yet fully visible. Because of this, replaceMap does not work in this case. To address this issue, after the menu is opened, we need to insert a code block that does not involve viewID or modelID. The only element on the screen that lacks either viewID or modelID in its code block is the Procify logo at the top.
documents.s: replaceMap does not work after menu opening sometimes

documents.t: There may be instances where a list of elements exists, and a specific item needs to be selected from it. For example, choosing the screen type of a section from a VH list. As depicted in the image below, we generate code for selecting the search screen type from the VH list. However, within the code block, no mention of 'search' is made; instead, it merely indicates the specific path or index where the search type screen resides. If the path or index of the search were to change, the automation would encounter issues at this stage. To address this issue , we've linked it with "search" such that it consistently selects the “search” screen type from the VH list, regardless of the index. Let’s see how we will do that. Upon generating the code in procify control list section , navigate to the properties tab of test recorder. There we will be able to see different properties from which we will be able to bind this element. Therefore, among the highlighted attributes, we choose the ones that can uniquely identify this element. Specifically, for this element, both the title and description can serve as distinguishing features. Lets see how we can do the binding in the code block :- In this scenario, the path within the binding path must be commented, and a new key-value pair should be introduced, specifically 'properties'. Within the value of 'properties', there should be another key-value pair, which includes the attributes derived from the properties section of the test recorder, which we are utilizing for binding. Here we are using title as attribute for search property and providing its value as “search” .

Automation testing is a software testing technique that uses automated tools to execute tests, compare actual and expected results, and generate reports. Automation testing aims to increase the speed and efficiency of the testing process while improving result accuracy and reliability.

To initiate automation, whether on a private or public node server, you must replace the existing openUI5_1_120_27 within the closedmodules directory with the new openUI5_1_120_27. Additionally, ensure the sap-ui-version.json file is copied into closedmodules. Following these steps, if operating on a private node, restart the server and proceed with re-registration.

WDIO is a hugely popular E2E testing framework for Web Applications. This also includes hybrid apps. It can drive a real browser and simulate a user interacting with the app. WDIO can work with apps that use any web framework but there are certain advantages if the testing framework integrates with the web framework. If this is the case, the tests could be much simpler to write and mainly, much more reliable. Reliability is of paramount importance for E2E tests that typically struggle with flakiness so any improvement can have significant effect on the TCO of testing process WDIO can work with any web application but lacks the awareness of the web framework that the application uses. WDI5, which is a WDIO plugin, bridges this gap and provides two key benefits, namely control locators and synchronization with the web framework. WDIO supports many types of locators - css, xpath, even plain javascript code but it lacks understanding of the UI5 controls. WDI5 exposes a browser.byControl() method that accepts a control locator and returns a proxy for the real control. Then the test can assert on the control state or even interact with the control. The second benefit is transparent but equally important – on every element interaction, WDI5 waits for UI5 rendering to complete and for the application to be completely stable.
documents.s: Use WDIO and WDI5 for testing UI5 apps

documents.t: Set of frequently used values, which remains constant, are provided as variables. These are framework provided and are extensible in shared flavor. But can not alter the framework provided fields. $USER login_id, employee_id, (userID) Owning_bp ExtendedBP + application extended fields. USER data is synced as a part of initial sync. All updates on user data are communicated to relevant endpoints of the user by FW vai kloBrokermessage using a user entity. Client side user entity should update the global $user variable. $BP has me, bp_type, Has_own_tenant + application extended fields $ROLE $role is a configuration data that needs to be modified only on dev and deployed on QA,PROD. It does not depend on flavor/version. And available for extension in Shared flavor. Application maintained data in the extended fields. Useful for controlling the UI Controls visibility/ editability per role within the flavor. My Role date is synced as a part of initial sync. All updates on the role date are communicated to relevant users by FW vai kloBroker message. On assignment of a new app to a user this is also pushed to the user. $SYSTEM (readOnly) - non extendable by application. flavor --transient field and calculated in runtime and set version --transient field and calculated in runtime and set role - not Available as kloBroker userID - not Available as kloBroker isMiddleWare isScheduler today --transient field and calculated in runtime and set (date ) now --transient field and calculated in runtime and set (timestamp value) $GLOBAL Application defined fields act as global variables. Gives the substitute feature. Usage All the above global variables are accessible on the event object, $Global is only available in client. When used as a string literal in a meta model in query, id series, authorization it is replaced with real value. E.g. $USER.login_id will be replaced with the currently logged in user id. Syntax: ${<Variable name>.<property id>} API EnvironmentalVariable.getEnvironmentMap(flavor,version) will return the env variable map, which will have all the ENV objects as key- value pairs, and use the ENV variable name to get the actual Variable Entity. BaseController has API to access ENV Variables in Controllers, Please refer KloTouch API Example: event[‘$USER’].login_id; will return you the current logged in user id; event.getEnv(“” getDefaultEntityQuery: returns instance of Entity Query with specified name getDefaultBOQuery:

An attachment is any file or document that you upload against any object. Attachment component is used for uploading and downloading the mime (images, videos, audio, pdf etc). This is an entity level flag and it indicates that attachment is allowed to store against the entity. If enabled, the attachment link entity becomes part of the BO. Users can only add/edit/delete attachments when the component is in edit mode. Framework adds primary relation with attachment link entity and the Entity where attachment is enabled. The name of the relation is ‘attachments’. Within one BO, Attachment Entity can have relations with multiple Entities like order_hdr and order_items both are attachment enabled. Uploads a file in a common folder(local) and also maintains a link with the object. Mime gets pushed to the server repository via middleware. If the parent object is deleted, it deletes the attachment also but not the mime. Mime might have a reference with another attachment. Attachment with new entity: as attachment is part of the same BO, commit and rollback works like other entities in a BO. Mime upload to the local folder is separate and it does not rollback if the transaction is cancelled or failed. To upload or display the attachment UI controls are part of kloTouch. Steps to enable the attachment for an entity: Import kloAttachment in Account flavor/s. Attachment config. Enable attachment in the entity definition. Define attachment type. Define attachment subtype. Call the APIs to upload and download the attachment. Attachment config: Account Landscape Attatchment_upload_class: Fully qualified name of the attachment class which implements AttachmentHandler interface which has two methods upload and download. This class is to be written by an application developer. These methods are available in controller or Rule. Sample code is provided below. Content repository: Location(base path) to store the mime on the server side is part of this upload class. thirdParty_application: Client application. min_battery: minimum battery required for upload and download. If the battery level goes down and the user tries to upload/download, it ends with an error/warraning. Sample code for upload class: public interface AttachmentHandler { public void upload(HttpServletRequest request, HttpServletResponse response,String landscape) throws IOException, JSONException, JCodecException ; public Response download(String file ,HttpServletRequest request,HttpServletResponse response,String landscape); } public class CustomAttachmentHandler implements AttachmentHandler { public void upload(HttpServletRequest request, HttpServletResponse response,String landscape) throws IOException, JSONException, JCodecException{ //TODO } public Response download(String file ,HttpServletRequest request, HttpServletResponse response1,String landscape) { //TODO } } Define Attachment Type: once “Has Attachment is marked TRUE, the attachment section in Data Studio will be enabled where you can define the attachment type. Below are the attributes: Attachment type: this is to categorise the attachment. Like Product, Equipment, Invoice, Profile pic, etc. Doctype: indicates that document type of attachment like user manual etc Max Files: max number of files allowed to upload. Download Type/Sync Type: WIFI, Battery Level, Always. Mime type: This specifies the accepted mime types of the mime. One mime type is mandatory. Multiple mime types are allowed with comma(,) as separator. Allowed mime types are .jpeg, .png, .mp3, .3gp, .wav, .mp4, .pdf, .xls, .xlsx, .doc, .docx, .zip, .RAR Application has to decide the mime types. There is no exclusion from the framework side. Size per file: Define the max allowed size (in KB) of a file to upload. If file size exceeds, it ends with an error. Size is defined per attachment type. Source: There are different sources from where media files are allowed to capture. Multiple sources are allowed with comma(,) as separator. If only one source is selected, it directly opens Camera or Gallery or Mice otherwise this gives the option to users to select a source for upload. Camera Take Photo Record Video Gallery/Folder Mice Need Location: Capture GPS location while adding the attachment. Upload endpoint/location: location where attachment has to be dumped on the server. ( folder path, mount etc.) Entity Name: name of the transaction entity for which attachment to be allowed. Attachment should be enabled in Entity definition. Define Attachment Subtype : subtype is just a categorization to store the Sub Type: it is a sub categorization(child) of attachment type and it is optional. For example, uploading images of type equipment with subtype as front side, back side, etc. Entityname: Attachment link: This stores the entity attachment info. This link table has a primary relation with the transaction entity that means it is part of every BO attachment that is enabled. Table name is ‘dcatt_attachment_link’. Attachment ID: GUID generated for attachment. This gets generated at the client side. Attachment ID is a unique id across all the endpoints. Attachment Type: passed from UI as parameter. SubType: passed from UI as parameter. File name: Input from application and this is displayed on the UI. Entity Key: This is a unique key with a combination of entity name and primary key set. Mime Type: mime type(file extension) of the attached mime. Only one value is allowed. GPS Location : If enabled in setting, it captures the GPS coordinates. Is default: This is input from UI at the time of upload. Default marked attachment is considered for preview or thumbnail in UI. Sequence: Sequence in which attachment is displayed in UI. Attachment APIs: Upload: call onAttachmentFileSelect(oEvent,parameters,fnOnUpload, fnOnError) function. Command Description Example onAttachmentFileSelect(oEvent,parameters,fnOnUpload, fnOnError) This uploads the mime and makes an entry in the link table. As the link table is part of the transaction BO it gets updated with the BO. some_function_in_controller : function(oEvent){var parameters = {"type":"type1","subtype":"subtype1","modelName":"entity_name","path":"/list/0/attachments","objectType":1,"entityname":"entity_name",};oController.onAttachmentFileSelect(oEvent,parameters,fnOnUpload, fnOnError);} Download: Command Description Example forceDownloadAttachmnet(attachmentId) This is to force download the mime from the server. oController.forceDownloadAttachmnet(attachmentId); Update: update attachment info like file name, is_default, etc. Delete: Use the Entity delete API. This deletes only the attachment link and does not delete the mime. Common folder : Common folder is used to store the mimes locally. This is hardcoded in the framework. While uploading the file it first copies the file to a local folder which might be different for mobile and desktop. Attachment id gets generated after the source of the image is copied to the common folder. Message processing: note that attachment entity and the mime are separate messages. Attachment entity message flow is similar to other entities and part of the parent entity’s BO. Upload: Mime messages get stored in _attachments table at client side and processed separately. From the device it is a direct Ajax call to the server for all the messages in _attachments table. Once it is synced to the server it makes an entry in the d_attachment_log table. Download: First check if mime is available in local storage. If not, a request is made from the device and mime gets downloaded to the local storage. This request is through middleware. Object cloning: attachment link is also cloned with the BO. This points to the same mime. Convert Object Type: attachment and mime does not get copied to the target object even though it is part of BO. Initial sync: write initial sync queries for attachment link. Download all: for all attachments, it loads the mime immediately after initial sync is completed. Download on demand: mime is loaded only on user request from UI. Send attachment with email: separate notification API. This is part of the Notification component. Archive Settings - Download/Upload only if: Download/ upload only on wifi Download/ upload only on wifi and power always download

kloConfig is application data defined during application development and embedded together with code. kloConfig data is maintained using kloTuner. kloConfig behaves like a read only entity, columns/property/fields called config property is defined by the application developer. Developers can specify multiple rows/ value set/ entityset for the particular configuration. Klobase selects and returns the qualified row at runtime. kloConfig is used to customise the application flow by using the variable value in code for decision making , or in UI for enabling disable/ controlling visibility of UI controls. All kloconfig except $Role are customizable per flavor, although best practice does not advise to change values across flavor. Broadly config needs below three parts to be completed to work: kloConfig Definition: modelling kloconfig by defining config properties with its type and Value Help if required. It follows a similar approach as entity definition. Providing default value is must for each config entity property, Default value is used for returning the value until real object values are loaded, hence default value must be most restrictive. Maintaining ValueRow per unique key. It should be done using kloTuner. Each row should be self-sufficient, it does not borrow values from other rows. Using the value: filtered row is returned by API, these APIs are async. To ensure value is loaded use fetch() to resolve. Until fetch resolves, the config object returns the default config property value. Configuration controls or changes the behaviour of the application. Below are the different type of configuration supported: Entity Config $Role Config Entity Status Config App Global Config

Possible set of configuration for an entity by which the application process flow or behaviour is controlled. Works when an entity is marked with ‘Has Config’ TRUE and configuration entity properties are maintained. Entity Naming convention: Framework creates a Configuration Entity. It is calculated from the entityname by replacing the first character to ‘c’. For example the main Entity is ‘d_order’ then configuration Entity gets created with the name of ‘c_order’. Entity names should use only english lower case alphabets (a-z), digits (0-9) and underscore (_) and upto 31 chars max length. Configuration is Object Type and Flavor based. In case of no object type applicable to an Entity, default Object Type is -1. Configuration can be defined on any entity in a BO but it is recommended to define at root entity level. In case a child entity does not have an object type but the root entity has the object type, it does not consider the root entity object type. Metadata definition(Entity properties) for configuration entities is to be filled using Data Studio. Each config has to be defined as Entity Property in Config Entity. Possible values for a Config have to be maintained through kloTuner. Configuration is accessible throughout the application including Rules and middleware. <entity instance>.configP will return you with a single row of the configuration maintained for this entity with respect to the current object this holds. If no object type is found / has an object type that is false, the framework will try to find a default configuration with -1 as the default object type. If no configuration is found, return an empty object. Define the configuration structure in Entity owning flavor only. Not customizable in other flavors. Configuration values are customizable across flavors. Steps for configuration: Mark ‘Has Config’ for the entity (d_order) in Data Studio. Framework creates a Configuration Entity. Add the properties in Data Studio with new Entity for all configurations. Run Update schema to create/update a database table. One Entity has only one Config table and one value per Object Type in a flavor. Define the possible values allowed for a configuration property in kloTunner. Each possible value has some meaning and definition or implication of that value also to be explained in detail. This helps consultants to change/maintain the configuration. Write business logic based on possible values of each configuration. Application behaviour can be controlled on client side or APIs/Backend based on the configured value. For Example, Sales Order has few configurations like: Credit Limit Check Free Goods Order Approval Order Close ATP Check Expected Delivery Days Part Delivery Allowed Configuration Entity name: c_order Field Name Data Type Possible values s_object_type int(11) (pk) All object types s_role varchar(32) (pk) credit_limit_check boolean TRUE/FALSE free_goods boolean TRUE/FALSE order_approval boolean TRUE/FALSE order_close boolean TRUE/FALSE atp_check boolean TRUE/FALSE expected_del_days int(11) Only Numeric values >=0 part_del_allowed boolean TRUE/FALSE APIs: <entityinstance>.config Returns config values of an object.This returns only one record for a given object type. Example: orderinstance.config or**this.config

If application behaviour differs on user role based, use role based configuration. Define Role configuration in Account “shared” flavor only. Not allowed to customise in other flavors. Config values can not be customised across flavor. Role and Designation of a user are two separate things. Example: One user can have only one designation. One user can have multiple roles assigned combined with ROT (Role+ROT is unique). Use for UI binding and business logic in controllers. Not available to use in server side Rules, MW because the role is not known in case of MW message processing, upload, etc. oController.getEnveronmentMap($role) will return you with a single row of the configuration maintained for logged in user’s role. Entity Naming convention: Entity name is ‘env_role’. Steps: Add the properties in Data Studio with new Entity for all configurations. Framework will take care of loading the config values. No need to write additional queries. Run Update schema to create/update a database table. Define the possible values allowed for a configuration property in Data Studio. Each possible value has some meaning and definition or implication of that value also to be explained in detail. This helps consultants to change/maintain the configuration. kloTunner facilitates the maintenance of the configuration. Maintain the config values for each configuration using kloTunner. Write business logic based on possible values of each configuration. Examples: Manual header discount in order. Manual Item discount in order. Configuration Entity Name: env_role Field Name Data Type Possible values role varchar(32) (pk) All roles manual_hdr_dis_so boolean TRUE/FALSE manual_item_dis_so boolean TRUE/FALSE APIs: Command Description Example oController.getEnveronmentMap($role) Returns config values of the user logged in. This returns only one record for a given role. oController.getEnveronmentMap($role)

In case application behaviour differs based on custom status and object type, use status config. Define the configurations in account owning flavor. Not recommended to customise in other flavors even though it is supported. Config values are bindable to UI elements and can be used in UI and backend both sides. For a selected object only one row(set of configuration) is qualified. If no configuration is defined it will return an empty object. If the status value is not known and trying to get the status config, it will return an empty object. <entityobject>.statusconfig will return you with a single row of the configuration maintained for the selected record. Entity Naming convention: It is calculated from the entityname by replacing the first character to ‘u’. For example the main Entity is ‘u_order’ then configuration Entity gets created with the name of ‘u_order’. Entity names should use only english lower case alphabets (a-z), digits (0-9) and underscore (_) and upto 31 chars max length. Steps: If an entity is marked ‘Has Status’ TRUE, Framework creates an status config entity where object type and status fields are part of the primary key. Entity type is ‘Configuration Entity’. Framework will take care of loading the config values. No need to write additional queries. Add the properties in Data Studio with new Entity for all configurations. Run Update schema to create a database table. Define the possible values allowed for a configuration property in Data Studio. Each possible value has some meaning and definition or implication of that value also to be explained in detail. This helps consultants to change/maintain the configuration. kloTunner facilitates the maintenance of the configuration. Maintain the config values for each configuration using kloTunner. Write business logic based on possible values of each configuration. Configuration Entity Name: u_status_config Field Name Data Type Possible values s_object_type int(11) (pk) All object types s_status_custom varchar(32) (pk) Status of selected object type s_role varchar(32) (pk) flavor_version varchar(32) (pk) manual_hdr_dis_so boolean TRUE/FALSE manual_item_dis_so boolean TRUE/FALSE

App config is a complete custom config decided by the application team. Use Global config in case of common or across BO scenarios or the scenarios where Entity, $Role and Status config do not fulfil the requirement. Define global configuration entities in any flavor. Customisation is allowed only in entity owning flavor. Depending on business requirements, multiple config entities can be created. Entity Naming convention: Entity name starts with ‘cg_’. Entity names should use only english lower case alphabets (a-z), digits (0-9) and underscore (_) and upto 31 chars max length. Steps: Create a configuration entity. This entity should be a type of ‘Configuration Entity’. This is a completely customised entity. Framework will take care of loading the config values on demand and filter the config at application side. No need to write additional queries. Add the properties in Data Studio with new Entity for all configurations. Run Update schema to create a database table. Define the possible values allowed for a configuration property in Data Studio. Each possible value has some meaning and definition or implication of that value also to be explained in detail. This helps consultants to change the configuration. kloTunner facilitates the maintenance of the configuration. Maintain the config values for each configuration using kloTunner. Write business logic based on possible values of each configuration. Example: Need a configuration to sync the objects to SAP with the restriction of BP ID and object type. Configuration Entity Name: cg_sync_to_sap Field Name Data Type Possible values flavor_version char(32) (PK) s_object_type int(11) (pk) All object types bp_id char(32) (PK) BP ID or ALL enable_sync boolean TRUE/FALSE

A domain is a unique set of values permitted for an attribute in a table. KloBase Datastore supports a variety of data types for property values. A domain represents data type. The following domain types are supported : CDomainType JS Type DB type MsgType Remark I8 number Number(3,0) number number I16 number Number(5,0) number number I32 number Number(10,0) number number I64 number Number(13,0) number number DEC number Number(p,s) number number B boolean Number(1,0) number (0/1) Returns true/false CHR string VarChar(n) string string ANUM string VarChar(n) string Not supported cwns string VarChar(n) string Not supported BLOB string VarChar(n) string string D Date Number(13,0) number (milliseconds) number (milliseconds) T milliseconds Number(13,0) number (milliseconds) number (milliseconds) DT / TSTAMP Date Number(13,0) number (milliseconds) UTC enabled CLOB Not supported GUID Not supported JSON Not supported DURATION Not supported Here, Domain is defined as an enum in CDomainType. Applications must use the JS Type for all coding purposes. Note: DT / TS is UTC-based date time, hence, must not be compared with local time as hard-coded time.

A network mode is a state, or means of operating, that a wireless network can employ. In other words, they describe the various operational characteristics of the wireless signals. kloBase supports a rich set of network modes. The two most frequent network modes are online and offline. Online: Online network mode refers to the capability of running the program in a browser or installed mobile app (client) to communicate with the server for day-to-day needs. Network connectivity from client to server is a must. For example, if the screen needs to show Open Orders, kloBO will go to the server to get the data for Open Order and give it to the UI for display. All the changes on the browser or device app will be collected and sent to the server for validating and saving. Offline: Offline network mode refers to the capability to run the program with weak or infrequent network availability. The application stores the relevant data locally and keeps the local cache and server data updated as and when it finds connectivity. Browsers and installed mobile apps (client) both are capable of offline operations. Cached Online: It refers to the client’s capability to connect with the server whenever required. Speeds up the interaction of the client with the server by suggesting data from the local cache. Offline Confirmed: It refers to the capability of the client to serve data offline. The save (message) always goes through online. It modifies the local cache. There is no message flow from offline to server during modification. SAP Online: This refers to the capability of all the transactions that go to SAP via the gateway server. SAP Cached Online: Refers to the configuration of the web browser or mobile application in such a way that the contents (static and dynamic) are stored in the cache, and the next request to the page concerned can be satisfied quickly from the cache. enum NetworkModes { OFFLINE = "OFFLINE", ONLINE = "ONLINE", PREFERRED_ONLINE = "PREFERRED_ONLINE", PREFERRED_OFFLINE = "PREFERRED", SAP_ONLINE = "SAP_ONLINE", SAP_PREFERRED_ONLINE = "SAP_PREFERRED_ONLINE" }

The medium through which the end users log into the application is known as the client. Web browsers are used to open an online application, here the browser is the client. Similarly, when an Android application is installed on mobile to run an application, the Android app becomes the client. Each client is identified by a unique identifier called the endpoint ID.

Tenant is an environment or space created for the users' data storage. Physical data on a server needs to be partitioned across multiple sets of users. Generally, in any multinational organisation, each department owns a tenant. Each tenant is assigned a unique endpoint ID. Individual tenants can host data for multiple organisations.

Endpoint helps klobroker in sending and receiving messages across various participants. Each endpoint is identified by a unique endpoint ID. Every user logging into an application sends a signal to the server through the installed app. Hence, each installation gets a unique endpoint ID. Each browser gets an endpoint ID. Every individual tenant and the external system linked to the server have an endpoint ID.
When one endpoint (source) sends the instruction (message) to another endpoint. The receiving endpoint (target) gets the message through the channel.

The app is an object-oriented programming system*.* Flavor encourages program modularity, eases the development of large, complex programs, and provides high run-time efficiency. Flavors are integrated into Lisp and Symbolic program development environments. Applications can use resources available in the current flavor plus the version only. API for: Shared flavor + version. Core flavor + version. Current flavor + version.
The Business Object Editor is the blueprint of the interface in KloBO administrator that allows you to manage (create, edit, and delete) the various aspects of a Business Object.

The loadAll feature retrieves all available rows from the database, including all configured properties for each record, in a single query execution. To enable this feature, set the loadAll flag on the queryInstance object before executing the query: queryInstance.setLoadAll(true); To revert to the default behavior, disable the feature and then execute the query: queryInstance.setLoadAll(false); Note: Enabling loadAll may increase memory consumption and query execution time when working with large datasets, as all records and properties are fetched at once.

documents.s: API: Application Programming Interface. A software intermediary that allows two applications to interact with each other. Each time we use an app like Facebook, send an instant message, or check the weather on our smart device, we are using an API

documents.t: C
documents.s: Business Rules: Business Rules provide a true abstraction level and separation from the user interface. The business rule is not actively selecting user interface elements to collect input values, which allows flexible modification of the presentation and the rule itself. The same business rule can service any number of data controller views regardless of the view types

documents.s: Deprecated: This is the process of taking older code and marking it as no longer being useful within the codebase, usually because it has been replaced by newer code. The deprecated code is not immediately removed from the codebase because doing so may cause regression errors

documents.s: Lisp: Lisp is the second-oldest high-level programming language after Fortran and has changed a great deal since its early days, and a number of dialects have existed over its history. Today, the most widely known general-purpose Lisp dialects are Common Lisp and Scheme

documents.s: Meta Model: A metamodel or surrogate model is a model of a model, and metamodeling is the process of generating such metamodels. Thus metamodeling or meta-modelling is the analysis, construction and development of the frames, rules, constraints, models and theories applicable and useful for modelling a predefined class of problems

documents.s: Query tree: It is an internal representation of an SQL statement where the single parts that it is built from are stored separately. These query trees can be shown in the server log if you set the configuration parameters debug_print_parse, debug_print_rewritten, or debug_print_plan

documents.s: Stateless Model: In simple terms, a client program makes a request to an application server, which sends data back to the client. The server treats all client connections equally and saves no information from prior requests or sessions. A website that serves up a simple static web page is a good example of the stateless model

documents.t: BOL Reference Guide Date of Issue: January 2023 Target Audience: Application Developer, Consultants. A Reference Guide for application creation, knowledge and work reference.

Parent Key Mapping: This is to auto populate the parent keys while creating an entity. Pass entity or JSON format on new entity creation. Keys are auto populated before save and accessible in UI controllers and callbacks. Key gets populated upto N level in a BO. In case if the object type is not passed, it will return with error. ID series gets generated on entity creation if applicable and populates the IDs to UI/Model. In case any child entity exists and ID is part of the primary key, it populates with the child entity also. Mapping for already existing objects. Like two BPs are already created and map these as BP relations. Primary relation: If primary relation is maintained for two entities, keys get auto-populated from the parent. To understand this, take an example of order creation. While adding a line item in order, the order ID gets filled from the header automatically. Aggregation: This is to populate the key in the entity which is not part of the same BO. Separate metadata input required if key mapping to be supported in aggregation relation. Or API to be provided. Association: This is a structural relationship which connects one entity to another. An associate between two entities is able to navigate from one entity to another entity and vice versa. From UI: From Callback: From Middleware message: Entity conversion: At the time of entity conversion from one object type to another, the new BO created is treated similar to new Entity creation from UI. Secondary key mapping: This is to decide either to perform create or update operation on messages received from Middleware. For example, order ID is a primary key in order BO and map this with legacy ID as secondary key. While processing messages from SAP this, if legacy ID already exists it performs update operation otherwise create operation. Field Mapping: Message processing Entity conversion Source entity Source entity property Target entity Target entity property Object type Mapping: entity conversion from one object type to another is allowed if maintained here. Source entity Source object type Target entity Target Object type

EntitySet is a collection of Entity objects. KloEntitySet extends the Array prototype. KloEntitySet has three behaviours. Query result: direct result of query execution. Part of primary relation: by accessing primary relation on entity returns KloEntitySet. Part of non-primary relation: by accessing non-primary relation on entity returns KloEntitySet.

Business Object (BO) is a logical unit used in a business. It is made up of one or multiple entities. E.g. If we take an invoice (bill of purchase) it consists of a header and purchased items. Header and item entities (tables) are required to store this information. Either item or header alone does not make any sense. So invoice header and invoice item entity together make the invoice BO. BO is a hierarchical tree of entities. Each entity must belong to one and only one BO definition. BO has only one root entity (top-level). The rest of the entities (child entities) are aggregated into root or other entities to construct the entity tree. kloBroker always transmits the full BO in the Message. When any entity becomes dirty it also pulls the root entity instance in the writeset. Deletion of any entity instance deletes all the cascaded aggregate entity instances. In authorization, all the authorization upon parents up to root are also applied except the middleware message process. Example: d_order (root entity/BO) d_order_item (child entity) d_order_conditions (child entity)

The data object in KloBase is known as Entity. An entity has one or more named properties, each of which can have one or more values. Each entity in the KloBase Datastore has a key that uniquely identifies it. In simple words, we can say Entity is a database table. In DBMS, we store data in the form of a table containing information about entity types like order, address etc. In an order database, a table containing information about all the orders. For example, orders have properties like customer, amount, products, etc these are attributes which combine to make a table. One entity must be part of only one BO. Types of Entity: Persistent: Entity which physically exists/ stored in a database as a table. Fields in Persistent Entities could be either Persistent or Transient. Persistent Entity by default Tenant Dependent can be made Tenant Independent <roadmap> Persistent Entity by default are User Dependent can be made User Independent Transient: It is an in-memory entity that doesn’t exist in a database. All fields in Transient Entity are Transient only. It can be constructed out of query results or by code to hold the value at runtime. Messages can’t be communicated through Middleware using a Transient entity. Config: The application can create a config entity that holds the fixed values provided at design time . It can be accessed with a key only. Query does not work on these entities. FW only- Types: Metadata <roadmap> Archive <roadmap> History Entity Naming convention and length​ Entity names should use only English lowercase alphabets (a-z), digits (0-9) and underscore (_) and up to 31 chars max length. The first char must be d/t/c based on type. Transactional (‘d’), Transient (‘t’), Config (‘c’). The following are auto-generated Status config starts with ‘s’ Custom Status starts with ‘u’ Framework entity starts with ‘m’ <roadmap> Archive entity starts with ‘a’ <roadmap> Union or archive and transactional entity starts with ‘v’ <roadmap> History entity starts with ‘h’ Each entity has one or more properties. Each entity property has one property type. Each property type has a domain assigned. Entity Entity Property (1-n) Property Type (1) Domain (1) Provide a unique entity name and mark if it is a root entity. The root entity is considered a BO. To define an entity you need at least one entity property, It could be either transient or regular (persisted in DB). Entity attributes: Attribute Description Entity Name : string Unique ID across all flavors. See the naming convention Is Root : boolean This defines the Root entity of a BO. BO Name is the same as this Entity Name. Root entity also behaves as BO. Entity Type Persistent/Transient/Configuration. Network mode This is an optional parameter. Effective network mode is determined with the following precedence rule. First having the highest precedence. 1. Network specified at QueryInstance Level. 2. Network specified at Query Metadata Level. 3. Network specified at Entity Metadata Level. 4. Network mode of Parent Query if it is a relation query. 5. Network mode of App. BO Name Name of Root entity name. Can create/read / update / Delete The default value is TRUE, insert/read/update/delete is allowed on the entity. False value forces insert/read/update/delete operation to return an error in the specified flavor. Use it for master and other protected objects to be editable only in maintenance or OEM flavor. Applied only on the Server side for calls initiated from clients. Server-side rules and kloBroker still allow even if false Check Dirty: re-evaluate all entities for dirty before calling on an update. Has created fields To know when and by whom facts are created in the datastore. if TRUE, s_created_on and s_created_by fields will be added. Values in these two fields are maintained only by a system, Application code can not alter this. s_created_on is a timestamp data type and s_created_by is the logged-in empID as a string datatype. Values of these fields are captured on user events hence if the entity is getting created by klobroker it accepts the value from the source. If a new entity is created within kloBroker message processing or by scheduler then technical user and creation time is recorded. Created By is the user by which the Background job is scheduled. Has modified fields To know when and by whom facts are last modified in the datastore. This records the last changed time and employee ID. If true, s_modified_on and s_modified_by fields are added. The system updates these fields on every create/change of entity. The system also considers the root entity of the BO updated together with the modified entity. Tri-State : 1. None: fields do not exist 2. byUser: value is updated only by user action. kloBroker processing does not modify the value. 3. always Has Status If TRUE, s_status and s_status_custom fields will get added by kloBase at the time of update schema. See more details in the Status section. Has Attachment If enabled, Framework allows the attachment against this entity object and the attachment link entity becomes part of the BO. See the Attachment section for more details Has Brand The entity is brand dependent or independent. if TRUE, the s_brand field will get added by FW at the time of update schema. See the Configurability section for more details. Has Object Type Entity follows Object Type behaviour. if TRUE, s_object_type field of type int(11) gets added by FW at the time of update schema. See the Configurability section for more details. Has Config Framework will provide a config entity which can be further customised with configuration fields. If object type is not applicable this is an object type independent config. Config is accessible in application by using entityInstance.config See the Configurability section for more details. <roadmap> Has Doc Flow <roadmap> Owns Doc ID <roadmap> Has History This is to maintain the changing history of a BO. If TRUE, it creates a separate blob or transactional table to maintain the history of all changes. Every change on an entity gets captured in the history table and the main transactional table holds only the latest record. The table name starts with ‘h’. Only on the root entity or full BO? Maintain change history only for specific status? Object type-based configuration? is this supported offline <roadmap> Has Archive This is to facilitate data archiving. This can be enabled only on the root entity/ BO. Always complete BO gets archived. Table name starts with ‘a’. One more table was created as a view which starts with ‘v’ to fetch transactions and archive table data as a union. > Is the ID series exhausted? - Server Side: Push data from the transaction table to the Archive table. This means data will get deleted from the main table once moved to the archive table. - Maintain configuration based on which data to be archived. - Background job scheduler to push data from transactional table to Archive table. While archiving no dirty objects are allowed. - APIs: archive(). This API will work only on the server side. - clearArchive() : this deletes all records from the archive table. - Update to offline endpoints. This deletes the entity in the local DB - ON_ARCHIVE event. - Query: by default, the query fetches data from the transactional table(d table) but if archiving is enabled, users can explicitly mark to fetch archived data. This is a union of both transactional and archived tables. - The IsArchived flag is returned TRUE by the framework if data is from the archive table. This flag can be used by the application to highlight archived data or disable edit options. - Do not allow the archived records to be updated. The framework throws an error if any dirty object is found for archived records. - Value help/ Association relation for archived masters. Example: - Update transaction entity: this should adjust the archive and view. - Add/Delete new property - New relation/ Delete relation - Client Side: delete data in client DB(local) and do not send any updates to the server. - API: deleteLocal() - kloQuery has deleteLocal(); Dependency: Does not allow you to archive until the related(supplied by application. Do not follow entity relation) object gets archived. Dependency is decided based on aggregate relations. Helper function to be written by Application to check if any dependent object exists. <roadmap> Has Time Dependent At any given point in time, an entity has a value for each of its attributes. If the values of any attribute for an entity may change over time and you are interested to know the value of an attribute at a particular point in time, it is meaningful for entities to have properties exactly when they exist and mark the entity as time dependent. In case you are interested only in the current value of the attribute, do not mark it as time-dependent. > This is to maintain the periodic(time-dependent) data with valid time. If any entity is marked as time-dependent, the framework creates below three fields in the table. In a BO any entity can be time dependent. - s_valid_from(Timestamp) - Validity start date and time. Part of the primary key. The default is the current date. - s_valid_to(Timestamp) - Validity end date and time. The default value is 31-12-9999. - s_active(boolean) - the latest record will be marked as TRUE. At a time only one entry should be active and the validity period should not overlap for two records. By default Valid from is current date but can be changed. Past date: Config to be maintained for a past date is allowed or not. Message processing(from SAP, device or to device) follows the config for the past date. If allowed it accepts the date from the message or UI otherwise it changes the FROM date to current. If the first entry, except the values provided from UI or Message, marks the active flag TRUE. In case of an update, modify the current existing active record’s s_valid_to accordingly(based on s_valid_from the new record). Also, mark the current entry as active flag FALSE and the new entry as TRUE. Both update and create should be in the same transaction. Mainly this will be used for master data tables where periodic data is required. For example, pricing, user address, etc. MRP/Pricing of a product can be changed periodically. Can not be changed based on object type or flavor. This can be defined only in the owning flavor of an account. <roadmap> Approval In case approval is required for a BO, at the time of creation of the BO it should not change the current record. Once it is approved, then only it gets activated. To consider this scenario, a separate blob table is maintained for ‘To Be Approved’ objects. Once final approval is done it will get moved to the main transaction table and activated. If enabled, an approval flag will be provided from the framework. - This is applicable for time-dependent and time-independent entities. - Configurable on object type based. Workflow will be discussed separately later. Is Metadata Has Tenant Is Config AppVariant Is History Is Archive Tenant Dependent TRUE Tenant Independent Configuration TRUE TRUE TRUE Transient TRUE Example: Take an example of order BO. Order BO has three entities: d_order, d_order_item, d_order_item. Out of this one entity has to be marked as a root entity to define a BO. d_order (root entity) d_order_item (child entity) d_order_conditions (child entity)

Entity Property is also known as an attribute or member variable in an Entity or field in the database table. It holds the value in runtime. It has a Property ID (name) and Property type. Property names are used for accessing the value of the entity. The Property Type defines the data type and behaviour of the property. The behaviour of the Entity Property is captured in the meta-model by defining the below attributes. Attribute Description Entity Property ID Unique within an entity across all flavors. Can’t be changed later. Property Type/Element ID Select the existing Property type or create a new one. This defines data type, field length, precision, etc. It can be changed only in the owning flavor of an Entity. Selection of a domain, size and property type:Choose to existExtend fromCopy and override: copy any existing property type and change the parameters. This makes a copy of all attributes except Property Type ID.Create New Type Regular / Primary Key / Transient Field / Calculated Field /System Fields. / Secondary Key Value Help Select already defined Value help ID. Wherever this property ID is bound in UI, VH is automatically applied. Can be overwritten in the screen field. Is restricted Value Restrict the input value within the associated VH. Tri value: None, Strict(UI and BOL), Suggestions(Only UI side). (Note: Moved this to Entity property from Property type). Is Mandatory Empty or Null values are not permitted during entity creation/update. Do not force the UI as mandatory. Non-Key mandatory fields are not necessary for selection. Default Value Default values will be populated immediately after creating a new Entity. $ Variables can also be used. ID Series Mention the ID series here if applicable for this field. Naming convention: Max length allowed for property ID is 31 char. Only English lowercase alphabets (a-z), digits (0-9) and underscore (_) are supported. Entity property ID starting with ‘s_’ is reserved for systems fields by framework. Types of Entity Property: Persisted: Property which physically exists/stored in the database as a table column. Persisted Property-owning Entity also has to be a Persistent Entity only. Transient: Transient property is a runtime attribute only. Use this to hold some value at runtime. Example: query result alias value, value-filled or determined in rule, from UI set and get attribute. Primary key: Primary key of a table. Values of the set of primary key fields must be unique. If the field is the primary key, the isNull/Nulable property will be marked as false automatically. System-Defined Properties: Based on the relevant flags in entity definition, the framework provides standard columns in a table. Field name, Data Type, Label, etc are already defined and no changes are allowed here. Developers can’t add a system field in the following: Object Type Status Brand Tenant ID Created On Modified On Created By Modified By Valid From Valid To Active Source Field name Field DataType Has Object Type s_object_type int(11) Has Status s_status,s_status_custom varchar(32),varchar(32) Has Brand s_brand int(11) Tenant ID s_tenant_id int(11)(pk) Created Fields s_created_on,s_created_by Timestamp,varchar(255) Modified Fields s_modified_on,s_modified_by Timestamp,varchar(255) Date dependent s_valid_from,s_valid_to,s_active Timestamp**(pk)**,Timestamp,boolean Calculated Property: When the property is read, an application-defined get<Property_id> is executed. When the property is written, the application-defined set<Property_id> is executed. Mostly used to return some aggregated value based on other conditions. Works when is calculated property is selected in the entity property definition. These fields do not persist and cannot hold any value at runtime. It can only return some value. The getter/setter function will be provided by the application developer. BOL will invoke this method when the property is accessed. This property is also bindable in UI. Property with Variable, Method and persisted combination? Providing getter/setter function for the calculated field: Mostly used for dynamic calculations. Define an entity property in metadata. For each entity, the framework provides a <entityname>.ts class which can be used to define the getter/setter function of any property. Through KloIDE, the app developer has to write a getter/setter function for the entity property. These functions are accessible using entity objects. <entityobject>.<propertyID>() and this.<propertyID>(). When the getter/setter is invoked, this will be the entity object and you are free to access any property/relation of the entity. Example: Getter: Syntax of property getter: get<space><property name with the first letter capitalised> public Qty1 : number; public get Qty():number{ return this.Qty1; } OR public get Qty():number{ return 20; } Setter: Syntax of property getter: set<space><property name with the first letter capitalised> public set Qty(newVal:number){ this.Qty1 = newVal; } Note: ‘this’ is an instance of the current entity here. More generated helper functions of property missing like <propertyID>_vh

Entity relation relates one entity with another entity. Relation has a unique name within the Entity. Relation name is used for accessing the result of the relation. Assessing getter of relation as property returns entitySet object which gets filled on ES.fetch() resolve and also triggers data change events. Relations are categorised as primary relation, aggregate relation and association. Association: An association is a structural relationship which connects one entity with another. Given an association between two entities, one can navigate from one entity to the other entity and vice versa. Association relations can be across BOs. By default, each relation is of type Association if it is not marked as Aggregated or Primary. Example1: d_order_item (source) d_material_master (Related) Create a relation to show the material description, LOB, or other properties of the material. Example2: d_order_item (source) d_order (Related) If you want to navigate from the order Item to the order header. Define a relation between the Item as Source and Header as Related entity. Aggregated Relation: Aggregation is a type of association where two entities(tables) are tightly bound. In some cases, we might come across “whole-part” relationships between two Entities, in which one entity is a part of another entity. Such a relationship is known as an aggregation. An aggregation relationship can be described in simple words as "an object of one class can own or access the objects of another class. Aggregate relations can be across BOs. Primary Relation: This is a special kind of aggregate relation within the BO boundary. All entities in a BO are navigable from the root entity once unidirectional and only once. Below are the use cases of a primary relation: Message processing Keymapping Find Parent Example: d_order ( root entity) d_order_item d_order_conditions Here d_order is the root entity and the other two are child entities in Order BO. Hence relation has to be defined between these entities. Create a relation on d_order entity with d_order_item of type “Primary” and query property is “order_id”. Create a relation on d_order_item entity with d_order_conditions of type “Primary” and query properties are “order_id” and “order_item”. Define Relationship: Let’s create a relation between two entities using the Data Studio. To create a relation go to the source entity where you want a relation with another entity.
