EntitySet is a collection of Entity objects. KloEntitySet extends Array prototype. KloEntitySet have three behavior. Query result: direct result of query execution. Part of primary relation: by accessing primary relation on entity returns KloEntitySet. Part of non Primary relation: by accessing non primary relation on entity returns KloEntitySet. Deprecated**:** add(obj, position,executeCreateRules) use newEntityP instead Deprecated**:** newEntity(insertAt: number=0, executeCPMRules: boolean=false, underlyingObject: {}={}) use newEntityP instead newEntityP(insertAt: number=0, executeCreateRules?:boolean=false, EntityJson?: string | Entity) promise<Entity> Creates a new entity and returns after CreateRule execution(if the second parameter executeCreateRules is TRUE). insertTo parameter specifies the position(starts at 0) on a new entity in the entity set. Default value is zero. executeCreateRules parameter specifies if Create Rule to be executed inline. Default is false. Returns Promise and resolves with new Entity Object. EntityJson parameter allows to following: • add a valid JSON Representation of Entity or Entity object itself to the Entityset. Object representation can be partial. Like {objecttype:0, Brand:’A’} If a Valid JSON is passed, if a deep structure Enityset will create an entity out of it including the primary relations recursively and adds to the corresponding Entityset. This call will resolve with the top level entity object. If the entity Object is passed it is used as a template and the copy is made with a new primary key. If added on Query result KLoEntitySet than parent primary keys needs to be explicitly filled by developer. During the commit of a transaction if the parent keys are missing or the wrong transaction will fail. If added on primary relation KLoEntitySet than parent primary keys are auto filled in the returned entity. Non Primary relation KLoEntitySet does not support New Entity use Add instead. All the fields marked internal ID series are populated. All the fields have default values specified are populated. Example: entitySet.newEntityP(1, TRUE, {}) applyFilter Manual filtration required calling the applyFilter method on the entity set. Value help filtration is automatically done if you are using an InputExtender or Combobox provided by kloTouch. Attach the livechange event handler to the search box control. Get the user typed filter string from the event parameter. Get the instance of the entity set bound to the list. Call applyFilter on the KloEnitySet with the filter string. Example: function(oEvent) { var sQuery = “” //get the value from live change event object var notifES = sap.ui.getCore().getModel('notification').getProperty('/list'); notifES.applyFilter(sQuery); } fetch() :Promise This fires a query on relation entity or value help and returns the result set. Syntax: entityInstance.relation_name.fetch(); entityInstance.<fieldName>_VH.fetch(); Example: Get Order Items from Order header. logisticsES[0].logistics_items.fetch().then(function () { var logItems = logisticsES[0].logistics_items; //do something on logistics item list }); addJSONtoEntitySet(dataObject: any, insertTo?: any, executeCreateRules?: boolean) archive(): Promise<any> Archive all the objects in EntitySet.

Middleware allows set of configuration on its functionalities.

This method allows to attach a new message processor, A message processor is a class which intakes a downloaded message and builds the BO structure out of it and persist these BO/Entity. When middleware starts processing the downloaded message from server, based on the download process count, messages are read and the message processor callback is invoked with the messages, Now then the MessageProcessor class is responsible to deal with the message and resolve when the message is processed or reject in case of error so that middleware can continue processing the next message and handle error on the current message. By default Klarion BOL will attach a MessageProcessor class to handle the V4 middleware messages, in case the message processing has to be changed, attach a new MessageProcessor and encapsulate the logic to it only the expected return is a Promise and resolve or reject Ex. mw.attachMessageProcessor(function(messages){ return new MessageProcessor().process(messages);})

Allows to attach convertor callbacks, which has to be called before BEFORE_ADD_TO_UPLOAD_Q BEFORE_PUSH_TO_SERVER_Q AFTER_PULL_FROM_SERVER_Q AFTER_LOAD_FROM_DOWNLOAD_Q These callbacks are called with the message object which can be morphed according to the application logic and the resultant message is considered by the framework. Each callback is expected to return the morphed message, or a Promise and resolves with morphed message. Each call back can get array of messages, call back should be able to handle this. Ex: mw.attachConverter(AFTER_PULL_FROM_SERVER_Q,function(messages){ //manipulate and resolve or return data here }) Dependent Entity: Maintain dependent entity while subscribing endpoint resolver. This will be send with WM message under Dependent[ ] section. Any entity is allowed. Relation is not mandatory.

kloudBase supports a rich set of network modes. Two most frequent network modes are online and offline. OnLine network mode refers to the capability of running the program in a browser or installed mobile app (client) communicating with server for every need. Network connectivity from client to server is a must. If Screen needs to show open Orders, kloBO will go to the server to get the data for Open Order and give it to UI for display. Similarly all the changes on the browser or device app will be collected and sent to the server for validating and saving. Offline network mode refers to the capability to run the program with weak or infrequent network availability. Application stores the relevant data locally and keeps the local cache and server data updated as and when finds the connectivity. Browser and installed mobile app both are offline capable. Cached Online network mode refers to the capability of client communicating with server for every need but speedup the interaction by suggesting data from local cache. Commit Online network mode refers to the capability of client serving the data from local cache but save always goes thru online and also modifies local cache. SAP Online refers to the capability of all the transaction goes to SAP via gateway server. SAP Cached Online

Collection of Object Types is Object Group. Screen usage Object Group which defines the behaviour of particular screen/object. Object types of similar kind of behavior and going to be used in one screen has to be bundled in one Object Group. Object Group to Object Type mapping(m:n): One object type can be part of multiple Object Groups. One screen can have only one Object group. Constants for Object Group? Abbreviation : define object group abbreviation like ‘i’ for invoice and ‘o’ for order. This abbreviation can be used in ID series as prefix or some other cases where you want to differentiate the object. Usage: Screen Rule execution Example: Object groups in Order: Sales Order Purchase Order Stock Transport Order

Object Type defines the possible behaviour of an BO/Entity. Object type has a unique key and description. Object type key is unique across all entities and can not be reused across entities. One entity can store multiple objects data if behavior of the objects are different then define multiple object types. Work when has_object_type is marked TRUE for an entity. Do not add any Entity property to add object type field this will be taken care by kloBase based on the Object type flag on Entity level. Possible object types for an entity has to be defined at design time and maintain via kloIDE. Data type is int(11). Max value is 2147483648. Supports merging based on uses relation. s_object_type holds the object type key. Descriptions are part of value help definition. Constants for Object Type. If the object type is false for an entity than -1 is reserved value. Abbreviation : define object type abbreviation like ‘i’ for invoice and ‘o’ for order. This abbreviation can be used in ID series as prefix. Syntax: $objecttype.abr Variable to be used: Constants $VARIABLE Object Group to Object Type Object Type to abbreviation Object Type to Object Type text Display Messages: Object type description supports translatable description use as substitute in title, message, etc with $objecttype.dec. Define language dependent text to support multilocal. Create Entity: while creating an Entity, Object Type has an important role to load the configuration, assign ID from ID series, Rule to be executed, VH to be loaded. Tuner: configurations are maintained on object type to control the behaviour of the application. For more details please visit the Config section. Rule subscription: rules are subscribed on Entity and Object Type. ID Series: ID series can be defined on object type or common for all object types. Value Help/F4: Object conversion mapping: Status: Custom Status: Middleware message processing can be controlled in endpoint resolver. Create operation(in UI-action or Rule) decide which object type to be used. From UI you can pass only the Object types which are part of the Object Group of that screen. UI elements behaviour can be defined like editable, visibility, mandatory, etc. Not supported: Authorization is not applied on object type. For example there are different types of orders. Object types in Order can be defined like: Normal Order Emergency/Fast Track Order

In today's modern world omni channel application supporting multiple form factors and tolerance to network is a must. To support the diversity of device/hardware, OS, Servers, Clouds etc.. we end up creating one application multiple times. For any business application underlying data is a back bone. Unlike old 3 tier application architecture KloudBase promotes micro service with stateless models. This architecture gives tremendous portability and infinite scalability to meet modern needs. With in built klobroker it also enables distributed computing hence multiple system owners can easily exchange their data among themselves to form the network. kloBO refers to mid tier in kloudBase architecture. It is based on the meta model. It accelerates the application development by providing configurability, override, run anywhere ( browser, android app, iphone app, windows mobile app). Developers can write the business rules in JavaScript and based on the deployment model kloBO runs it. kloBO is stateless hence provides infinite scalability and redundancy. kloBO also provides the authorization for security. kloBO consists of a few core objects like Entity, Query, Rule, Transaction, Value Help and configuration etc. Query as name refers are similar to database query. It is used for fetching data from a database. To understand it better let’s go with example I have an entity ( table) called “d_order”. It has multiple columns including a column named “state”. I want to fetch all the record where state == “open” In db term I will write sql as “Select * from d_order WHERE state = ‘open’” and execute to get the desired result. Query also does the same with a few value added services like it gives the ability to fetch the data for offline applications similar to online application. Abstracts the multiple syntax of Odata, SQl, Json etc. so the programmer can concentrate on the business logic. It gives a few short hand optimization like pagination column select. Security features like authorization etc.. For general purpose understanding, we can see it like below. Following mapping only helps to kick start with assumptions. Db Table: Entity definition Db Table’s Column: Entity Property definition Data type of column: property type with domain Business logic: Rule Commit: Transaction.save Rollback: Transaction.refresh Db SQL query: kloQuery Execute Query: kloQuery.executeP() Result of SQL execution: EntitySet behaves as array of entity Row of sql result: entity Value of column in a result row: entity’s property We can also visualize kloBO as ORM each entity represents a class capable of saving it’s own data, entity properties acts as class member rules acts as methods. Behavior of kloBO varies as per environment. Given the same model ( meta model for application) behavior of query when it is executed ui ( device or browser) are different compared to when it is executed by kloRule as business logic. Let’s see the working example for Order Object. Simple example of reading and writing Data define( abc) Var Orderid = “1234” Var qMan = kloUIQueryManager.getInstance(); Var q = qMan.getEntityQuery(“d_order”); Q.orderid = myOrderID; q.executeP().then((es)=>{ If (es.length >0){ Var ord = es[0]; Ord.qty = Ord.qty +1 Tr. save().then(()=>{ console.log() }); } });

The Status of an object represents the current state of a particular object. Possible status of transactional objects is maintained in a meta model using kloIDE which has Key and Description. Based on the current status of the object screen behavior can be controlled like Visibility, Read-only, Actions, other behavioural decisions, etc. Work when has_status is marked true for an Entity. s_status column is created in all the entities where Has Status is marked as True which holds the status key. Supports merging based on uses relation. To understand Status usage let's take an example. There is an Order placed on any online web portal. Order has the status like Order Placed Dispatched Delivered Canceled Returned Here the first three status are sequential but order can be canceled only with the status “Order Placed”, “Dispatched”. Also “Dispatched” and “Delivered” status can be changed by Delivery Boy or Backend team but “Canceled” status can be set by Customer, Supplier Backend team and Customer Care Executive. Status Profile Status Types: None Single Multi valued Custom status Customization of status as per account/rollout Works when has status is marked true for an entity Possible mapping between status as per implementation is maintained in m_status_custom table as metadata Supports merging based on uses relation. Used in the implementation phase. s_status_custom holds the value of custom status key Description, icon or additional properties will be part of value help definition. Object type will have -1 if the entity does not have object types.

On server physical data may need to be hard partitioned across a set of people. Normally in a multi organization scenario each establishment owns a tenant. Each tenant has a unique end point id assigned.One tenant can also host the data for multiple organizations.

Every attempt to create, update, or delete an entity takes place in the context of a transaction. A single transaction can include any number of such operations. To maintain the consistency of the data, the transaction ensures that all of the operations it contains are applied to KloBase Datastore as a unit or, if any of the operations fails, that none of them are applied. Furthermore, all strongly-consistent reads (ancestor queries or gets) performed within the same transaction observe a consistent snapshot of the data. Auto replace dirty object in query. Merage of result. Intermixing across flavor, version, network more etc? Deprecated: TransactionManager::getTransaction(txnName: string): Transaction use Transaction.getInstance(txnName: string) instead. static getInstance(txnName: string) Returns the Transaction Object. Creates new if it does not exist, otherwise returns the current named one. Transaction.getInstance(); add(txnObject: KloQuery): Transaction Adds the query object into transaction. Any object returned from this query will participate in this transaction. If query not added explicitly in transaction becomes part of default transaction. Why do we need this here?? Need in case of separate transaction. Move to Transaction section baseController:: getTransaction(transaction_name(optional) : string, bAddToController: boolean ): TransactionManager @parameter: transaction_name - this is name of the transaction. @parameter: bAddToController - flag either to add to controller model transaction. This is optional. Default value is true. A transaction is a sequence of operations performed (using one or more Query statements) on a database as a single logical unit of work. The effects of all the Query statements in a transaction can be either all committed (applied to the database) or all rolled back (undone from the database). In a Controller, Model is defined and has a name. Transaction can share the same name or could be different. In case if you need an additional transaction to perform some task in between the main transaction, create the transaction with parameter myTransactionName. oController.getTransaction(myTransactionName); To understand the Transaction concept, let’s see there is a scenario of “create delivery from an order”. In this case there are below three operations to be performed: • Create delivery Reserve the stock Update order All these operations should be either success or fail but together. Commit the transaction if all success or roll back if any one of them failed. Commit Transaction. Clear Transaction Examples: //Get transaction by name and add. oController.getTransaction(myTransactionName).then(function (Transaction) { oController.getQueryP('d_logistics', "E", oController)then(function (oQueryInstance) { oController.addToTranscation(oQuery, oController); or Transaction.add(oQueryInstance); oQueryInstance.executeP(); resolve(oQueryInstance); } } hasDirtyObjects(): boolean Returns TRUE if any object in current transaction is dirty, else FALSE. Example: var transaction = oController.transaction; transaction.hasDirtyObjects() clear(): boolean Removes the object added to transaction validate() Performs as save on all the operations except DB Commit. commit(): Promise<any> Commit has to be invoked when you need to persist with the changes in DB. getStatus(): string Returns transaction status hasDirtyObjects():boolean Returns true if txn objects contain at least one dirty object.

In Application, ID/key is frequently used to store the related data. In the user interface descriptive explanation is required. To achieve it, the ID/key is represented by other single/ multiple data from the related table. Value help is also used to supply the choices available to fill ( combo, dropdown, auto complete) as selection data. Value help can impose the restriction for accepting the input value only from valid set. Value Help (VH) is independent reusable object hence as a best practice always check the existing VHs for reuse before creating the new one. While creating a new one always categorize with entity name so later others can find it easily for reuse. It should be named . Value help Type: Define Value Help: Value Help Name(32 char): unique id across all flavors. Space is not allowed. Entity Name Object Type Query Saved Query VH Transaction VH Language Dependent Config Config Language Dependent System Fields Query Type Runtime Modeled Native Description(255 char) Restrict Value Life Cycle On Session On View Dependent Live Change Parameter: query ID? Scope Dependent Key Display Text: can give multiple values? Icon Query Property change Live Change Threshold Data Sync Query ID Naming convention: Length: 32 char Starts with ‘vh_’ Assign VH: Usage: Provide users with a set of possible values or suggestion items. Show text in UI. VH Design: Associating VH: Entity <>----> Entity Property ----> Property Type -----> VH Query <>----> Query Property -----> Property Type -----> VH VH can be used independently in UI and inside kloRule. Provide users with a set of possible values or suggestion items. Value help is provided by either by an entity or generic, hence it is grouped by an entity. Example: material master can provide a value help that gives material_id and material_description and can be used at multiple places like sales order or in procurement. Property type captures the value help id used for this entity property. Value help definition will be captured separately. One VH ID can be used at multiple places. Goes with offline preferred approach.
TYPES OF VALUE HELPS The type of ValueHelp to be used can be selected under object_type in BOL_EDITOR**. **The Following valueHelps are supported :

Queries are used to read the data from the table, so these queries can be used in valueHelps as well. On Selection of object type, query type has to be selected, it could be one of the following : Runtime Query Native Query Modeled Query On Selection of Runtime Query, query id is has to be set from the existing BO/Entity Names.. On Selection of Native, query Id has to be set from the existing Native queries. On Selection of Modeled, query Id has to be set from the existing Modeled queries. App developer designes a query. Query id is provided as a part of value help definition, which will return a set of values, which will be used as suggestion items. BOL will simply fire the query to get the data. Key, Display Text and Dependents has to be set based on the query type selected. Key & Display Text: Key and Display Text values can vary based on the query type selected. If Runtime Query is selected it contains the entity properties from the selected Entity Name. If Modeled query or Native Query is selected it contains the list of entity properties of the **return Entity **of the selected Query. Dependents : Dependents values can vary based on the query type selected. If the Modeled query or Native query is selected it contains a list of query properties based on the selected query . If Runtime Query is selected it contains a list of entity properties from the selected Entity/BO represented as EntityName.PropertyId. Example: Let’s assume the valueHelp is grouped under “d_material “ Entity which has material_id and material_description as two properties The Key is set to material_id and Display Text is set to material_description. Both Key and Display Text values can be displayed to the user concurrently or just Display Text can be showed and key is set internally. In The above Image Key is IN and Display Text is India. Dependent Example : Let's assume there are two comboBoxes which contains Country, State In The query, we will create one query properties country and create the query as SELECT * FROM States WHERE country =:country And assign the dependent field as country. We will take the country from the first comboBox and fire the Query which gets required Data. *Multiple Dependent Properties are Not supported. If Multiple Dependent Properties are required we can fire EntityQuery with multiple where conditions natively and assign the model explicitly.

Saved Queries are similar to queries which are fired during initial Sync, so these saved queries can be used in valuehelp as well. After which we have to select the saved query id. And for savedquery as well the key, Display Text and Dependent fields are enabled and works the same way they did for query these can be referred from here. App developer designes a saved query and saved query id is provided as a part of value help definition

VHID Dependent Filter ID Text Icon Lang …... priority - 0 low - EN priority - 1 medium - EN priority - 2 high - EN priority - 3 Very high - EN w_type - 4 WORK1 - FR w_type - 5 WORK2 - FR w_type - 6 WORK3 - FR w_type - 7 WORK4 - FR Config has two subtypes CONFIG CONFIG LANG Both of them use the same table to get the data. CONFIG: In case of CONFIG we start by creating a valuehelp and providing a valuehelp name and by selecting the object type as Config and we provide the name in which the value should get filtered from the table as parameter. Ex: From the above table to get the values of priority we start by giving the valuehelp name as vh_priority or any name And in the field of parameter we provide the value as priority. Framework provide value help table which captures value help id, filter, description, icon, language code and translated description. Every Entity is associated with system properties like s_object_type,s_status and s_brand each of these are in turn associated with there own description, icon etc. Hence these system fields can be used as valuehelps. The values for these are stored in the metadata tables ex: object_type Entity name description 101 so_hdr header System fields like s_object_type,s_status and s_brand can have its on description and icon provided as a part of definition The usage of these values (l_satus_ivon,l_status,l_object_type) etc are provided by framework as valuehelps. (to be continued) SEMANTICS When an entity property has value help (property type holds a value hep id), then a new property with name [<property_name>_vh] will be provided by framework. This property will hold icon : returns icon value provided description : returns description suggetionItems : returns set of suggestion items These properties are bindable to sap ui5 controls and can be used in Rules also While using, make sure it is loaded completely, since this can go for a lazy load. <property_name>_vh.fetch().then(function(){ //ensures that the values are loaded. }) Fetch will return a promise. Fetch has to be used if value help is accessed other than in sap ui5 bindings. Example: For material_id: material_id_vh will return { icon:””, description:””, suggestionItems:[] }

ID series are used for populating the IDs/ Key in the entity’s property by kloBO. If an application wants to allocate the ID self, either it should not assign the ID series or marked it as none. kloBO will allocate the ID on the first read of the ID.

ID Series are customizable in application during configuration hence it supports override or selection of id series based on Brand and Object Type. Application can maintain multiple entries of ID Series ( Entity, Property, [Object Type], [Brand] -> ID Series). Most accurate matching ID Series definition is picked by kloBase for further processing based on precedence first to object type next to brand. For example, the “Order” Object has maintained the following. ID series “order_base_series” with no Brand and no Object type ID series “order_b1_series” with “B1” Brand and no Object type ID series “order_ot1_series” with no Brand and no “1” Object type ID series “order_b1_ot1_series” with “B1” Brand and “1” Object type Object type abbreviation? $objecttype.abr If the order instance in question belongs to B1 and object type 1 then order_b1_ot1_series definition will be picked for processing . If the order instance in question belongs to B1 and object type 2 then order_b1_series definition will be picked for processing . If the order instance in question belongs to B2 and object type 3 then order_base_series definition will be picked for processing .
documents.s: How to assign the ID series to Entity Property

documents.t: Highest: Exact match of ObjectType and brand Medium: Exact match of Object type and Brand as “All”. Low: Object type “All” and Brand as “All”. Lowest: no key allocated.

ID series support two types of counters. GUID: returns 32 char UUID as key Autonumber: returns incremental number for allocated chunk. The auto number section. None: no number is assigned to the developer to fill the number. Generally used during override in tuner to remove the ID series. ID series value to be filled in assigned entity property comes from counter. Once the counter generates the key it can be formatted with prefix, post fix, $vars etc. Counter and pattern To be filled… AutoNumber AutoNumber is a running number that starts from Starts till end. Each tenant and offline devices gets the reserve interval from auto number. Size of the allocated interval can be controlled using the Size parameter. Scope: Default is global, only one autoNumber is used for all the tenant and offline endpoints interval. Tenant: per tenant separate series is used. User: per user separate series is used. Chunksize: default 100 can be set to desired number. Range: start and end range. Populating ID/Key in child object / key mapping behaviour

kloQuery is a meta model for fetching the data from the data store, like SQL in RDBMS. For example, the entity ( table) name “d_order” has multiple columns including “s_status”. To fetch all the record for open order in RDBMS need SQL as “Select ord_id, qty, ord_date from d_order WHERE d_order.status = ‘open’ Orderby ord_date ASC” and execute to get the desired result. kloQuery behaves similarly with a few value added services, it gives the ability to fetch the data seamlessly for offline applications and online applications. Abstracts out multiple syntax of Odata, SQl, Json etc. so that programmers can concentrate on the business logic. It gives a few short hand optimization like pagination column select. Security features like authorization etc.. Runtime Query does not need modeling. It inherits behavior from entity and BO definition and operates with API. Later we will consider more control on query by modeling the kloQuery. kloQuery is made with Query, QueryProperty, PropertyType, Select, orderby etc.. It returns kloEntityset. kloEntityset is an array of kloEntities. For e.g. consider following SQL SELECT ord_id, qty AS ord_qty, ord_date FROM d_order WHERE d_order.status = ‘open’ Orderby ord_date ASC” Let q = await oController.getQueryP(“d_order”); q.setProperty(“d_order.status”, ‘open’); q.setOrderBy([{fieldname:”d_order.ord_date” , sort_type:”ASC”}]); Let result: kloEntitySet = await q.ExecuteP(); Above SQL needs to be represented by kloQuery. WHERE clause of SQL d_order.status is the input search criteria modeled as query property and property type of the query property will describe the type(string) caption and value help. Similarly kloQuery also has OrderBy and Select together with other constructs to hold the SQL constraints. Query objects are directly bindable in UI for user input and capable of providing label and value help. kloQuery can be represented by premodeled query by name and at runtime enhancing with constraints. Acquiring the Query instance: Deprecated: getQueryWithTanscation use getQueryP instead Deprecated: getQuery use getQueryP instead Query Manager Deprecated use kloQuery.getQueryP(...) instead. In UI controller extended from baseController oController.getQueryP(queryName : string, Transaction(optional): string): promise<KloQuery> In side Rule context.getQueryP(queryName: string, Transaction(optional): string): promise<KloQuery> For HTML Apps in UI kloQuery.getQueryP(queryName: string, Transaction: string): promise<KloQuery> To get the query instance of given query name, call getQueryP method. In UI Controller Normally use getQueryP without passing the Transaction name as parameter. By default all queries are added into the base transaction of the controller. Base transaction name is mentioned in the controller definition. UI Controller: If you want to explicitly separate out the transaction boundary then mention the transaction name in getQuerP(queryName, myTransaction). In case if the Base controller name and myTransaction name are the same it will be considered as base transaction. Rule: Separate Transaction is not allowed in Rule, only base transaction allowed. HTML: Transaction name is mandatory in getQueryP(queryName, myTransaction) KloQuery extends EntityManager. Examples: In Controller: oController.getQueryP("d_logistics").then((oQueryInstance)=> { // }); }); OR //Get transaction by name and add. oController.getQueryP(‘d_logistics’, ‘myTransaction’) In Rule: context.getQueryP(‘d_logistics’) In HTML: kloQuery.getQueryP(‘d_logistics’, ‘myTransaction’) clone(): KloQuery convertTo() clone() duplicates the query instance. This returns the new query object instance without result set. All parameters which are set to original query will remain as is in the object and can be changed before executing the clone of query. If you need multiple objects of query, call clone method multiple times. Example: q.clone**()** @parameter : @Return : KloQuery getEntitySet(): KloEntitySet getEntitySet returns the instance of query’s return Entity type(kloEntitySet). Entity set will be empty if executeP is not invoked yet. This will return the full result set after query execution. Refer to the KloEntitySet section for more details. Example: queryInstance.getEntitySet**()** @parameter : @Return : KloEntitySet help(): To see the list of property on console use the query instance and call the “help()” method. This will print all the available properties. Example: queryInstance.help**()**

kloQuery supports multiple types of query modeling which are easy to define and use in the application. Based on application scenario and use case query type has to be decided. Runtime Query ( single and multiple entities) Meta Query - Dynamic Native Query - Advance query plain SQL Saved Query User Saved Query Initial Sync Query Delta Query

Entity itself can be used as query without any modeling. Use entity name as Query name. Fetch data from a single entity(table) or multiple entities of the same BO. All properties of the entity can be added as “where” conditions using setProperty(). Available methods are listed below: setProperty(fieldName: string, value: any): IKloQuery @parameter : fieldName - is name of query property @parameter: value - is the value of the property .id = value; q.’tableName#fieldName’ = value (#,@,.) q[tableName.fieldName] = value Query property defines the value of where clause these properties are used as parameter in prepared statement. Formation of WHERE clause controlled by query modeling. While setting the property in a given query you must know the exact name of the property. To see the list of property on console use the query instance and call the “help()” method. This will print all the available properties. Provided value must be of type as defined in query properties's property type. For date it can accept a well formatted string representing the date. It also supports relative dates like “today +3D”. In case if the table name is not passed it will take the return entity name by default. All parameters passed here are case insensitive. Example: E.g. Query which needs to fetch all the order of customer “cust1” and query takes the customer ID as input, use the setProperty. q.setProperty(‘d_order#customer_id’, ‘cust1’); // Pass field name with table name ‘tableName#fieldName’ Or q.[d_order#customer_id] = ‘cust1’; Deprecated: setLoadAll(bValue: boolean): use setPageSize(0) Deprecated : setTop(): use setPageSize(n) setPageSize(pageSize: int) @parameter : pageSize - This operation can perform significantly better for loading large numbers of entities. Defines the pagination behavior for query execution. Query originated inside kloRule ignores this and always loads full results at once. Query originated in kloTouch usages the default value 10 as page size. Use Value 0(ZERO) for pagesize to load all the records at once. All other positive values(1 to n) indicate the page size. To return the single record use setPageSize(1). Please note query.executeP always return entity set with the length representing the number of records qualified by query independent of specified pagesize. And all the entities of entityset are accessible even if not loaded and records are fetched per page only once is accessed by the context or code. If pagination is set before rule will be called along with execute but after execute rules will be called only on the page not for all the result. If UI or controller try to read the entity not loaded because of pagination page fault will occur now page ( set of rows) belonging to page will load after execute rule will be fired and ui update event will trigger. Example: queryInstance.setPageSize(20); setOrderBy([{fieldname: string, sort_type?: string}]): IKloQuery @parameter : fieldname - return entity field(property name) @parameter : sort_type - possible values are ‘ASC’ or ‘DESC’ @Return : IKloQuery The OrderBy is used to sort the query result-set in ascending or descending order of given field(entity property name). Sorting can be on one or multiple fields. Like you can sort on Name and Age both with Name as Ascending and Age as Descending order. By default it sorts in ascending order. To sort the records in descending order, use the DESC keyword. Sorting Sequence is the same as parameters passed. Separate field required in metadata. Table name in fieldname Keywords: Ascending Order: ‘aes’ Descending Order: ‘desc’ Example: queryInstance.setOrderBy([{field:'sales_order_id', order_type:'asc'}]) queryInstance.setOrderBy([{field:'sales_order_id',order_type:'desc'}]) Multiple fields sorting: q.setOrderBy([{field:'sales_order_id', order_type:'desc'}, {field:'order_date', order_type:'desc'} ]), setSelectClause([property1,property2,property3]): boolean LoadPartEntity([property1,property2,property3]): boolean @parameter : table field name. @Return : boolean With partial list of return entity fields makes the query selective select query. By default query execute returns all fields of return entity. This can be added in metadata or using API. LoadPartEntity: Pass one or multiple property names. Select metamodel: add list of selective fields in metadata using BOL editor. Can add more fields using setSelectClause(...). Please note meta model Select is different from Selective select as behavior. - has to capture in metadata. When application accesses the entity’s properties not part of list or entity is getting modified, kloQuery will internally fetch the missing column for accessed entity with the “select * where the primary key” query and make the entity complete. Example: queryInstance.setSelectClause([‘order_id’, ‘customer_id’, ‘order_date’]) Load Full detail of object in detail page or lead selection. -New API required. Page fault for selective select. Example: queryInstance. Expand All Example: queryInstance. setNetWorkMode(networkMode: value): IKloQuery @parameter : networkMode - Application code can set the network mode explicitly to override the network mode for query instance at runtime using setnetworkMode. It is required in exceptional situations only. Best practice is to define it by meta model. Network mode is determined in the following precedence order. • Set Network Mode(highest) Network mode in query definition (if specified) network mode in entity definition (if specified) Network mode of parent query. Applicable only for relation. Network mode in flavor (Mandatory field) (lowest) Network mode defines the process flow for query. Same query can be called ONLINE as well as OFFLINE. Possible values: • ONLINE - call the server. OFFLINE - call to local App/Browser DB. SAP_ONLINE CACHED_ONLINE Online: • On client before Query events are executed. On server before Query events are executed Data is fetched on server On server after Query events are executed On client after Query events are executed. Result is returned to the caller. Offline: • On client before Query events are executed. Data is fetched from local db on the client On client after Query events are executed. Result is returned to the caller. SAP Online: • On client before Query events are executed. SAP server is asked for data to be returned. On client after Query events are executed. Result is returned to the caller. CACHED_ONLINE: New Name to be decided. • On client before Query events are executed. Data is fetched from local db on the client On client after Query events are executed. Result is returned to the caller. On server before Query events are executed Data is fetched on server On server after Query events are executed Result is merged in entityset. Caller is informed about change in data. CONFIRMED_OFFLINE: Example: queryInstance.setNetWorkMode(“ONLINE”); Reset and Clear All query instance? reset(): kloQuery This will clear all the query parameters and set the query instance to the initial stage(fresh instance). This will not clear the result set of query. In case you want to clear the result set, execute the query. Network mode can’t be changed once query is executed. Example: queryInstance.reset() Deprecated: execute(fnSuccess?:Function,fnError?:Function): use executeP() Deprecated: refresh(): call executeP() again. executeP(forceExecute: boolean): promise<kloEntitySet> executeP will go for execution of query to fetch the result. The Query is prepared by setting all the required properties and parameters. ExecuteP returns promise. Once execution completes, the promise is resolved with the kloEntitySet which represents an array of entities as a result. On the same Query if executeP is called more than one time it rechecks for change only in case of difference re-execution happens. Also earlier execution if in process are rejected. Please note queryInstance.executeP always return the same instance of kloEntitySet which can directly retrieve from query property “entitySet” executeP only fills it with appropriate result. Default value of forceExecute is FALSE. Calling multiple times executeP() is not allowed. Use force execute parameter to execute without any change in query parameters. Network mode can’t be changed in subsequent execute calls. • If any property is set “null” it will get ignored at the time of query execution. Example: q.executeP(function(dataES){ …… //do something on the resultset. // resolve promise }) Deprecated: getCount(fnSuccess?: Function, fnError?: Function): Promise<void>: use getCountP() getCountP(forceExecute: boolean): Promise<number> getCountP will execute the query to fetch the count of qualified records. When you only want to get the count(number of records) from Query, you can use this api. getCountP returns promise. Once execution completes, the promise is resolved with the number which represents count as a result. What if called after executeP? : Can call and will return the same value of executeP return. Bindable property is required to bind it for static reports / home page etc. Example: queryInstance.getCountP().then(function(number){ //do something with }).catch(function(error){ //handle error }) @parameter : @Return : Promise applySavedQueryValues(savedQueryID) This applies the parameters of saved query to current query instance. • Overwrite all parameter values with saved query values and then more parameters can be added. If any property is set “null” it will get ignored at the time of query execution. User saved the query only. Is this functionality useful? - behaviour should be the same as Saved Query. Example: queryInstance.applySavedQueryValues(‘d_order’); archiveP(): promise<bool> archiveP will go for deleting all the entity qualifies with the query result on the client side from the local data store. It does not do anything on the server. The Query is prepared by setting all the required properties and parameters. ArchiveP returns promise. Once execution completes, the promise is resolved/rejected. Query archive does not work in a cascaded way. Hence only qualified entities are deleted. Child entities of BO or aggagated entities are not touched and they can become orphon. For cascade archive please call archive on entity. This call has high throughput. Example: Await q.archiveP()

Adding operators to query properties while setting through API (on Query instance ) or with bindings. Supported operators are: AND, OR, EQUAL, NOT EQUAL, GREATER, LESSER, GREATER_EQUAL, LESSER_EQL, LIKE, NOT, IS NULL, IS NOT NULL, IN, NOT IN Syntax: <query instance>[‘QueryProperty<_><operator>’] = value Example: q[‘item_number_GT’] = 20 q[‘item_number_LT’] = 50 This will filter the results having item numbers between 20 and 50.

This is part of Runtime query with a special case where you want to fetch the data from multiple tables within a BO boundary. Use entity name as Query name. Based on the setProperties parameters it decides either to query on single entity or multiple entities. All parameters in setProperty should have a table name also if property belongs to other than return entity. If the table name is not mentioned, it will consider the return entity name. All entities should be part of one BO. If all entities are not part of the same BO, it will throw an error at runtime. getQueryP(entityName: "d_order") @parameter: entityName: entity name(case sensitive) @Returns**:** Query Instance (KloQuery) It is not necessary to use root entity only as query ID. Any entity(within BO) can be used and joins could be on parent or child entity. Example: d_order d_order_item d_order_conditions Can use d_order_item as return entity and user d_order entity’s property in setProperty function. Here JOIN will be added for d_order in the constructed query. Features supported: Fetch data from multiple tables in single BO. Joins are decided as the entity properties used in seProperty. All parameters are optional. If the participating/join table parameter is not passed, JOIN will not be applied. Not supported: Filter expression Group By Distinct SUM/COUNT/AVG OR SELECT( function, alias) Examples: Let’s take an example Online Order placement to understand the kloQuery functions. Refer Entity section for table definition. Table(Entity): d_order >> d_order_item. Here d_order is the main header table and d_order_item is a child table with foreign key relation as order_id. documents.t: Authorization is the process of giving someone permission to do or have something. In multi-user systems, authorization defines for the system which users are allowed access to the system and what privileges of use. Authorization can be defined on Property Type only. Authorization can’t be defined on object type or some other parameter. In case if you want to add/remove/change authorization on base property type, extend the property type in separate flavor. Define the authorization at Entity Property Type to apply on all the queries of a BO where that particular Property Type is used in Entity Property definition. Property type can be used in multiple Entities, in this case authorization will be applied on all queries of these Entities. For example, ‘user_id’ is a property type and this is used in ‘user’ column definition of multiple Entities(tables) like d_order, d_logistics, etc. Now all the queries where the return entity is ‘d_order’ or ‘d_logistics’, you will get the filtered result based on user logged in. Authorization is applied on the whole BO irrespective of return Entity. If authorization is defined on any child/root entity it will be applied on all the entities which are part of that BO. When used as string literal in meta model in authorization it is replaced with real value. E.g. ${$USER.login_id} will be replaced with currently logged in user id. Similarly authorization can be applied on other $VARAIBLES also. For more details refer $VARIABLE section. $Variable is available in Rule and Endpoint resolver but not available while processing middleware messages. Syntax: ${$<Variable name>.<property id>} Rule Execution: Authorization is applied when query runs inside BO Rule on server side. In case of client side Rule execution authorization is not applied as client DB should have only filtered data. If any client(endpoint) is not authorized to see the data it should not get synced to the client. Which means authorization is applied at the time of initial sync and data(message) push to client. Inherit Authorization: Authorization of parent object added automatically to the child. This means if authorization is applied based on customer_id property type on order Entity, the same will be applied on the child entities(upto n level) also. Authorization is applied in Read and Create operations. As it is applied on Read operation, Delete operation is covered under this. User can’t delete the data which is not allowed to read. Authorization is not applied while querying data in middleware message processing as the system does not know the User. Authorization is not applied to scheduled jobs as the user configured in Job is common. APIs to be provided to get the $variable values in non-odata call. Authorization has to be applied on Upload data. How to skip authorization in one particular scenario? Can be useful in debugging in development system.

Data archiving is the process of moving data that is no longer actively used to a separate storage device for long-term retention. Archive data consists of older data that remains important to the organization or must be retained for future reference or regulatory compliance reasons. Enable Archiving: Separate tables will get created if archiving is enabled on particular entity/BO. Table name starts with ‘v’ instead of ‘d’. Archive Data: Frequence of data archiving is decided based on the business requirement. Developer has to write a background report to push the data from the main transaction table to the archive table. Fetch Archived Data: take input from user to show the archived data. On Entity level or BO level? Role wise archive data authorization? Acquiring the Entity by Entity Unique ID: Entity Unique ID is a concatenated value of Entity name and primary key set in an alphabetic sorted Order.. <entity_name>##<pk1>##<pk2>......... Deprecated: Query Manager Deprecated use(...) instead. In UI Controller Normally use getQueryP without passing the Transaction name as parameter. By default all queries are added into the base transaction of controller. Base transaction name is mentioned in the controller definition. UI Controller: If you want to explicitly separate out the transaction boundary then mention the transaction name in getQuerP(queryName, myTransaction). In case if Base controller name and myTransaction name are same it will be considered as base transaction. Rule: Separate Transaction is not allowed in Rule, only base transaction allowed. HTML: Transaction name is mandatory in getQueryP(queryName, myTransaction) KloQuery extends EntityManager. Examples: In Controller: oController.getQueryP("d_logistics").then((oQueryInstance)=> { // }); }); OR //Get transaction by name and add. oController.getQueryP(‘d_logistics’, ‘myTransaction’) In Rule: context.getQueryP(‘d_logistics’) In HTML: kloQuery.getQueryP(‘d_logistics’, ‘myTransaction’) APIs: Get unique ID(getUniqueID(primaryKey: String)): This returns a unique ID with Entity name and primary key set. Unique ID is constructed with d_order_item##<order_id>##<item_id> Load entity by ID(getEntityByID(uniqueID: String)): This returns the full entity of given unique ID. Till now you have gone through the Runtime query where modeling is not required. Let’s model a Query using Procify Data Studio. To create a query go to the entity which will be returned as a result. Provide a unique Query name. Query names should start with q as best practice. It must not start with “d, c, a or m”. Query name and entity name must not be the same hence name used as entity id or query id can not be used for others. Select Query Type as “D” or “Modeled Query” Define Query property Define Query Relation: Test Query Query definition is broadly categorized into two sections one as “SQL Section” relevant input as definition to prepare SQL statement and other defines the behavioral expects. Section to define SQL needs to know participating database tables join rules, where clause, return columns, groupby etc. second section concentrate on business aspect like before query rule, after query rule, network mode, property mapping, part return, authorization, etc.

Select: SQLfunction (tablename.fieldname) AS alias Can be blank, default value is taken as returnEntityName if table/entity name is not specified with any field.* If column name in the return result set is not matching with return entity property name value will not be populated hence use Alias to rename it as return entity property name. In case of multiple tables, specify the select list with table name and alias so results can be mapped with return entity property name. Return entity or entity property can be transient or persisted. Supported db function can also be applied on the field [{Function:””,Entity:”d_ord”,Property:”r_qty”,Alias:”” },{Function:””,Entity:”d_ord”,Property:”gross”,Alias:”” }..]. Alias is to match the property name with transient entity property. PartEntityLoad: to be added in metadata. Read selective fields of return entity. By default full return entity is returned as result set. Add one or multiple fields here for selective return. In case the entity is changed, the framework will load full entity internally with primary key set. Is primary key fields added by default with selective fields? Distinct: True / False/ IF child JOIN as value. If true distinct all(select clause parameters) is considered for return row. Default value is false. FROM: Can be blank, default value is taken as returnEntityName. In case of transient entity or even in case of persistent entity specifically in case of aggregates calculation we may need to specify different from entity than return entity. Use Native query if you want to use multiple table names in FROM section like in case of parent child relation in the same table. JOIN: Provide a unique Query Relation ID and define the relation using Entity relation with Join type. Entity relation has the full details of both side fields to define the Join. JOIN Type Entity Alias Name Entity Property Name Supported Join Types: Inner Join Full Outer Join Left Join Right Join Default value for Join Type is “Inner Join”. Join will be avoided if the parameter is not passed or not part of select or Authorization or traveling path for other table fields. Where: supported filter expression Add Query property with the Entity you want to put a where condition. Following parameters as input: Query Property ID Entity Name Entity Property ID Operator : excluding formula all other operators are supported. GroupBy / Having: Having support filter expression OrderBy: [{fieldname: string, sort_type?: string}] setOrderBy([{fieldname: string, sort_type?: string}]): IKloQuery @parameter : fieldname - return entity field(property name) @parameter : sort_type - possible values are ‘ASC’ or ‘DESC’ Supported Operator AND, OR, EQUAL, NOT EQUAL, GREATER, LESSER, GREATER_EQUAL, LESSER_EQL, LIKE, NOT, IS NULL, IS NOT NULL, IN, NOT IN Supported Functions: COUNT, SUM, MIN, MAX, AVG. Syntax: Supported Variables: Query property name Syntax- :<query_property_name> Constant: Syntax - “”. Provide constant value in double quotes. $ variable if not a MW message. Syntax - ${$USER.owning_bp} Parent/participating/Join Tables Property. Syntax- :<tableName.fieldName> Example: SELECT * from d_order where customer_id = :cust_id and order_type = :”prime” order by order_date desc; SELECT * from d_order Inner join d_order_item on (d_order.order_id = d_order_item.order_id) where customer_id = :cust_id and order_type = :”prime” order by order_date desc; Filter Expression: - to be discussed. Filter expression is binary tree of operator, table.fields, function, variable, entity property and const. Tree can be evaluated only as a one way to construct the filter expression. Tree nodes can have an operator with left and/or right values. Value can be another node itself. Boqlquery: Holds the SQL like string for better understanding of what will go to DB
Nested queries are not supported. Formula not supported (like a*b) Limit not supported

Return Entity Name: Result set will be kloEntitySet containing the instances of named return Entity. Return entity could be Persistent or Transient. In case if Persistent entity is not fitting in as a return data set, you can create a Transient entity which has all the required entity properties as per business requirement and use this entity as return entity. Visit Entity section for more details on definition of Transient entity. This is the use case you need: Return the data from different entities. Additional fields to store some calculated value at runtime. Is_across_tenant: If query needs to be extended across tenant data. Be careful for security. By default queries are tenant specific. This will return the data of all the tenants within a landscape. Network mode: Normally left null or “” or “Default” so it is picked as per precedence. Specify only in specific flavor as per override rules. Return entity mapping Pagination behavior: Pagination is applied only if query is executed from UI. In case if query is executed from any rule(Entity or Query) it will load all qualified data. Features supported: Fetch data from multiple entities(tables) across BO. Join with another entity(table) supported with relation. All query properties are optional. Most used SQL functions and operators are supported.

Till now you have gone through Runtime and Modeled Query. Native query is a row SQL query which supports all operators and functions of SQL as part of query statement(not part of metadata). This should be used only as a last option if nothing fits. This type of query must not be used in a product or reusable module. Native query is highly flexible but non migratable. Let’s write a SQL Query using Procify Data Studio. To create a query go to the entity which will be returned as a result. Provide a unique Query name. Query names should start with q as best practice. It must not start with “d, c, a or m”. Query name and entity name must not be the same hence name used as entity id or query id can not be used for others. Select Query Type as “Z” or “Native Query”. Write SQL statement Define Query property Test Query Native query working in online case may not work in offline network mode if query is incompatible with webSQL. It is comparatively slow because to db it is submitted as a nested query. Use only if requirement is not fulfilling with Runtime or Modeled queries. Authorization will be applied the same as other query types. Example: SELECT * from d_order where customer_id = :cust_id and order_type = :”prime” order by order_date desc; Here cust_id is the query property you have to define. All query property values are mandatory to pass at the time of execution. Not supported: Query Relation: use Join in SQL statement. Archiving Date dependent features Part select of return entity fields?

You can subscribe the Rule to a query which is executed before or after query execution. Rule subscription is part of kloIDE. To subscribe to the Rules you need to provide the details below. Rule ID: Event Type: Before Query (BEFORE_QUERY) After Query(AFTER_QUERY) Channel Type: All, D2K- Client, D2K- Server, K2K, E2K, Sequence No: In case multiple Rules subscribed on one query, it will execute in a given sequence here. All positive numbers(1-n) excepted. Rules can not be executed on Runtime Queries. For more details on Rule execution refer to the Rule section. Skip rule execution: execution can’t be skipped. put a condition within Rule code. Entity also had query rule? Metadata help or real? Rules can be subscribed on query to write the business logic. Query Rules are mainly used where some calculation required on before executing the query or query resultset to show the manipulated data on UI. Result sets can be modified, add or remove records in AFTER_QUERY rule. Rule Execution: Please note before execution is called only once after execution in case of Pagination, selective select or expand all cases also. Subsequent internal calls do not call before_execute. After execution may not get the correct count of records or all records or all fields. Please ensure you have considered selective select case, pagination case and expand all cases. After_Query will be executed after every internal call all the data manipulation will be accepted as is to form the return entity.

As you have gone through all query types explained above with all features supported in different types of queries. Based on the features supported programmer can decide which type will fit in what scenario. While selection of type of query, you give priority in below sequence(1 is highest priority): Runtime Query Modeled Query Native Query Below are few frequent use cases and query type usage: Advance Search screen: use Modeled query. F4: use Runtime query Initial Sync: use Modeled query. Report: use dynamic query normally as input parameters are dynamic in most of the reports. List Screen: Details screen: Normally Runtime Query with Entity by ID Measure performance Example: loadLogisticsOnline: function (oController, order_id, TXN) { return new Promise(function (resolve, reject) { var logistics = oController.getModel().getProperty('/detail'); oController.getQuery('d_logistics').then(function (orderQI) { orderQI.d_order#order_id = order_id; orderQI.setNetWorkMode('ONLINE'); TXN.add(orderQI); orderQI.execute(function (orderES) { orderES[0].s_action = 'DEL_RELEASE'; orderES[0].s_status = 'RELEASED'; resolve(orderES); }); }); }); } Operators Runtime Modeled Native WHERE Y Y Y AND Y Y Y OR Y Y NOT Y DISTINCT Y Y Y JOINS (inner, left, right, full, self) Y Y ORDER BY Y Y Y GROUP BY Y Y Y LIKE Y Y Y IN Y Y Y BETWEEN Y Y HAVING Y Y TOP Y Y COUNT Y Y MIN/MAX Y Y AVG/SUM Y Y IS NULL Y Y

documents.t: kloQuery is a parameterized query which takes the properties’ value at runtime. We may need these property values to be persisted and execute the query with the persisted value without asking application users to provide the value. Saved Query is a Query container that holds the predefined properties’ value for a given query. Saved Query is identified by ID hence … It is also used in the Initial Sync. Saved query can use dollar variables and date literals as property values. Saved query can hold all the variable values which can be set at runtime by API. User saved query? Single user? Multi User? Designation based? Flavor based? Object type based? Brand based?

Delta Query is used to update the local db on a periodic basis from the server. It asks the server to provide the data modified from the last execution till now. Results are handed over to the executor. Delta queries are internally used by cached online and by value help.

Dialogs opened via the KloController.openDialog API should be closed using the KloController.closeDialog API, not the sap.m.Dialog's close method. The sap.m.Dialog's close method should only be used when the dialog was opened via the sap.m.Dialog.open() method.

It has been noted that some applications are using the sap.m.Dialog's close method to close dialogs that were opened via the KloController.openDialog API. This can result in inconsistencies and potential issues. To maintain uniformity and prevent problems, it is essential that the KloController.closeDialog API is used to close dialogs opened by the KloController.openDialog API. This document provides guidance on how to correct this issue and ensure that your code follows the correct API usage patterns.

After correcting the code, please perform the following tests to ensure the dialog functions as expected: Open a dialog using KloController.openDialog. Close the dialog using KloController.closeDialog. Ensure that no errors or unexpected behaviors occur.

IMPORTANT: Transnode Binding Requirements For Excel download functionality to work correctly, the following binding requirements MUST be followed: The section with Excel download must be bound to an EntitySet transnode All controls within the section MUST be bound to properties of the same EntitySet transnode Controls MUST NOT be bound to properties of a different transnode using dsrc (data source) binding Correct Implementation Example ✓ Correct Binding ✗ Incorrect Binding Section: Bound to 'CampaignContacts' (EntitySet)Column 1: ContactName → CampaignContacts.ContactNameColumn 2: Email → CampaignContacts.EmailColumn 3: Status → CampaignContacts.StatusResult: Excel download works correctly Section: Bound to 'CampaignContacts' (EntitySet)Column 1: ContactName → CampaignContacts.ContactNameColumn 2: Email → ContactDetails.Email (dsrc binding)Column 3: Status → CampaignContacts.StatusResult: Excel download FAILS

This event will be triggered when the excel data has been converted to raw JSON data. The application developer can access this raw data and perform modifications based on their needs. The modified data (or lack thereof) will then be sent to the server for further validation and creation/modification of entities.
NAME TYPE DESCRIPTION rawData Object Raw excel data in JSON Format errors Object Errors (if any) can be passed that will then be displayed in the error log.

NOTE: This is a synchronous event. It does not support asynchronous await calls inside the function. If await is used, the event will continue with its execution without waiting for the results of the async function. If data is modified after the await call, modified data will not be sent to the server for processing. If errors are attached after the await call, attached errors will not reflect in the error log. Incorrect Usage Example: In the above example, due to the await call to an asynchronous function, the data will be sent to the server for processing before modifying the data.

The Menu Editor table includes a search field above the menu tree to help locate a specific Menu ID or Menu Text quickly. How search works: The search matches against both Menu ID and Menu Text, and applies partial/fuzzy matching — you don't need to type the exact full value. If your search term matches a parent menu item only, the filtered tree shows just that parent row (its children are not pulled into the result unless they also match). If your search term matches a child menu item, the filtered tree shows that child along with its parent, so you always retain context of where the item sits in the hierarchy. Note on the child-count indicator: The number shown next to a parent menu item always reflects the total number of children that parent actually has in the full menu tree — not just the ones currently visible in your search results. This count does not change based on your search filter. For example, searching for a parent's name may show a count of 3 even though none of those 3 children match your search text and are therefore not shown below it. Tip: To view all children of a parent, clear the search field (or expand the node directly) rather than relying on the search result or the count next to it.

Middleware (Message Monitoring) is an application that is used for fetching all the information about the entries that are present in the device Info or tenant Info. We can also reprocess the failed messages present inside the error_q of the tenant. Device Info: When we are sending any data/action from server to device we store the message in the device info to know its information and state. In device info, every message is an outgoing message. So, the successfully sent messages are shown here. So, It goes from In queue to success. Tenant Info: When we are sending/fetching any data/action from server to SAP LOCAL or sending data from device to server. We store the message in tenant info to know its information and state. All the messages from Device to Server and SAP Local to server are visible in Inbound MessagesServer Queue Monitor screen. All the messages from Server to SAP Local will be visible to the Outbound queue screen and all the messages from server to device or SAP Local to device will be visible in Device OutboundDevice Queue Monitor screen. Purpose of Message Monitoring​ Message Monitoring is used to show information about messages (UPGRADE, DEBOARD) and the state of the message whether it's in the in-queue, Success, or failed. Every message has a state out of the three states mentioned below : In-Queue: The message is ready for processing. Success: The message has been processed successfully. Failed: Message processing has failed. We can also reprocess the Failed message. The reprocess function is only available for tenant_q. When we are sending/fetching any data/Action from server to device or server to SAP local, we store it in terms of messages to know its information and its state. Navigate to Message Monitoring​

documents.t: An Upsert operation refers to the combination of update and insert actions, where data is either updated if it exists or inserted if it doesn't. When syncing messages, an Upsert scenario behavior typically involves checking if a message already exists in the destination system or database. If it exists, the system will update it; if it doesn't, the system will insert it as a new record. 1.5.1.Upsert Behavior in Middleware for Syncing Messages:​ Data Creation and Update: If the data is new (does not exist in the system), a new entry will be created. If the data already exists, the existing record will be updated instead of creating a new one. Upsert for Root Business Objects (BOs) and Primary Relations: Upsert is only applicable for Root Business Objects (BOs) and their primary relations. For non-primary relations, the Upsert operation will work only if the relation is established using primary keys. Parent-Child Relationship: If a parent is new, but the child data related to the parent already exists, this is considered an unexpected scenario. The user must handle this manually, as it is not automatically managed by the middleware. 1.5.2.Delete Scenario Behavior:​ Parent Entity Deletion: If the parent entity is deleted, the child entities will only be deleted if the user explicitly sends the isdeleted flag as true in the request body for both the parent and child entities. This applies to both primary and aggregate relationships. Child Entity Deletion: If the child entity is deleted, only the child will be deleted. The parent entity will remain intact.

Messages that are failed to process can be found in the error q. The error can be found in the error message. Possible reasons a message can fail are. Application logic - When an application logically rejects a request for processing the message. I.e. Adding items to a closed order. Adding shipments to a closed Delivery etc. Suggested solution : Find the root cause why these messages are generated. Eg. screen still allows adding items even if the status of order is closed. And fix the issue / add validation in the client side also. Application bugs - Some cases where application code has a bug, due to which an exception can be raised the message will fail. Eg. Improper null handling, wrong API parameters, typo etc. Transaction User not configured - File processing, transaction user has to be configured with required application & permissions. As all the messages are processed based on the access of the user, messages generated by files need a user to validate against. Refer to the Landscape Editor for how to configure the transaction user. Configured user doesn’t have application assigned : When messages from SAP / File processing are failing with “Access denied: user lacks permission to the required application.” error, it means, the user (SAP communication user / File processing user) does not have that flavor assigned to them. Database Deadlock / Lock Timeout Errors: - When the middleware encounters a transient database deadlock or lock wait timeout (e.g., "Deadlock found when trying to get lock; try restarting transaction"), messages are automatically retried up to 3 times with a 1-second delay (default values) between attempts. - If all retries are exhausted, the message will move to the error queue. - It will have an error message like - "Message <msg_id> failed after 3 retry attempts due to Lock wait timeout exceeded" or "Message <msg_id> failed after 3 retry attempts due to Deadlock found". - The retry settings are configurable via config.json: "MiddlewareRetrySettings": { "DeadlockRetryCount": 3, "RetryDelaySeconds": 1 }

When an application team logs in from multiple or random devices without properly deboarding the previous devices, those devices can continue to be considered active endpoints. As a result, messages may continue to be generated for these endpoints even though the application team is no longer actively using them. Platform Reference: Account Console 7.0 - User Guide — "Whenever any new user registers in the application, a new endpoint ID is created against that account... when they log in again the status becomes Active." Each login is a distinct endpoint; none are deregistered automatically on crash or app closure.
documents.s: 2.1. Multiple Logins Can Create Active Endpoints

documents.t: Because these endpoints remain active, messages generated for them may not be synchronized with the device immediately. Over time, a large number of messages can accumulate in the queue. This can give the impression that a large number of messages are stuck. Platform Reference: Message Monitoring 7.0 - User Guide — In-Queue is defined as "all the data that are currently present in the device_q and which are not processed yet." A high In-Queue count reflects endpoints awaiting sync, not failed or lost messages.
documents.s: 2.2 Messages Can Accumulate in the Queue

documents.t: When the corresponding device comes online , the queued messages are synchronized with the device. Once the server successfully sends the messages and receives the required acknowledgment from the client, the messages move to Success. If the device is offline, the messages remain in the queue until the device becomes available. Platform Reference: Message Monitoring 7.0 - User Guide — device_q entries move to device_log_q (Success) or device_error_q (Failed) only after processing; until then they remain In-Queue, consistent with holding messages for an offline device until it reconnects.
documents.s: 2.3. Messages Are Synchronized When the Device Becomes online

documents.t: A message can reach the device successfully, but the actual processing on the device may still fail. From the server's perspective, the message can be marked as Success when the client acknowledges that the message was received while the device was online. Therefore, Success on the server does not necessarily mean that the message was successfully processed by the application on the device. Platform Reference: Message Monitoring 7.0 - User Guide — "In device info, every message is sent or is in the process of being successfully sent. So, every message is outgoing and never fails. Hence, It goes from in-queue to success." This confirms Success tracks the send/acknowledgment, not on-device application processing.

The application team may not be aware that previously used devices are still registered as active endpoints. This can result in messages continuing to be generated and queued for those endpoints. Note: This is a training/visibility gap rather than a platform defect. Recommend making Sections 1–4 of this topic available to application teams so "stuck message" reports can be self-diagnosed before being escalated as incidents.

A scheduler runs every Sunday to clean up old endpoints. Note: The scheduler currently deboards endpoints that have been inactive for more than 7 days. Once an endpoint is deboarded, its corresponding entry is removed from the endpoint table. Property Value Class name deboardInactiveUsers CRON expression 0 0 0 ? * SUN * (every Sunday at midnight) Current inactivity threshold (this environment) 7 days Platform default threshold 15 days — this environment has been configured below the default Channel type BOTH, unless restricted to DEVICE or BROWSER Table cleaned up Endpoint's entries removed from madm_ep_apps Platform Reference: Account Console 7.0 - User Guide — "Deboard Inactive Users": CRON Job Expression 0 0 0 ? * SUN *, class deboardInactiveUsers, parameters No_of_inactive_days {default: 15} and Channel_type {default: BOTH}; "this scheduler will deboard all the users who are inactive since given days and it will delete the entry of all deboarded endpoints from madm_ep_apps."

If the default 7-day cleanup period does not meet the application's requirements, the scheduler can be customized to use a different endpoint deboarding period. To change it: Go to the job-instances page in Cockpit and locate the deboardInactiveUsers job. Open the job instance's parameters. Update No_of_inactive_days to the desired threshold. Update Channel_type if the cleanup should be restricted to a specific channel. Save. The new threshold takes effect on the job's next scheduled run (the following Sunday, per the fixed CRON expression). Note: The CRON schedule itself (currently fixed to Sunday) is a separate setting from the inactivity threshold — changing how often the job runs, as opposed to how many inactive days it waits, would need to be confirmed as in-scope for this customization request.

Overview The Middleware Message Forwarding feature allows you to automatically sync data changes between different flavors of your application. When data is changed in one flavor (source), it can automatically trigger message generation for users of another flavor (target), ensuring all users stay synchronized regardless of which flavor they're using.

Multi-Flavor Setup​ ✅ You must have multiple flavors (source and target flavors) ✅ Both source and target flavors must be deployed and accessible ✅ Flavors should share common entities that require message sync Entity Design​ ✅ Target Entity: Must exist with identical entity name and table name ✅ Target Entity: Must have ENDPOINT_RESOLVER event configured with proper implementation

Administrative Access​ ✅ Access to Operations Monitor application for configuration ✅ Permissions to create/modify Middleware Message Routing entries ✅ Message monitoring access for troubleshooting and monitoring Development Environment​ ✅ Private node setup with DEV landscape (for testing) ✅ Access to both source and target flavor codebases ✅ Debugging capabilities in development environment

Message Processing Infrastructure​ ✅ Message processing must be functional Monitoring Tools​ ✅ Message Monitoring screen access for tracking forwarded messages ✅ Queue Monitor for viewing message queues and error queues ✅ Log access for troubleshooting and debugging

Development Team​ ✅ Understanding of entity event implementation (ENDPOINT_RESOLVER) ✅ Familiarity with addEndpoint() method usage ✅ Knowledge of message queue and processing ✅ Experience with multi-flavor application development Configuration Team​ ✅ Understanding of flavor versioning and deployment ✅ Knowledge of landscape management (DEV/TEST/PROD) ✅ Familiarity with Operations Monitor configuration tools

To enable message forwarding, you need to configure mappings in the Mw Message Routing Screen in Operations Monitor: Configuration Screen - Mw Message Routing Access this screen through Operations Monitor > Middleware Message Routing Required Fields​ Source Flavor: The flavor where changes originate Target Flavor: The flavor that where the changes should be also be forwarded for message generation. Is Active: Set to true to enable forwarding Target Version: Only for DEV Specify a particular version of the target flavor. Use this for debugging purposes. In QA & Production, the latest version is used. Configuration Steps​ Open Operations Monitor application Navigate to "Middleware Message Routing" Click "Add New" to create a mapping Fill in Source Flavor and Target Flavor names Set "Is Active" to true Save the configuration
