documents.t: Multi-Flavor Applications​ If your application has multiple flavors (e.g., online and offline versions) that share common entities, this feature ensures data consistency across all flavors. Example Scenarios:​ Portal + Mobile App: Changes made in the web portal should sync to mobile app users Hierarchical Applications: Parent flavor changes should sync to child flavor users How Does It Work ?​ Data Change Trigger: When you create, update, or delete data in a source flavor Automatic Detection: The system detects if forwarding is configured for that flavor in Middleware Message Routing ( Operations Monitor ) Trigger Endpoint Resolver: The ENDPOINT_RESOLVER event will be triggered in target flavor if the same entity exists. Message Generation: Messages are generated for target flavor users based on the target flavor ENDPOINT_RESOLVER logic. Synchronized Delivery: All related messages share the same reference ID for tracking

documents.t: Target Entity Setup​ Your target entity must have:​ Same entity name as source entity Same table name (tb field) as source entity ENDPOINT_RESOLVER event configured Event implementation in the entity class file Example Entity Event Implementation​ // In your entity class file (e.g., src/flavor/entity/your_entity.ts) async onEndpointResolver(txn, dataObj, headers) { // Your logic to determine which users/endpoints should receive messages this.addEndpoint(userList, EndpointType.User, ChannelType.Both); }

documents.t: When message forwarding fails, check the Error Queue for detailed information: Error queue entry showing failed forwarding message with MSG_FORWARD type Error Queue Analysis​ Message Type: Look for "MSG_FORWARD" type entries Error Details: Review error messages for troubleshooting Retry Options: Use message reprocessing to retry failed forwards

documents.t: Message Generation​ Additional Messages: You'll see target flavor messages in device/tenant queues Message Grouping: Related messages share the same reference ID Cross-Flavor Sync: Changes in source flavor should trigger messages in target flavor Error Handling​ Isolated Failures: If target flavor processing fails, source transaction still completes Error Queue Entries: Failed forwards create entries in error queue with type MSG_FORWARD Retry Capability: Failed messages forwarding can be reprocessed later. It will only retry the forwarding, not the original transaction. The dirty state and from state is preserved from the original transaction.

documents.t: What is a Reference ID?​ The reference ID (ref_msg_id) is a unique identifier that groups all messages generated from a single transaction. How It Works​ Original Message → ref_msg_id: "ABC123" ├── Source Flavor Message → ref_msg_id: "ABC123" ├── Target Flavor 1 Message → ref_msg_id: "ABC123" └── Target Flavor 2 Message → ref_msg_id: "ABC123"

documents.t: In your entity event handlers, you can detect if the event was triggered by message forwarding: async onEndpointResolver() { let headers = await this.getHeaders(); let sourceApp = headers.src_app; let currentFlavor = this.txn.$SYSTEM.flavor; if (sourceApp !== currentFlavor) { // This event was triggered by message forwarding this.info(`Message forwarded from ${sourceApp} to ${currentFlavor}`); } else { // This is a normal event execution } }

Notification callbacks let you attach files to outgoing emails. They are split into two layers: the Entity Callback (which triggers the notification) and the Notification Callback (which adds attachments). Follow the three steps below to set them up.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/Notification Developer Guide/How to Add Notification Callbacks

documents.t: Open the Notification Center, select your template, and go to the Callbacks tab. Add a row for each callback method you want to call, and set the sequence number to control the order in which attachments are added to the email. Open Notification Center and select (or create) your notification template. Go to the Callbacks tab. Click Add and enter the callback method name (e.g. attachInvoice). This name must exactly match the method you write in the notification callback file. Set the sequence number. Callbacks run in ascending sequence order — seq 1 runs first, seq 2 runs second, and so on. Click More Info on the Callbacks tab to see the list of allowed attachment file types before uploading. Save the template.
documents.s: Step 1: Register Callbacks in Notification Center
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/Notification Developer Guide/How to Add Notification Callbacks

documents.t: Create a TypeScript file in the notification folder of your app. The file name must match the template name. The class must extend KloNotification, and each method name must match what you registered in the Notification Center. File naming rule: File location: src/<App>/notification/send_notif_attach.ts Class name: same as file name (send_notif_attach) Method names: exactly match what is set in Notification Center Callbacks tab Use this.entityObject to access the entity that triggered the notification Use this.userObject to access the Object passed while sending the notification Always guard with hasAttachmentP() before calling addAttachment — skip gracefully if not found General template: // File: src/<App>/notification/send_notif_attach.ts import KloNotification from "kloBo/kloNotification/KloNotification"; export class send_notif_attach extends KloNotification { // Callback method name must match what is set in Notification Center public async attachInvoice(): Promise<void> { let txn = this.txn; let q = await txn.getQueryP('d_attach_store'); // Use entityObject to get the linked attachment ID q.setProperty('id', this.entityObject.invoice_attach_id); q.setLoadAll(true); let results = await q.executeP(); if (!results || results.length === 0) { this.warn('Attachment not found'); return; // skip gracefully, do not throw } let attach = results[0].p_file; if (!(await attach?.hasAttachmentP())) { this.warn('No file data on attachment record'); return; } await this.addAttachment(attach); this.info('Attachment added successfully'); } }
documents.s: Step 2: Create the Notification Callback File
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/Notification Developer Guide/How to Add Notification Callbacks

documents.t: In the entity file, call sendInstantNotification or addNotification inside onCreate, onUpdate, or onDelete. Pass the template name and the entity object (this). sendInstantNotification — runs in the same transaction. If it fails, the entity save rolls back. addNotification — queued asynchronously. Entity save succeeds regardless; failures logged in ma_tenant_error_q. // File: src/<App>/entity/d_order_subscription.ts export class d_order_subscription extends KloEntity { public async onCreate(): Promise<void> { // For immediate transactional email (rolls back if it fails): await this.txn.sendInstantNotification('send_notif_attach', this); // OR — for async/queued email (entity save succeeds regardless): // await this.txn.addNotification('notif_temp_2', this); } }
documents.s: Step 3: Write the Entity Callback to Trigger the Notification
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/Notification Developer Guide/How to Add Notification Callbacks

documents.t: The following is a working example based on the test case where d_order_subscription triggers sendInstantNotification with send_notif_attach. Two callbacks — attachInvoice (seq 1) and attachTerms (seq 2) — fetch files from d_attach_store and add them as attachments. Both method names must be registered in Notification Center before committing the file. What to set up in Notification Center first: Template: send_notif_attach Entity: d_order_subscription, Object Type: -1 (BOL) Callback 1: method name = attachInvoice, sequence = 1 Callback 2: method name = attachTerms, sequence = 2 Notification callback file: // File: src/<App>/notification/send_notif_attach.ts import KloNotification from "kloBo/kloNotification/KloNotification"; export class send_notif_attach extends KloNotification { // Callback 1 — registered as 'attachInvoice' at seq 1 in Notification Center public async attachInvoice(): Promise<void> { let txn = this.txn; let q = await txn.getQueryP('d_attach_store'); q.setProperty('file_name_1', 'invoice.pdf'); q.setLoadAll(true); let results = await q.executeP(); for (let i = 0; i < (results?.length || 0); i++) { let attach = (results[i] as any).p_file; if (!(await attach?.hasAttachmentP())) continue; await this.addAttachment(attach); } } // Callback 2 — registered as 'attachTerms' at seq 2 in Notification Center public async attachTerms(): Promise<void> { let txn = this.txn; let q = await txn.getQueryP('d_attach_store'); q.setProperty('file_name_1', 'terms.pdf'); q.setLoadAll(true); let results = await q.executeP(); for (let i = 0; i < (results?.length || 0); i++) { let attach = (results[i] as any).p_file; if (!(await attach?.hasAttachmentP())) continue; await this.addAttachment(attach); } } } Tip: Test locally using Private Node before committing. Add a debugger statement inside any callback method to inspect this.entityObject and this.userObject. Once validated, commit the file to public. sendInstantNotification(written in server side callback) -> triggers the notification callback if present -> in the notification callback need to do addAttachment as shown in the examples above(attachments should already be present).
documents.s: Example: Test Case Setup (d_order_subscription with send_notif_attach)

documents.t: In shared or multi-user devices, an FCM push notification may be received on a device where multiple users are registered. When a user who is not the intended recipient clicks the notification, the system now detects the mismatch and prompts them to switch accounts.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/Notification Developer Guide/How to Add Notification Callbacks

documents.t: When a notification tray is clicked, the app checks whether the currently logged-in user matches the notification's target user: If the users match → the notification opens normally. If the users don't match → a "Switch User" warning dialog is displayed, showing: The notification's intended user A prompt to switch to that account A warning if there are any unsaved changes (dirty objects) that will be lost on switching If the user transaction has no dirty object: If the user transaction has any dirty object(s): If the intended user is in the background (i.e. present at that device), then after clicking the “Switch User” button, it will redirect the user to the login page. If the intended user is NOT in the background (i.e. device clear-cache scenario), then after clicking the “Switch User” button, it will redirect the user to the registration page.

documents.t: When the intended user logs back into the device, they can review all notifications that were received while they were inactive. These missed notifications are available in the Notification Centre, accessible via the bell icon (🔔) at the top of the screen. This ensures no notifications are lost, even if they were received when a different user was active on the device. NOTE: After clearing the application data, the entries will be removed from the Notification Centre.

documents.t: Date of Issue: February 2024 Training Version Number: 7.0 Target Audience: Developers, Clients.

Notification is an alert message like SMS, email and notification in an app. Notification can be sent whenever it is required. This will work similarly to an endpoint resolver (it can send notifications to multiple receivers). The notifications sharing service is done by a third-party service (fcm) provider to clients. However, the data storage, the notification body, and the channel types are all configured by us. The types of notifications we deal with are as follows: Email notification SMS notification Application Notifications or Push Notification (fcm) To Send a notification, the Notification template should be created first, Refer to this Notification Modeler document to know more about modeling the notification template. Note on In-App/Push Notification Delivery: In-app and push notifications are delivered only to users who have an active login session (i.e., a registered/active endpoint) at the time the notification is triggered. If a user is not logged in when a notification is generated, they will not receive it retroactively upon a later login — the notification is not queued or replayed for that user. This is intentional platform behavior, approved by both Framework and Application teams. Developers should account for this when designing workflows where a notification's relevance persists beyond a single session (e.g., by using entity-based flags/screens instead of relying solely on the notification queue for critical information the user must eventually see).

addNotification is a transaction/eventContext API which can be used to trigger notifications to the users. This can be used to trigger SMS, EMAIL and push notifications for a given set of users with a specific template. addNotification should only be called on the server environment. This API will trigger a notification, it will add a notification to the queue, and it will be picked and processed based on the queue. So, use addNotification for triggering notifications which are not immediately required. Eg. the Status update, Report generated notification,... Do not use for: Triggering time critical notification which has to be sent immediately. Notification triggered with this API will be added to the queue and will be processed later based on queue/service availability. To trigger the notification immediately, use sendInstantNotification. Note: After calling addNotification(), you need to call commitP() with the same transaction to ensure the notification is committed and the email is triggered. addNotification(template, entObject?, userObject?, to_list?, cc_list?) Template​ Notification template ID should be provided for the template. A notification template can be created using Notification Modeler. To know more about how the user object & the template are being mapped refer to this section. entObject​ An object is an entity object from which data can be used to replace the template variables. userObject​ UserObject can be used to provide custom properties to the template which are not provided by the object. The same properties from entObject will be overridden by the userObject. to_list​ to_list is an array of strings (user_id / mobile number/email id) to which the notification has to be sent. If none is provided the current env user will be taken. Email, mobile, and Endpoints of the user will be used from the user details with user_id. If email is disabled or the template is not present, all email IDs in the list will be ignored. If SMS is disabled or the template is not present, all mobile numbers in the list will be ignored. mobile number/email address / Push notification endpoint is pulled from the user ID. If the App is enabled, all the endpoints will get the push notification. cc_list​ cc_list is only used for email. Example: public async onCreateInvitation(event: EventContext){ this.txn.addNotification('invitation_template', null,{user_name:this.first_name+" "+this.last_name},[this.user_id]) }

sendInstantNotification is an EventContext API which can be used to send notifications immediately. This can be used to send SMS, EMAIL and push notifications for a given set of users with a template. sendInstantNotification should only be called on the server environment(server-side callBack). This API will send a notification immediately. So, use sendInstantNotification for triggering notifications which are immediately required. Eg. OTP, Task Assignment,... Do not use: For triggering regular (non-urgent) notifications. For adding the notification to the queue to be sent, use addNotification For tracking regular changes or logging. This is an expensive functionality. API:

Template​ Notification template ID should be provided for the template. A notification template can be created using {elink Notification Modeler documentation}. entObject​ An object is an entity object from which data can be used to replace the template variables. userObject​ UserObject can be used to provide custom properties to the template which are not provided by the object. The same properties from entObject will be overridden by the userObject. to_list​ to_list is an array of strings (user_id / mobile number/email id) to which the notification has to be sent. If none is provided the current env user will be taken. Email, mobile, and Endpoints of the user will be used from the user details with user_id. If the email is disabled or the template is not present, all email IDs in the list will be ignored. If SMS is disabled or the template is not present, all mobile numbers in the list will be ignored. Mobile number/email address / Push notification endpoint is pulled from the user ID. If the App is enabled, all the endpoints will get the push notification. cc_list​ cc_list is only used for email. public async onCreateInvitation(event:EventContext){ this.txn.sendInstantNotification("reportComplete", null, {reportid: "Age Report"}, ["user101", "user104"], ["user002"]); }

documents.t: The cordova.plugins.notification.local.schedule function in Apache Cordova is part of the Local Notifications Plugin. This plugin allows you to schedule local notifications to be triggered at a specified time or after a certain delay.

Before using cordova.plugins.notification.local.schedule, you need to install the plugin: Install the local notifications plugin by running the following command in your Cordova project directory: “cordova plugin add cordova-plugin-local-notifications” Once the plugin is installed, you can use cordova.plugins.notification.local.schedule to schedule a local notification. Example: cordova.plugins.notification.local.schedule({ title: 'Attention!', text: 'have you submitted your Timesheet?', attachments: [https://myapps.procifynow.com/p6/MyAppsPRC/index.html\], actions: [ { id: 'yes', title: 'Yes' }, { id: 'no', title: 'No' } ] });
documents.s: Setting Up the Local Notifications Plugin

documents.t: The Cordova Local Notifications Plugin supports two types of Actions: Button actions Input actions Button Action: Displays buttons within the notification, and the user can tap on them to trigger specific actions (e.g., "Reply," "Snooze"). Example: Adding a Button Action cordova.plugins.notification.local.schedule({ id: 1, title: 'New Notification', text: 'You have a new message.', actions: [ { id: 'reply', title: 'Reply' // Button label }, { id: 'snooze', title: 'Snooze' // Another button label } ], trigger: { at: new Date(new Date().getTime() + 5000) } // Notification triggers in 5 seconds }); Input Action: Displays an input field where the user can type a response directly in the notification, and upon submission, the input text is processed. Example: Adding an Input Action cordova.plugins.notification.local.schedule({ id: 2, title: 'Input Required', text: 'Please enter your message below:', actions: [ { id: 'input', title: 'Submit', // Button label for submission input: true // Indicate that this action is an input action } ], trigger: { at: new Date(new Date().getTime() + 5000) } // Notification triggers in 5 seconds });

To schedule a notification using the addNotification API, follow these steps: Create the Notification Template: The notification template is created through the Notification Modeler and usually contains details such as the title, body text, and any dynamic content like variables (e.g., {{user_name}}, {{event_name}}). Use the templateId to schedule the notification: Once the template is created, it gets a unique identifier (templateId). You will use this templateId when calling the API to schedule the notification. Make an API Call to schedule the notification: Call the addNotification API: This API allows you to schedule a notification for a future time. You’ll need to specify parameters such as the message content, cc_list, to_list. For recurring message notifications, We first create a job in the job definition screen (job scheduler) and define the cron expression to specify the required time for sending the notification. Next, we create a <class_name>.ts file inside the scheduler folder, where we implement the onExecute() method as outlined in the attached document.(Job scheduler) Within the onExecute() method, we call the addNotification API to send the notification. The cron expression determines the schedule for triggering the job at the specified intervals. Once the job is added to the scheduler, it will execute automatically at the defined times. In the scheduler, onExecute method, call addNotificationAPI with the template ID, objects, and the list of users / emails ID to whom the notification should be sent.
documents.s: How to create a scheduled notification;

documents.t: The Callbacks tab is available within a notification template in the Notification Editor. It allows you to register server-side callback methods that run when the notification is being processed, enabling you to attach files dynamically to outgoing emails. Each callback method is defined by a name and a sequence number that controls the order in which it is executed. Callbacks tab inside a notification template in Notification Editor What you can do in the Callbacks Tab View all registered callback methods for the template, listed in the execution sequence. Add a new callback by entering a method name. This name must match the method implemented in the notification callback file. Delete an existing callback by selecting it and clicking Delete. Reorder callbacks by dragging and dropping rows in edit mode. The sequence number determines the order in which methods run and the order attachments are added to the email. Click the More Info button to see the list of allowed attachment file types. Only files with allowed extensions will be attached to the email — others are silently skipped. Key Rules The method name entered here must exactly match the method name written in the notification callback file, which extends KloNotification. Sequence numbers control both execution order and attachment order in the final email. Reordering is only possible in edit mode. Drag handles appear on each row when edit mode is active. Callbacks with disallowed file types are skipped gracefully without failing the notification. For implementation details, code examples, and how to write the callback file, refer to the Notification Developer Guide.
Working with Template Variables and Rich Text Formatting

documents.t: When creating email templates, you can use template variables to insert dynamic content. Template variables look like this: <%= variable_name %> Common Examples: <%= rfx_no %> - Shows the RFx number <%= rfx_description %> - Shows the RFx title <%= new Date(rfx_closing_date).toLocaleString() %> - Shows the closing date <%= supplier_name %> - Shows the supplier name

DO NOT apply text formatting (bold, italic, underline, etc.) to template variables themselves. The rich text editor inserts invisible HTML tags when you format text. These tags break the template variables and cause errors.
documents.s: Important Rule: Formatting and Template Variables

documents.t: Example 1: Bold label, normal variable Steps: Type your text: Closing Date: <%= new Date(rfx_closing_date).toLocaleString() %> Select only "Closing Date:" (not the <%= %> part) Click the Bold button Result: Closing Date: <%= new Date(rfx_closing_date).toLocaleString() %> Example 2: Variable within formatted sentence Steps: Type: The RFx <%= rfx_no %> has been closed. Select "The RFx" (before the variable) and click Bold Select "has been closed" (after the variable) and click Bold separately Leave the <%= rfx_no %> part unformatted

Wrong Right Select entire line with <%= %> and click Bold Select only the text labels, not <%= %> Type <%= rfx_no %> then format it Type it, leave it unformatted Copy-paste formatted text containing <%= %> Paste as plain text, then format around <%= %> Use bullet points that include <%= %> Put <%= %> on separate line or outside bullets

Step 1: Switch to HTML View If available, switch to HTML view to see your template variables clearly. Step 2: Type your content with variables RFx Title: <%= rfx_description %> Closing Date: <%= new Date(rfx_closing_date).toLocaleString() %> Step 3: Format carefully Highlight only "RFx Title:" (exclude the <%= %> part) Click Bold button Repeat for "Closing Date:" Step 4: Verify in HTML view RFx Title: <%= rfx_description %> Closing Date: <%= new Date(rfx_closing_date).toLocaleString() %> Step 5: Test before saving Use "Preview" button if available Check for error messages

Error Message: "Unexpected token '<' while compiling ejs" Cause: You accidentally formatted a template variable. Solution: Switch to HTML view Find the template variable mentioned in the error Look for HTML tags like <strong>, <em>, <span> inside <%= %> Remove the HTML tags from inside the template variable Reapply formatting only to the text outside <%= %>

Task How To Make a label bold Select label text only (not <%= %>), click Bold Add new variable Type <%= variable_name %>, leave unformatted Format around variable Format text before and after separately Fix error Switch to HTML view, remove tags from inside <%= %> Verify template Check HTML view: no tags between <%= and %>

If you see template errors: Switch to HTML View Check that no <strong>, <b>, <em>, <i>, <span> tags are inside <%= %> Use HTML view for templates - It's easier to see what's happening Format first, add variables later - Format your static text, then insert <%= %> variables in unformatted areas Keep variables simple - Don't try to format dynamic content; format the labels instead Test with sample data - Always test your template

A notification is a message, email, icon, or another symbol that appears when an application wants you to pay attention. Notifications are a way to alert you on the various important facts that have happened in your application that are worth your attention while you are not using the application. Notification Modeler is used to create a notification. One can create, edit, copy, and delete the different types of notifications in this editor. This tool is used to perform CRUD operations for the Notifications.

Upon clicking on the notification template ID, a detailed screen will open where we can check the notification details. In this detail section, users can perform CRUD operations on notifications.

The elements on the Notification Modeler screen have been explained below: Elements Description Template ID A Unique ID for each Notification. Description This is the description or implication for the Notifications. Module Type Notifications are used in two places, BOL and Workflow. To differentiate these two categories Module type has been introduced. Entity An entity is a data object created to store information about the entity in a table format. An entity can be created in the BOL Editor. Entity Object Type Object type is a unique identifier that helps understand the entities' possible behaviour. Channel It denotes the types of Notifications (e.g.: Email, App, SMS) FO Owning app.

documents.t: This Adapter is mainly written in the scope of oData v4. As most of the features supported in oData v2 are retained in oData v4, it should work seamlessly with the oData v2 system.

oData provides standard features for CRUD operations on the system. This adapter provides the ability to communicate with any oData service via Klarion’s query and data manipulation features. However, some FW features are not supported for this oData network mode.
Target location: mm_klobroker_ext As per your landscape configuration.
Fill with your landscape ID.
Value: “gateway_url”

In gateway url maintain the oData service root. Example: oData Product List Url: https://services.odata.org/V3/OData/OData.svc/Products The service root would be: https://services.odata.org/V3/OData/OData.svc Note: Don’t leave a forward slash ‘/’ at the end. In case you are using multiple service roots Maintain the common part in gateway_url and place the remaining in entity > service_name Eg: you are using service root https://services.odata.org/V3/OData/OData.svc/Products and https://services.odata.org/V3/OData/Northwind.svc/Airports, then maintain the gateway_url as https://services.odata.org/V3/OData and in entity maintain the service_name as OData.svc/Products and Northwind.svc/Airports respectively.

This is an optional column. Some oData service needs the "odata.type": "oDataDemo.Products" in the body during creating and modifying the data. If your service needs this information for POST and PATCH then maintain the schema as per the oData metadata. Eg: If your service root is https://services.odata.org/V3/OData/OData.svc get the metadata from the https://services.odata.org/V3/OData/OData.svc/$metadata and inside the metadata, find schema and namespace and fill here. Note: If your service does not accept any key in the payload other than the columns, keep this column value as null. And the odata.type will not be added to the payload.
value: ODATA This is to identify this service as an oData service for this landscape.

value: None | Basic The auth type column is used to maintain the authorisation protocol of the oData service. Currently, only authentication types of None and Basic are supported. None: No authentication is done in the requests.Basic: Basic authentication is added to the header. Basic authentication is based on user_name and password, so, user_id and password should be maintained for this auth type.
This is an optional field. If the auth_type is maintained as Basic, maintain the odata service user_name used for authentication.
This is an optional field. If the auth_type is maintained as Basic, maintain the odata service password used for authentication.

value : v1 | v2 | v3 | v4 oData runs on various versions, maintain your service’s version here. It will decide the interaction of the Klarion server with the oData service. This is present in your service root. Eg: https://services.odata.org/V3/OData/OData.svc, in the mentioned oData service root https://services.odata.org/V3/OData/OData.svc . v3 denotes the version. Note: Maintain version with lowerCase v

The configs are used to add any additional data to the header. Thus it is an array of objects with structure { "config_name": "<key>", "config_value": "<value>" }. For Eg: I need the API key in my header added as API-KEY, it should be maintained as \{ "config_name": "API-KEY", "config_value": "ASDFERNnsd234KKNFHRLJKA24jkHn234l23454" \} It will be reflected in my header as \{ ... "API-KEY": "ASDFERNnsd234KKNFHRLJKA24jkHn234l23454" ... \}
Basic API for the creation of entities such as newEntityP, and upsertEntityP are supported.

Entity Name: Entity name can be created as per the user’s requirement. Only Root entities are currently supported for OData. Service Name: Maintain the service name exactly (case sensitive) as per the entity set. E.g.: https://services.odata.org/V3/OData/OData.svc/Products in this service Products is the service name. If you are using more than one service root refer here for more details. Set the network mode as ODATA. Note : (skip, if odata.type is not required by your service) For creating and updating data, if your service needs odata.type in the body, maintain schema in config. The entity name should be the odata type case sensitive. Eg: For EntitySet Products ( https://services.odata.org/V3/OData/OData.svc/Products ) in this service root the Entity Name can be found in metadata. It will be in <Schema.EntityName> format. Thus, the entity name should be kept from this metadata as Product. Relations are not supported.

Rule to follow: The entity property name should match exactly the oData properties (case sensitive). Create entity property for all the fields you are going to use from the oData service response. Create all property as in the service is all is used. All the primary keys in the oData service should be created and marked as primary keys. If any property is created which is not in the OData service, it has to be explicitly marked as is_fw. Note: Qualifier properties are not supported.

Supported property types and oData to klarion property mapping are listed below: Property type map: ODATA KLARION Edm.Boolean Boolean No conversion required (oData will provide proper boolean value) Edm.Byte Integer(8) Edm.Date / Edm.DateTime Date Edm.DateTimeOffset Date Edm.Decimal Decimal Edm.Double Decimal Edm.Duration String Edm.Guid String (length = 36), guid is 32 digits separated by 4 hyphens Edm.Int16 Integer (16) Edm.Int32 Integer (32) Edm.Int64 Integer (64) Edm.SByte Integer (8) Edm.Single Decimal (n,7) Edm.String String / Clob Edm.TimeOfDay TimeStamp Use these above references to create the appropriate domain, length and precision in Klarion.

Deletion of oData entry is supported by deleteP API. Note: All the modifications which go in a single batch, are split into individual requests. Thus, if any request fails, requests which are successful before the failed request will be committed, and the rest will be rejected. Thus it is suggested that all saves go in individual commits.
Date of Issue: October 2023 Version: 7.0 Prepared by: Hari Krishna D Target Audience: Developers

Greater than & Greater than or Equal to (TESTED) Lesser than & Lesser than or Equal to (TESTED) NOT equal to (TESTED) Equal to (TESTED) Is null (TESTED) Is not null (TESTED) and (TESTED) or (TESTED) not (TESTED) in, not_in (Experimental) based on the oData service support this may or may not work. Like (Experimental) - will only support ‘%string%’,‘%string’, ‘string%’.
Partial select (selecting only a specific set of properties) (TESTED) Limit (TESTED)
Single property order is supported (TESTED) Multiple property order is supported (TESTED)
Selection operators are unsupported (eg. SUM, MIN, MAX…) Aliases in selection are not supported.
Joins are not supported. Groupby is not supported. Having is not supported. Expandall is not supported. Native query is not supported.
GetCountP is not supported. groupByP is not supported.

Metadata URL: If your service root is https://services.odata.org/V3/OData/OData.svc get the metadata from the https://services.odata.org/V3/OData/OData.svc/$metadata. You get the metadata URL from adding $metadata to your service root.
Updating any oData properties and committing to the oData server is supported.
User Guide Date of Issue: 09.02.2026 Target Audience: Application Developers, Consultants, Trainees, Customers Prepared by: Arjun Kumar Ram Platform Version: 6.0 ODATA SERVICES User Guide

This document provides a comprehensive reference for OData services in the Procify platform. It clearly outlines which operations are supported, which are not supported, and provides practical examples for the application development team.

This user guide is designed to help application developers understand and correctly implement OData service calls It includes authentication mechanisms, supported query operations, error handling, and best practices.
Service URL Pattern https://{customer}.procifynow.com/odata/{landscape}/{fvid}/{entityname} Authentication Bearer Token (OAuth 2.0) Content-Type application/json OData Version OData v4.0

Obtain bearer token before making OData requests: POST https://{customer}.procifynow.com/p6/{landscape}/getToken Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded Request Body: username={user_id}&scope=offline_access&password={your_password}&grant_type=password&client_id=multi-tenant Note : OData POST API supports bulk record creation by accepting an array of JSON objects Example: “username=john.doe&scope=offline_access&password=mypassword%401234567890&grant_type=password&client_id=multi-tenant” Response: { "access_token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...", "token_type": "Bearer", "expires_in": 3600, "refresh_token": "dGhpc2lzYXJlZnJlc2h0b2tlbg..." }

POST https://stest.procifynow.com/odata/dev/flavor1/People Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9... Content-Type: application/json Accept: application/json { "FirstName": "John", "LastName": "Doe", "Email": "john.doe@example.com", "Age": 30, "Status": "Active", "Department": "Engineering" }

To send relational (child) data along with the parent entity in a single request, include the relation name as a key and pass an array of JSON objects. { "FirstName": "John", "LastName": "Doe", "Email": "john.doe@example.com", "Age": 30, "Status": "Active", "Department": "Engineering", "RelationName": [ { "Field1": "Value1", "Field2": "Value2" }, { "Field1": "Value3", "Field2": "Value4" } ] }

Get All Entities: GET https://stest.procifynow.com/odata/dev/flavor1/People Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9... Accept: application/json Get with Filter: GET https://stest.procifynow.com/odata/dev/flavor1/People?$filter=Age gt 30 Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9... Accept: application/json

PATCH https://stest.procifynow.com/odata/dev/flavor1/People('person_123 Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9... Content-Type: application/json Accept: application/json { "Email": "john.doe.updated@example.com", "Department": "Product Management" }

To send relational (child) data along with the parent entity in a single request, include the relation name as a key and pass an array of JSON objects. PATCH [https://fwtest.procifynow.com/odata/UT/odata_test_1-0-2/d_e1('01332d8cc3913b2f8848462c095e1e37')](https://fwtest.procifynow.com/odata/UT/odata_test_1-0-2/d_e1('01332d8cc3913b2f8848462c095e1e37) { "descr_": "UPDATED", "boolean_": 0, // 1::1 "d_e1_d_child_aggregate_1": { "my_key": "fddd08b8cf723625a0737926af22a125", "descr_": "UPDATED - PATCH", "boolean_": false }, // 1::N "d_e1_d_child_primary_1": [ { "auto_no": "1", "descr_": "UPDATED - PATCH", "boolean_": false }, { "auto_no": "6", "descr_": "UPDATED - PATCH", "boolean_": 0 } ] } Important Points: Primary Key Handling: If the Primary Key value is provided in the request payload, the existing record will be updated. If the Primary Key value is not provided or not matched, a new child record will be created under the respective parent entity. Relationship Cardinality Support: For 1::1 relationships, the related entity must be provided as an object. Array or null values are not supported for 1::1 navigation properties. For 1::N relationships, the related entity must be provided as an array having the object(s) PUT Method Behavior: When using the PUT method, missing non-mandatory, non-primary properties will be populated with their configured default values. If no default value is configured, the property will be set to null. Previous Behavior: it was directly setting the value to null for the missing non-mandatory, non-primary properties. Transaction Handling: Parent and child entity operations are executed within a single transaction. If any validation or processing error occurs, all changes are rolled back. Invalid relation IDs or property names in the request body are silently ignored with a warning logged, allowing the valid parts of the update to proceed. $expand in URL: GET with $expand returns parent along with nested child entities in response. URL Exmaple: [https://fwtest.procifynow.com/odata/UT/odata_test_1-0-2/d_e1('01332d8cc3913b2f8848462c095e1e37')?$expand=d_e1_d_child_aggregate_1_1,d_e1_d_child_primary_1](https://fwtest.procifynow.com/odata/UT/odata_test_1-0-2/d_e1('01332d8cc3913b2f8848462c095e1e37) If $expand with the required relation IDs is/are not specified in the URL, the child entities will not be included in the response. However, the deep update operation will still complete successfully, since $expand only controls the response representation and does not affect the update operation itself. documents.t: Query Option Description & Usage $filter Filter results using logical operators Example: GET https://stest.procifynow.com/odata/dev/flavor1/People?\$filter=Age gt 30 Example with multiple conditions: GET https://stest.procifynow.com/odata/dev/flavor1/People?\$filter=Age gt 25 and Status eq 'Active' $select Select specific fields to return Example: ?$select=FirstName,LastName GET https://stest.procifynow.com/odata/dev/flavor1/People?\$select=FirstName,LastName,Email,Department $orderby Sort results by field(s) Example: ?$orderby=LastName asc GET https://stest.procifynow.com/odata/dev/flavor1/People?\$orderby=Department asc,LastName asc GET https://stest.procifynow.com/odata/dev/flavor1/Orders?\$orderby=created_on desc $top Limit number of results returned Example: ?$top=10 GET https://stest.procifynow.com/odata/dev/flavor1/People?\$top=5&\$orderby=created_on desc $count Include total count in response Example: ?$count=true GET https://stest.procifynow.com/odata/dev/flavor1/People?\$count=true&\$filter=Status eq 'Active'

documents.t: Operator Meaning Example eq Equal to Age eq 30 GET /odata/dev/flavor1/People?$filter=Age eq 30 GET /odata/dev/flavor1/Orders?$filter=OrderTotal eq 1500.00 ne Not equal to Status ne 'Inactive' GET /odata/dev/flavor1/People?$filter=Status ne 'Inactive' gt Greater than Age gt 30 GET /odata/dev/flavor1/People?$filter=Age gt 30 GET /odata/dev/flavor1/Orders?$filter=OrderDate gt 2026-01-01 GET /odata/dev/flavor1/Orders?$filter=OrderDate gt 2026-02-17T01:00:00.000Z For date supports both edm.Date and edm.DateTimeOffset format. ge Greater than or equal Age ge 30 GET /odata/dev/flavor1/People?$filter=Age ge 30 lt Less than Age lt 40 GET /odata/dev/flavor1/People?$filter=Age lt 40 le Less than or equal Age le 40 GET /odata/dev/flavor1/People?$filter=Age le 40 and Logical AND Age gt 25 and Status eq 'Active' GET /odata/dev/flavor1/People?$filter=Age gt 25 and Status eq 'Active' or Logical OR Status eq 'Active' or Status eq 'Pending' GET /odata/dev/flavor1/People?$filter=Status eq 'Active' or Status eq 'Pending' not Logical NOT not (Status eq 'Inactive') GET /odata/dev/flavor1/People?$filter=not (Status eq 'Inactive') contains String contains contains(Email, 'example') GET /odata/dev/flavor1/People?$filter=contains(Email, 'procify') startswith String starts with startswith(LastName, 'Sm') GET /odata/dev/flavor1/People?$filter=startswith(LastName, 'Sm') endswith String ends with endswith(Email, '.com') GET /odata/dev/flavor1/People?$filter=endswith(Email, '.com')

documents.t: To add an action for the page, add an aggregation “kloAction” for the page. Once the kloAction is added, create a new button control for the action. After adding a control add properties for that button control.

Similar to page actions we can add actions to our sections. To add actions for our sections kloToolbar needs to be added for that section. After adding kloToolbar add an aggregation kloAction for the kloToolbar. After adding kloAction aggregation follow the same steps as page actions. On click of add button:
An aggregation is a way for one control (called a parent) to reference another subordinate control (called a child).

For Grid, Tree, and Auto Grid section types, the Builder automatically applies horizontal alignment (hAlign) and text align property based on the control type and its associated binding. So the column header and the control will be aligned as per the standards based on the domain and control type Numeric Field Alignment​ If a control is bound to a property whose domain type is Integer or Decimal, the Builder automatically adds the hAlign config property and textAlign control property with the value Right. This automatic alignment is applied only when: The control is an input-based control. The control is bound to a property of domain type Integer or Decimal. Alignment Updates on Control Changes​ During updates, if: A control's value property or dsrc is modified, or A new binding is added to the control, the Builder automatically detects the bound property and updates the alignment accordingly. Domain/data type Data alignment Header Alignment Boolean [if control is checkbox or switch] Center Center Blob N/A N/A String Left Left Clob Left Left Date Left Left Decimal Right Right Integer(16) Right Right Integer(32) Right Right Integer(64) Right Right Integer(8) Right Right Timestamp Left Left Control-Specific Alignment Rules​ The following alignment rules are applied automatically: Control Type hAlign Value Switch, Check Box Center Button, KloAction Right Auto Grid Behavior​ For Auto Grid sections, automatic alignment is applied only in the Desktop view. For the Mobile view, the default alignment behavior is retained and no automatic alignment adjustments are applied.

documents.t: onPageInit​ onPageInit hook method will be called only once as soon as the controller is loaded The transaction, model , and the UI is yet to be created for this, so those will not be available in this method. onPageModelReady​ onPageModelReady event will be called when the model is created and the transnodes are initialized, but the data is not set to the model yet. From this hook method developer can call skipModelPreparation method which will skip setting the data and executing the query. If the developer skips the model preparation, then developer should be responsible for setting the data is the model onPageEnter​ onPageEnter hook method will be called whenever the page enters the visible area by means of navigation(both forward and backward navigation). If the navigation is within the same page, this method will not be triggered onPageExit**:**​ onPageExit hook method will be called in the source page whenever the user navigates to a different page onPageDestroy: onPageDestroy hook method will be called only once when the page is destroyed. Page will be destroyed during the back navigation Example : if you are navigating back from PageB to pageA then PageB will be destroyed
Refer to this link for TransNode API.
Refer to this link for navigation API.
Controls are used to define the appearance and behaviour parts of the section. Types of controls: Open UI5 controls Klo controls
5.7 kloControls contains all the information about the kloTouch controls.
The class field in the property section of the control describes the class of the control.

A tooltip is often used to specify extra information about the elements when the user moves the mouse pointer over an element. Follow the following steps to use the tooltip for the screen title: Step 1: Add two properties to the screen. Step 2: Mark isTitleTooltipRequired as ‘true’ and provide value(as string) to titleTooltip. Now when you hover on the title of the screen you will show the titleTooltip value. Refer to this for more information Tooltip for Screen Title
The label field in the control’s property section is to set whether the label is needed for the control or not (specific for card and form type section).

The card layout provides you with only one column. Hence, earlier there was no option to provide a label. But, since we are adding multiple controls in the same column, it is better to identify the control with the label. Now, with the provided property, it is possible to put labels on the controls inside the card layout. Step 1: Add the property islabelForCardRequired to the property subscreen and mark it as ‘true’. Note: If you have already added the label during the entity creation for that property, then that label will appear after adding the islabelForCardRequired as true. And if you haven’t added the label during the entity creation or you want to add another label then you can simply provide your text in the ‘label’ property.

In the tree section, we can drag and drop the controls from one section to another. OR Create a new control. Right-click on the section where the control needs to be added, click on ‘New’ and then click on ‘Controls’ to add a control for that section. After clicking on ‘Controls’ below page will appear to add the control. Note: Control id should be unique under a section (Two controls / config /section toolbar can’t have same id) Adding control without binding i.e. if dsrc or value field is empty, it will show a warning message.
Klotouch Editor is divided into four major sections, which are listed below. Tree Preview Detail Page Data Model

The tree section in the kloTouch editor contains the hierarchy of the page. The tree will contain no data unless a page is created/selected from the toolbar. Once a page is created/selected it shall automatically reflect in the tree section.
Expand All option is to expand all the collapsed sections (sections, pageLayout, controls, pageArea, actions).
Collapse All option is to collapse all the expanded sections (sections, pageLayout, wcontrols, pageArea, actions).

This filter button will open a popup as : It will contain fuzzy search, section drop-down and clear filter option. The use of fuzzy search is to filter the items based on the Ids. Section dropdown is used to select and preview a particular section / pageArea of the page. This will filter the tree only for the selected section and its children. Clear filters are used to clear the filters applied.
Using the cut copy-paste options, we are able to copy paste the controls/section /pageAreas. Note: These buttons are inactive in read-only mode.

The create section button is used to create a section and to add required properties from a particular type of transnode. Clicking on this button, it will open a popup : In the above popup, we need to mention section id, section title, section type and page data model with which the section is supposed to be binded. After selecting the page data model, properties list will come in the Page Data Model Node section from where we can select the required properties. Note: We can edit the section after creation from the Editor.
The Preview section is to preview the page before the final execution.

This is also known as the Preview type. The use of preview types is to see the look and feel of the same page on different types of devices. The devices that it can be viewed on are given below. Any new version of the device comes, likewise, it will be updated. Preview samples

Usage of the auto-refresh button is to refresh the preview in design time i.e. if the auto-refresh is enabled whenever the user changes anything in the page’s metadata it will be previewed (auto-refreshed) automatically.
The usage of the preview or refresh button is to refresh the preview page to make the changes visible.
The full preview option is used to view the page in full view.
The close option is to hide the preview section, to enable the preview section make use of the section toggle buttons Buttons Identity To Expand to Full Screen. To Close the Preview Section.

DnD on Preview is a drag-and-drop feature. It is an option to Drag and Drop properties and elements in multiple ways. DnD from Unused to MainTree: Step 1: From the page data model, select the transnode, go to its unused property tab and drag the Property. Step 2: Drop that Property to any section you want. After preview, the newly added property will be shown on the screen. DnD from MainTree to MainTree: Users can Drag and Drop any main tree element across the tree. Step 1: Drag an element from any section and Drop it into the different sections in the same tree. When an element is dragged and dropped between sections, a prompt appears asking whether to Move or Copy the element. Selecting Move removes the element from the source section and places it in the target section, while selecting Copy duplicates the element in the target section without affecting the source. Note: The Move and Copy options are shown only when the drag-and-drop action occurs between two different sections.
Details of the item selected in the tree section will be shown in this detail section: This depicts the name or ID of the item selected in the tree.

The property tab in the detail section displays the properties that are added and options to add new properties that are associated with the selected item (page, pageArea, pageLayout, sections, controls). Refer to this to understand binding concepts. Value:​ The value field will hold the value provided for the property. Path:​ In this path field, users can only bind with exactly one property or value. This can be used if there is only one property to bind. Parts:​ In this path field, users can bind multiple properties or values. This can be used if multiple values or properties need to be provided for binding. (Note: If we are using formatter function, then it is mandatory to provide either parts or path value) Formatter Functions​ Controller function name (formatter function) can be given for the field. Type:​ In the type field, the user can provide the datatype for the control’s value. Formatter Options:​ Formatter options define how a value is formatted and displayed in the UI. Validation Constraint:​ Constraints are optional and define how an input value that is entered in the UI should look like. During parsing, the value is validated against these constraints. For example, an Integer type has a constraint for the maximum that is automatically validated when parsing the input values. Add new Property:​ To add a new property, click on the add icon in the property section toolbar. On click of the add icon the properties associated with the control will be listed. Click on the property that needs to be added, it will be added to the control. Provide the property value for the newly added property. Property Group:​ The Property group consists of the following: Property Group Details Appearance The appearance property group will filter the properties that are responsible for the appearance of the control. Example: visible, textAlign, wrapping, textDirection. Data The data property group will filter the properties that are responsible for the binding values of the control. Example: value, src, text, href. Dimension Dimension property group will filter the properties that are responsible for the dimensions of the control. Example: width, size, height. Behaviour The behaviour property group will filter the properties that are responsible for the behaviour of a control. Example: editable, enabled. Misc Properties other than the above-mentioned groups will come under Misc. Select All/ None:​ This option is used to select/unselect all the properties. Cut:​ This option is to cut and paste the property of one control to another control. Copy and Paste:​ The Copy and Paste options are used to copy/paste one or more properties from one control to another. Delete Property:​ To delete a property, select the property that needs to be deleted and click on the delete icon in the properties section toolbar.

The Aggregations tab in the detail section displays the aggregations that are associated with the selected item (page, pageArea, sections, controls) Path:​ Binding Path addresses the different properties and lists in a model and defines how a node in the hierarchical data tree can be found. Examples: $M>/list, $M>/items Add new Aggregation:​ To add a new aggregation click on the add icon in the aggregation section toolbar. On click of the add icon the aggregations associated with the control will be listed. Click on the aggregation that needs to be added, it will be added to the control. Select All/ None​ This option is being used to select/unselect all the aggregations. Cut​ This option is to cut and paste the aggregations of one control into another control. Copy and Paste​ The Copy and paste options are being used to copy/paste one or more aggregations from one control to another. Delete Aggregation:​ For delete, select the aggregation that you want to delete. And click on the delete icon in the aggregation toolbar.

The Events tab in the detail section displays the events that are associated with the selected item (page, pageArea, sections, controls). Functions​ The controller function name should be given in the field, which will be called in case of the event. Example of Controller function: Parameters​ The values passed in the field can be accessible in the function as a parameter. Add new Event:​ To add a new event click on the add icon in the event section toolbar. On click of the add icon the events associated with the control will be listed. Click on the event that needs to be added, it will be added to the control/sections / pageArea. Note: If we are adding a new event then, it is necessary to add or select the function name. If we are adding a function from the vh as OpenDialog, it will show a popup with all the pageAreas to select,from which we want to navigate. Select All/ None:​ This option is being used to select/unselect all the events. Cut:​ This option is to cut and paste the event of one control to another control. Copy and Paste:​ Copy and paste options are being used to copy/paste one or more events from one control to another. Delete Event:​ To delete an event select the event and click on the delete button from the toolbar. Events list on page In the page-level events, we have an option to see the list of events added to this page. Step 1: Select the page in the Page Builder page tree section Step 2: Select the events tab in the page detail section Step 3: enable the toggle button Once it is enabled, all the events added to this page will be listed below

NavTo is a kloController API that is used for navigation across the application. In the Events tab of the Page Builder, if we select NavTo as an event method, the below parameters will reflect for NavTo. Parameters for Navigation​ The following are the parameters for the navigation: Target Page: It is an F4 of the screens where sections of the current screen, related screen (screens created with related entities) and all the screens of the respected app are present. Section: It is an F4 of all the pagelayouts, pageAreas and sections of the target page. Tags: It shows all the TagIDs maintained in the target screen. Mode: It is a dropdown for different screen modes. App Data: It is a field where the application can send any data while navigating to the target screen. Page Data Model: It is a F4 of all the Data models of the target page. Active Index: It accepts the index to which setActive will be called in the list. Page Data Model Map: It is an array of JSON which expect SourceTransNode & TargetTransnode(i.e SourcetransNode data will be copied to TargetTransnode) Query Parameters: It is for navigation by query(navByQuery). Share Mode: This is for setting whether the mode will be shared after navigating between the source and target pages. Share Model: This is for setting whether the transaction will be shared after navigating between the source and target page.

The Style Class tab in the detail section displays the quick styles that are available for the control/pageArea/sections. There are style classes that have already been added and there are options to add a new style class for the selected item (pageArea, sections, controls). QuickAdd:​ Quick Add for Sections:​ Below is the list of quick adds available for specific section types: Section types Quick Adds Card, card List Card styles Grid Grid styles Card Styles:​ Grid Styles:​ Quick Add for Controls:​ Below is the list of quick adds available for specific controls: Controls Quick Add Icon Font size, Text color Text, Label, Title, Link Font size, Text color, Bold, Italic, Underline Button, Switch, info label Font Size, Background color, Text Color, color combination, Bold, Italic, underline, border style Input, TextArea, DatePicker, TimePicker, DateTimePicker, MultiCombobox, MultiInput, SearchField, comboBox Font size, Text color, Bold, Italic, Underline, border style Font Size:​ Text Colour:​ Bold:​ Italic:​ Underline:​ Background color:​ Color Combination:​ Specific Style:​ Category:​ In this category field, we can choose the style category that needs to be applied to the selected item. Style Class:​ Class names should be provided for this field, which will be applied to the selected items. Style class works after selecting the category. In the below image, we have taken the border as our category. Hence, border options are seen in the StyleClass. Note: The style class should not be empty. Format Rule: Always: If the format rule is marked as always, it will always apply the style. Text Contains: If the format rule is marked as the text contains, it will apply the style if the value contains the one mentioned in the format value. Formula: If the format rule is marked as formula, it will apply the expression maintained in the format value field and based on the result set of the expression (result is expected to be true or false) the style class will be applied to that control Example Format value for formula : {= ${$M>/temp/save}?true:false} Format Value:​ If the format rule is marked with text contain, then text will be taken from this format value field and it will be compared with the control’s value. If the format rule is marked with a formula, then the expression will be taken from this format value field and based on the result set(the result should be expected to be true or false) of the expression, the style class will be set. Example Format value for formula : {= ${$M>/temp/save}?true:false} Full Row:​ If the full row is marked as true, then the style class will be applied to the entire row, where the control is placed. Note: For tree screen type, full-row in style class will be applicable only when the section’s screen type is full row, it will not work for control for control type tree tables. Add new Style Class:​ To add a new style class click on the add icon in the style class section toolbar. On clicking the add icon, a new entry will be created for the style class. Select the category and add the style class accordingly. Cut**,** copy, and paste:​ For cut, copy, and paste you need to select the styleclass and then use the cut, copy, and paste accordingly. Delete​ Select the StyleClass item you want to delete and then click on the delete icon from the toolbar. Grid Cell Coloring:​ For adding css(background) to whole cell of grid section, user can do following: Add user defined class in control of grid section use :has Pseudo-class, and do required styling Example: as given below: td:has(.invAmountColorWholeCell) { background: #0c8123; }

Vienable is the short form of visible and enable. The Vienable tab in the detail section displays the vienable dashboard and UI Auth for the page. Toolbar:​ Page Entity:​ Copy and paste:​ Upload and Download Excel:​ Role Info:​ Status Info:​ Vienable toggle button Info:​ 2.3.5(i). Vienable DashBoard:​ Control ID:​ The Control ID column displays the available controls on the page. Entity:​ The transNode of which the control is bound. If it is not marked as true, status and role-based vienable will not work. Permission:​ The permission of the entity in flavor on which control/element visibility will be decided for logged-in users. If permission is not filled by developer, then proceeds with with vienable calculation If permission is filled by developer, but filled permission not given for logged in user, then the current control/element will be hidden by skipping vienable calculation If permission is filled by developer, filled permission given for logged in user, then proceeds with with vienable calculation Show As Label:​ If the control is disabled, and the showAsLabel is marked as true then the disabled control will be rendered as a label. Page Size(S, M, L, XL):​ The page sizes S, M, L, and XL define small, medium, large, and extra-large size page resolutions. If the control is marked as non-visible for page size S, then the control will be hidden for that particular resolution. If the control is marked as disabled for page size S, then the control will be disabled for that particular resolution. Note: The resolution will be considered based on the parent section’s resolution for control. page Mode (Create, Edit, Display, Review):​ There are four modes for a page: Create, Edit, Display, and Review. Among the page modes display will be the default mode. We can change the page modes based on the requirements. Role:​ Role-based vienable helps the control to be visible/enabled based on the current logged-in person’s role and object type of the bound entity. For this role-based configuration, KloTuner is used. For role-based vienable, config has to be maintained for the respective entity. If it is not maintained in the entity level, It will consider the role maintained in the app-level. While configuring the config table, provide the s_role_rollup value as below: Role s_role_up Owner 10 Supervisor 20 Reviewer 30 Overlooker 40 Status Group():​ Status: open, approved, accepted, processed, rejected, completed. Based on the s_status_group, s_status, and object type for that particular entity, we will be able to make the control visible/enabled. For status-based configuration, Klotuner is used. Note: Similar to role-based vienable, status-based vienable status configs have to be maintained for the entity. Result:​ In the result column, we can see the final result of how the controls will be rendered, for the selected page mode, selected role, and selected status group. The yellow background in the column header represents the selection of the column. 2.3.5(ii). UI Auth:​ Element Id:​ It is the control ID of the control. Object Type:​ For this object type, UI Auth will be applied. Role:​ For this role, the UI Auth will be applied. Status:​ For this status, UI Auth will be applied. Mode:​ For this mode, UI Auth will be applied. Mode Value:​ This will determine the control’s visibility / enableness. Add new UI Auth:​ To add a new UI Auth click on the add icon in the toolbar of the UI Auth section. On click of the add icon, a popup will be displayed. In the popup select the control for which UI Auth needs to be applied. Select the role, mode, object type, and status after selecting press OK. A new entry will be added in the UI Auth section. Vienable Runtime precedence:​ If all the vienable sections (screen size, screen mode, role, status) are maintained for control, below will be the flow of the section it will take into consideration.

The Modeller tab in the detail section displays the modeller only if the modeller is available for the selected section type. A modeller is generally used for modelling the sections. Note: The modeller will load only if the particular section is visible in the preview section. To access the modeller of a section select that particular section in the tree section to preview that particular section. Card & cardList Modeller:​ WYSWYG (What You See What You Get) Card WYSWYG allows the users to arrange/resize controls of the Card. The Card WYSWYG is available in the tab called “Modeller” of the kloTouch Editor if the section type is given as cardlist/card. These are the following steps to use WYSWYG: Step 1: Select the section (of type “cardlist” or ”card”) or any child of the section (of type “cardlist” or ”card”). Step 2: Open the “Modeller” tab. Users can arrange/resize controls as required. Step 3: For arranging the controls, the user can simply drag a control and drop it anywhere on the axis as per the requirement. While doing the arrangement or resizing, if any other control exists in the same axis, red lines will be shown. Step 4: For resizing the controls, Users can simply click on the controls and resize them as they want. Before resizing: After resizing: NOTE: Users can select multiple controls(by holding the control) and “Make the same size” (Vertically/Horizontally). Reveal Grid: With this button, one can enable and disable the gridlines. Tabular Card Modeller: On clicking this button, a tabular card modeller will open where the user can manually provide a column/row span for the alignment of the card/cardList. Alignment: Options for Alignment, space distribution, equal size: Modeller Size: To make the card modeller screen size the selected item’s size one uses the modeller size (Tab, Desktop, etc) tab.(This option has been disabled: To use this, change the screen resolution from preview type) Absolute/Relative: The absolute button will make the modeller as the previous version without additional features. On the other hand, the Relative button will set the modeller section as the newer version(5.7) with all the additional features. The card is generally a css gridlayout and the cardlist is generally a list of css grid layouts. ScreenSize Spans available XL, L 36 column span M 24 column span S 12 column span For more information about CSS grid layout click here Note: if column span and row span are not maintained for a particular screen size then it will pick from the default span (if maintained). But if either of the one is maintained then it will pick both the values from that particular screen size. Note: As the Page Area of type Dialog doesn’t have any direct assignment with any of the page Layouts, the Modeler/preview will not be available.This Modeling can be achieved by adding that particular section to any other page Area (which is assigned to any page Layout). Once the modelling is completed, reassign to the Dialog Page Area. Grid Modeller:​ Grid modeller is used to model the grid type section. Using this grid modeller we will be able to change the column width, we can assign filters, and sort for a particular column. Pivot Modeller:​ There are two types of pivot modellers Design time Run time Note: The difference between the design time and run time modeller is that the design time modeller cannot be modified by end users it is predefined by the developers. The design time pivot can be set as the default view of the section by use of the ‘default report’ property of the section. Design Time Modeller :​ Design time pivot will be created by the developers which will be predefined, and cannot be modified by the end users. Step 1: Select a section which is of type card list or grid type and then add the report Step 2: Select the newly created record and click on the modeller to see the design time pivot modeller. Note: For how to use it you can refer to this document Pivot Modeller Run Time Modeller:​ The pivot modeller is used to configure the grid and card list subscreen. You can customise the pivots and charts based on your preferences, using this modeller. These are the following steps to enable the run time Pivot Modeller: Step 1: Select a section which is a card list or grid type and then add a toolbar to that subscreen. Step 2: Now in the toolbar detail, add two properties (reportSelectionField and pivotModellerButton) and mark these properties as true. Once the above properties are added during the design time, the modeller button and view selection will appear in the toolbar of the table during runtime. Note: For how to use it you can refer to this document Pivot Modeller CSS Grid:​ CSS grid is the screen container that can hold page areas or sections. Under CSS Grid, users can arrange subscreen controls in any way they want in any layout. Step 1: Make the Page Layout or Page Area screen type as ‘CSS Grid’. Step 2: Right-click on that page layout or page area and add the page layout data to it. After assigning the page section or PageArea, the page layout or page Area will look like this. Step 3: Now go to Modeller then click on ‘Tabular card Modeller’. Step 4: Add row/column-span to align subscreens as you want.

Language toolbar​ Components Description Language Dropdown (Select Language) This will list all the available languages in the dropdown. On selection of a language a new column will be displayed with the selected languages. Editable Language This will display all the selected languages from the language dropdown. Once the language is selected the language column will be editable. Search This will filter the grid rows of the text ID table. Add To add a new item or entity to the Item grid table. Translate To translate all the selected items that have been added to the row of the table. Show/Hide References It will hide/display the reference column. The reference column displays the destination where a particular textID has been placed. Add a new Entry​
To add a new entry/text click on the add button () on the Language toolbar. A Dialog box will appear.

In the Dialog box we need to give a TextID (Example: Header, Text, Caption, etc) and choose a category from the category list. Then click on OK. Category Description Text This refers to normal text labels for any text that has been added in the editor. Tooltip The tooltip helps in showcasing short descriptions about a particular entity or entry when the cursor is hovered over them. Title This represents the Normal title. TextID This represents the text ID. Ghosttext (PlaceHolder) This represents the texts in any kind of Input box. Text will be added to the screen. Editing the Languages:​ Select the languages that need to be made editable in the language dropdown and in the editable languages dropdown, to make the column editable. Translation:​
Select the items from the grid that need to be translated.

documents.t: Click on the translate button to translate to the required language. Reference:​ Reference sections display where the text ID is being used. By default, the reference section will be hidden. To enable the reference section click on the reference button in the toolbar.

Expand all options are used to expand all the collapsed sections(sections, controls, containers, actions). Add Model Path:​ By using the add model path button we will be able to create a new model path for the page. Model Path/TransNode:​ Properties Description Entity This field will display the entity name that is associated with the transNode. Property Description Displays the property description. folded_from This field will display from where the path is folded. node_type Node Type determines the type of the model path. on_arrive Refer to onArrive. q_auto_update If this is marked as true, then any change in the transactional data will be automatically updated in the model. q_object_group The Object group mentioned here will be filtered for the particular query type. q_object_type The object type mentioned here will be filtered for the particular query type. q_pin Coming Soon q_saved_qur_action Refer to q_saved_qur_action q_saved_qur_id This implicates the saved query ID which needs to be fired along with the search (if q_saved_qur_action is marked as fill). relation This field displays the name of the transNode. screenid This field displays the page ID. set_active_if Refer to Set_active_if Node Type:​ Entity: Entity defines a single entity (single row in a database table). Entity Set: An entity set is a set of entities (an entire table in a database). Query: Query which is associated with the entity. Other: Other types of transnode represent that the node is not associated with any entity. Its data can be bound from the controller. onArrive:​ Blank: If the model path is marked as blank then the data will not be set to its folded path. First: If the model path is marked as first then the first index of its entityset(folded from) will be set. History: If the model path is marked as history then it records the active index of the entityset. For example: if the model path is marked as history, then each selection of entity will be recorded. None: If the model path is marked as none then the data will not be set for that path. Set_active_if:​ Set active is classified into three categories as listed below: Always: Always defines navigation without any pre-conditions except menu navigation. Saved: Saved means navigation is permitted only if there is no dirty object in the transaction. If dirty entities are found, the Save confirmation dialog comes to ask the user if he/she wants to save the changes, otherwise, navigation is cancelled. Valid: Valid is a default value. Valid means navigation is permitted if there are no dirty objects or dirty objects are in a valid state with no error. If dirty objects are there and in an error state, the errors are highlighted on the page for the user to correct before moving forward. If the mode path’s set_active_if is provided as “valid”, on time of navigation the onValidate function (if the function is maintained in the <entity_name>.ts file) will be called. Please refer to the below matrix for all combinations of set_active_if: always saved valid Within Screen Same index of entityset(tab selection change) CREATE No Validation, No Dirty Popup No Dirty Popup No Validation Not CREATE No Validation, No Dirty Popup Dirty Popup Validation Different index of entityset Any No Validation, No Dirty Popup Dirty Popup Validation Close Detail Any No Validation, No Dirty Popup Dirty Popup Validation Different Screen Through Manu Any Dirty Popup Dirty Popup Dirty Popup Through Link inside screen Any No Validation, No Dirty Popup Dirty Popup Validation q_saved_qur_action:​ Execute: Execute will autofire the query while rendering the page. This is set as the default value. Fill: If the q_saved_qur_action is marked as true then the “q_saved_qur_id” will be filled on search. None: None means it will take no action.

We can edit some of the usage of any particular property from the tree section. Properties Usage elementid Entity property id. entitypropertyid This field will display the entityPropertyid. relation This field will display the TransNode of the entity property. screenid This field displays the page ID. base_control This field will display the ui5 control that has been assigned for this property. One can change the control of the property by using the value help. (Updating these fields will update at the property type level and impact across the application) col_span Using this field we can assign the column span for the property. has_filter If marked as true, the filter is available for the property column in the grid type section. has_fuzzy If marked as true, fuzzy is available for the property column in the grid type section. Fuzzy indicates a search field. has_groupby If marked as true, groupby is available for the property column in the grid type section. has_sort If marked as true, sort is available for the property column in the grid type section. Sort indicates sorting in ascending and descending order. ismandatory This field displays whether the selected property is mandatory or not. length This field displays the selected property’s datatype length which is assigned during property creation. max_value This field displays the selected property’s maximum value which is assigned during property creation. min_value This field displays the selected property’s minimum value which is assigned during property creation. r_domain The data type of the entity property. row_span Using this field we can assign the row span for the property. textid The value of this field will be displayed as a label in the case of the form type section. vh_type It determines the VH type whether it should be combobox, f4, or autoComplete. width Using this field we can set the default width of the property. For ex: This is the property type created by default using Data Studio: Suppose the property type has been changed as per below: To reflect the same changes in the application as well, please follow the mentioned steps: Step 1: Open the screen metadata in the Page Builder.
