KloTouch module of Framework is providing default Page Data Models: Properties Usage deviceInfo Indicates user’s device type with Boolean values for properties: desktop, tablet, phone Example Binding: {= ${$M>/deviceInfo/desktop} } $M: Model deviceInfo: Page Data Model Desktop: Property perm Contains all enabled permissions in app Example Binding: {= ${$M>/perm/d_sales=CR_ACC} } $M: Model perm: Page Data Model d_sales=CR_ACC: Getter for Create permission enabled in entity d_sames which returns Boolean value env_user Contains all Env User Properties Example Binding: {= ${$M>/env_user/owning_bp} !== 'BP001' ? true : false } $M: Model env_user: Page Data Model role: One of the properties of Env User env_system Contains all System Data(transaction.$SYSTEM) Properties Example Binding: {= ${$M>/env_system/roleID} !== 'DEVELOPER' ? true : false } $M: Model env_system: Page Data Model role: One of the properties of System Data(transaction.$SYSTEM)

By using this embedded section we can embed sections or containers from other pages to our current page. Note: KloGuid and KloLink controls will be disabled when added inside the embedded subscreens. Also, the title, icon and actions provided for the embedded subscreen will not be rendered. Page layout type” flexible_col” is not supported inside embedded section.

To create an embedded page create a page Layout in the page where the section is embedded from. In our current page create an embedded section. In the layout data of the embedded section provide the value below: flavor.pageId.pageContainerId if it's a separate app. pageId.pageContainerId if the embedding page is from the same app. Note: Developers can pass supported navTo() properties from a parent screen to an embedded child screen. TN and NT parameters will be passed to child functions (such as onPageEnter() and onSectionEnter()) only when they are explicitly maintained in the embedded section's screenParameters configuration.

The properties available in the embedded config are listed below. Embedded config can be added from context menu of the embedded section NAME TYPE DEFAULT VALUE DESCRIPTION flavor string - App from which the page should be picked from. App is mandatory only if the app of the screen to be embedded and the app of the hosting page are different. screenid string - ID of the screen. Mandatory subscreenid string - ID of the subscreen. Mandatory. isTransactionShared boolean false If true, the hosting screen and the embedded screen will share the transaction. Else, transaction will be different for both the screens isSharemode boolean false If true, the hosting screen and embedded screen will share the mode. When mode is set via the controller for the hosting screen, the same screen will be set to the embedded screen as well and vice-versa. Else, the mode will not be shared. When set to the hosting screen, the mode will not be set to the embedded screen. tnmap Array<JSON> - An array of JSON with the keys fromtn and totn. The value of the keys should be the transnode relation ID of the host screen and embedded screen respectively. The transnode of the embedded screen will be added as a child to the transnode of the hosting screen so that when setActive is called on the parent transnode, data will be set on child. Example : [{"fromtn": "no_hdr_list", "totn": "detail_embedded"}] screenParameters INavToData This property expects a JSON the same as the navTo parameters. All the navTo parameters can be passed here. Flavor, Screen ID, subscreen ID, isTransactionShared, isSharemode and tnmap can also be passed as key-value pair here instead of separate properties.
Config Properties Provided: tnmap: [{"fromtn": "no_hdr_list", "totn": "detail_embedded"}] subscreenid: pageArea01 screenid: s_0021_27_10__002 Embedded Screen:

onValidate:​ If the transNode’s onarrive (in the transNode’s detail section) is provided as valid then, onValidate will be called during navigation. onAfterCreate:​ onAfterCreate method will be called once the new entity is created. onDelete:​ The onDelete method will be called once the entity is deleted.

Setter function will be called once the entity property value is changed. Example: public set firstName(new_value:string){ if(new_value == this.firstName) return; this.name:string = new_value+" "+this.lastName; this.s("firstName",new_value,"string",false,false); } Getter function will be called whenever the entity property is getting read. Example: public get name():string{ return this.Firstname +" "+this.lastName }
Page Builder User Guide- 7.0 Date of Issue: January 2023 Target Audience: Application Developer, Consultants. A User Manual for application creation, knowledge, and work reference.

What is kloTouch? kloBase platform is a modern low-code platform to build enterprise-class cloud-enabled portals and mobile business applications. Its unique layered development empowers to build powerful reusable models for the continuously evolving business needs. kloTouch is a low-code visual designer tool that helps application development efficiently and effectively. What is the objective of kloTouch? kloTouch is a visual designing Page Builder that is effective in building applications that work on portals and mobile applications. kloTouch has the following objectives: Ease of Operating: It involves least to no complex coding, thus, making it an easy-to-use tool, not only for the modellers but also for common people with limited technical knowledge. Efficient: This Page Builder is programmed in a manner that requires a limited to negligible coding process. This prevents the modellers and developers from losing time by writing lengthy codes, thus saving time. Rich In-Built Features: Multiple add-ons and real-time notifications to name a few, help make it a featureful application.
Note: goto will only work on mobile and tab. On a little scroll of the screen, the goto button will be visible.

All the page Area ID(s) provided in the page’s layout section will implement the master-detail-detail paradigm by displaying up to three pages (page Areas) in separate columns. For a Flexible column layout, only three columns will be rendered, if more than three layout containers are provided in the layout section it will take the first three layout containers/sections. Configuration:​ For using the flexible column layout, select the screenType of a pageLayout as flexi_column. In the layout section of that pageLayout add the layouts. The setLayout() method was used in Flexible Column to define the layout width. As Flexible Column is now deprecated, it is recommended to use setFirstColumnWidth() in pagelayout type Two Column to configure column widths. Example: Flexible_col one Column Expanded Flexible_col two Column Expanded Flexible_col three Column Expanded
documents.s: 12.1. Flexible_col (Deprecated, Use Two Column Pagelayout Instead):

documents.t: It is similar to a flexible column. The only difference is that it can only implement the master-detail paradigm up to two pages only. And also unlike a flexible column it provides a horizontal splitter between the two pages.. Configuration:​ For using the two column layout, select the screenType of a pageLayout as two_column. Assign pages and sections. Use setFirstColumnWidth() to configure column widths. two_column one Column Expanded two_column two Column Expanded

Stack is a layout structure where the required elements show up one by one on a particular action based on the given metadata. Configuration:​ For using the stack layout, select the screenType of pageLayout / PageArea as stack. Example: We have a pageLayout of screentype stack: Stack will render only one layoutSubscreen at a time. As a default, the first layoutSubscreen is rendered. When it is navigated to the second layoutsubscreen it hides the first one & displays the pageArea it is navigated to.

Tab Layout represents a collection of tabs with associated content. The number of tabs rendered will be equal to the number of section/section container ID(s) given in the layout Data section. The tab title will be taken from the section/page Area’s title property, the tab title will only be visible if the flags are maintained in the layout data section and the showTitle property is marked as true. Configuration:​ For using the tab layout, select the screenType of pageLayout / PageArea as tab. In the detail section, mark the showTitle as true. After adding the showTitle as true, in the layout section. For the layouts added (pageArea / section ) add the property showTitle and title, provide the values. Note: selectedKey reflects the currently active tab/section — it is not a one-time "default tab" setting. If bound to a data field, the Tab control will always show whichever tab that field currently holds, and will keep showing it on subsequent loads/refreshes unless the field's value is explicitly reset. If the supplied key doesn't match any tab/section currently rendered, the control falls back to another available tab instead of forcing the configured one. To always land users on the same section regardless of prior state, drive it explicitly through navigation rather than relying on selectedKey alone.

The page refers to the single visible screen of the application. The page is the topmost layer of an application. It will be embedded with a pageLayout.

Create Blank Page:​ Step 1 - Select the Add icon to create a Blank Page To create a new page click on the Add icon from the top toolbar. Three options will be shown, from those options select ‘Create Blank Page’. After selecting the option a popup will be displayed. ![Screenshot](./img/page-builder-image585.png)![Screenshot](./img/page-builder-image577.png) Step 2 - Fill the popup to create a new page In the popup, provide the ID and name/title for the new page. After providing the details, click on the Submit button. ![Screenshot](./img/page-builder-image362.png) Note: Newly created pages will be updated in the database only after saving. To save click on the save icon at the top toolbar (right side of the edit action button). Properties Usage Description Description for the page. leadentity Coming Soon docid The ID/text will be displayed along with the title (bindable). icon If value is provided, the icon will be displayed in front of the title. navbyquery In case user is navigating from a different page to the current page with passing the QP (Query Parameters) in navTo, then this field is mandatory to filter the data based on the query properties passed Example: {“sourcePath”: “search”} navbykey In case user is navigating from a different page to the current page with passing the D (entity unique key) in navTo, then this field is mandatory to set that particular entity’s index as active. Example: {“sourcePath”: “list”} Pip enabled If marked as true, picture-in-picture(PIP) mode will be enabled for the page. screencontainerdefault Default page Layout ID for the page can be provided here. screencontainerdesktop The page layout ID for the desktop can be provided here. screencontainermobile Page Layout ID for mobile can be provided here. screencontainertab Page Layout ID for the tab can be provided here screenid Not an editable field, displays the page ID. title The page name will be filled here, it will be the title for the page. Create Page from Wizard:​ Step 1 - Select App and click on the Edit button ![Screenshot](./img/page-builder-image627.png) Step 2 - Page selection Click on the add icon dropdown and select “Create a page from wizard”. ![Screenshot](./img/page-builder-image651.png) Step 2 - Provide page information ![Screenshot](./img/page-builder-image60.png) Once the wizard popup is displayed, provide the screen information. Select the Data Source and check whether Page ID, Page Title, Menu Text, Icon, or Menu Group is pre filled or not. Page Id, Page Title & Manu Text should be prefilled and will be Entity`s description or entity`s ID. Select the Data source (entity or query) by clicking on the vh icon, and give page ID and Page title and Menu Information. By default, the entity id will be Page Title. Page Id should be unique in the particular app, if we are creating more than one pages with the same entity, the Page Id will be auto incremented by 01 as a suffix. Menu Group will come from the app header. We can provide a menu text and can select a group and icon to be displayed there from the Choose button . It will update the page to the selected menu group. Menu Icon will come from Entity’s icon or default icon will come. Also we can allow operations by clicking on the icons provided: ![Screenshot](./img/page-builder-image38.png) This shows the options to perform CRUD in the main entity. These icons are for Add, Edit, Delete, Multi Delete, Download Excel operations respectively. By default all these icons are selected. We can deselect them by simply clicking on the icons. Click on Next. Step 3 - Select the required section, relation, type, template, position and actions. ![Screenshot](./img/page-builder-image184.jpg) The screen is displaying different requirements to select for all section types of each relation. Relation: It shows the return entity name along with the relationId of the entity. Section: It shows the type of section of the corresponding relations. Type: It shows the screentype of the section that will be created using the relationid. Display options: It shows the different templates of the screentype. It depends on the Type selected for the section. Position: It shows the position of the sections in the application. Eg: If a relation has the Position as dialog, then it will appear as a dialog whenever navigation happens to the section. Required Actions: It shows the option to perform CRUD in the corresponding section created from the relation. We can select the relation required from the checkboxes displayed on the left most of the screen. NOTE: A 1:1 relation can be added only as a Detail section and is supported with Form and Card screen types. The section can be placed as a Section or Subsection on the page.Template Id is supported as Read Only and Inline Editable Section type can be selected from the drop down for different sections (search, list and detail). ![Screenshot](./img/page-builder-image590.png)![Screenshot](./img/page-builder-image600.png)![Screenshot](./img/page-builder-image586.png) For List type of section, we can edit the template from the dropdown (Read Only, Inline Edit or Popup Edit) We can specify the position for sections as section(tab) or subscreen or dialog. Actions can be provided to each section type by selecting the icons from required actions.(These are selected by default). The relations have a DND (Drag-and-drop) feature, if we are changing the sequence then the sections will also be generated accordingly. Template tab will not be there for wizard dialog. The detail screen for all child entities will be opened in a popup. Template types:​ Read Only It is non-editable. We will get an edit button for the detail tab only, not for relation list tabs. ![Screenshot](./img/page-builder-image276.jpg) ![Screenshot](./img/page-builder-image569.png) Inline Edit We will get the Edit button for the selected tab in the relation list. ![Screenshot](./img/page-builder-image621.png) Popup Edit We will get an edit button in each row of data. ![Screenshot](./img/page-builder-image507.png) Click on Next at the bottom of the screen. Step 4 - Specify the availability of fields on screen ![Screenshot](./img/page-builder-image253.png) On navigating to the screen. all the properties of the lead entity & the selected relations will appear. All the properties will be selected for the detail section(if Detail is selected) & first 5 properties excluding the primary keys will be selected for the list(if List is selected). After page creation, if we are changing its cardinality from Data Studio,it will not be reflected on the UI automatically. We have to delete the transnodes manually and have to create them again. For Example: If the user is creating a wizard with 1:n relation and after creation, the cardinality of the relation will be changed to 1::1 from the Data Studio and tries to update the page from wizard, before that the user have to delete the transnodes manually and have to recreate it again. Deletion of a section or control​ If we are deleting a section from Page Builder, it will be updated on wizard also: In the same way it will work for other sections. If we delete any property from the Page Builder, it will be deselected from the wizard popup also. Anything we are changing from Page Builder, it will be reflected in the wizard popup. Step 3: Click on the submit button and the current page will be copied to the provided app. Note: The above example was making a copy of a particular page in the same app. What if we are copying a page in a different app and that app doesn’t have the associated entity? If we are doing so then the Page Builder sends an alert message (“Entities/Queries are not found in the app. Do you still want to continue?”) Note: If we click on OK then the particular screen will get copied in the target app without a pagedata model. And if the target app contains the associated entity then the screen will render with all data.

PageLayout is the topmost layer embedded with the page. At runtime, only one pageLayout will be picked based on the device type. Example: If the page is being loaded on the desktop, and the screencontainerdesktop property is not maintained (empty) then the pageLayout ID maintained in the screencontainerdefault property will be rendered. Layouting can be also possible using a pageLayout. CardList​ Screentype cardlist is generally a sap.m.Table with one column. CardList Config​ Config properties are used to set the behaviour of the cardList. Refer to this link to learn more about cardlist config properties. Adding config to a cardList section Step 1: Right-click by selecting the cardlist section. Card:​ A screen-type card is a single CSS grid that can hold a single entity. **Note:**On adding checkbox type of control for card or cardlist screen type, dsrc property should not be maintained, otherwise it will show labels along with the checkbox.To bind with a data source, we can use the ‘selected’ property. This includes holidays and special periods underlying the organisation’s calendar. For how to use it you can refer to this document. Adding config to Calendar section: Refer to the same steps as mentioned in the Cardlist or grid. Adding config to Multi Calendar section: Refer to the same steps as mentioned in the Cardlist or grid. Form​ Screen Type form is generally a simple ui5 form. Note: If you want to customise/configure form then with the following way we can do that: Step 1: Add config to the form type section: click on the form type subscreen click on ‘New’ and then click on ‘add config’ : In the Page Builder, the F4 value help for the columnSpan property displays options "All" and "None". All: Displays all available entries without filtering. None: No filtering criteria applied, showing all possible values. Step 2: Now add the ‘density’ property to the ‘form config’. NAME TYPE DEFAULT VALUE DESCRIPTION density string default Specifies whether the form needs to be displayed in default or compact mode Step 3: Now add value to the property. It has two values: compact and default. In compact mode, the labels take the entire column width and shift above the controls. In default mode, the labels appear beside its control. Form in compact mode: Form in default mode: Grid​ Screen Type grid is generally a sap. ui.Table. Grid Config​ Config properties are used to set the behaviour of the grid. Note: If we are adding config properties, then the value of the properties should not be empty. Timeline​ A timeline is a screen type of section that is used for showing the timeline of any order/process. A common use case is to provide information about changes to an object, or events related to an object. Timeline Config​ Config properties are used to set the behaviour of the timeline. Refer below table to learn more about timeline config properties. Add Config to a Timeline section​ Step 1: Add config to the Timeline type section: Right-click on the timeline type subscreen then click on ‘New’ and then click on ‘add config’. Step 2: Timeline config will be added for the section. config for Note: If we are adding config properties, then the value of the properties should not be empty. NAME TYPE DEFAULT VALUE DESCRIPTION displayShape string Circle Specifies whether the shape of the timeline will be a circle or shape. displaySize string XS Specifies the size of the timeline. backgroundColor string Accent6 This property specifies the background color of the timeline. Tree​ The Tree Screen Type is designed to represent hierarchical data in a structured manner. It allows users to visualize relationships between parent and child nodes, making it ideal for displaying nested information such as organisational charts, file systems, or any other hierarchical datasets. Implementation: Data Preparation:​ To prepare the data for a Tree Screen Type, we will use a JSON format that represents the hierarchical structure. Here’s a sample JSON array: [{ "key_01": "value_1", "key_02": "value_2", "key_03": "value_3", "child": [{ "key_01": "value_11", "key_02": "value_22", "key_03": "value_33", "child": [{ "key_01": "value_111", "key_02": "value_222", "key_03": "value_333", "child": [{ "key_01": "value_1111", "key_02": "value_2222", "key_03": "value_3333", }] }] }] }] JSON Structure Each object represents a node in the tree. The child array holds nested objects, representing the child nodes. Key names for child nodes are consistent with parent nodes, ensuring a clear relationship. We will store the data in other type transnode. Screen:​ Step 1: Create one pageArea with screentype, fit_to_area and a section with screentype, tree. In the section layout, add one property autoHeight as true. This ensures that the section dynamically adjusts its height based on the content displayed. Step 2: Create an other type transnode. Step 3: Add Controls for Data Binding Create controls within the section for each key in your JSON data (key_01, key_02, key_03). Bind the section to the other type transnode that contains the hierarchical JSON data. Ensure that each control is correctly bound to the corresponding key in the JSON structure. Section toggle buttons are used to make the sections hide / visible. Each toggle button is described below: This is the tree button. This is used to show the hierarchy of the page sectionally. With a click of this button, it will hide the tree section. However, if you click back it will show the tree section again. This is the preview button. This shows a live view of the changes that have been made to the page. With a click of this button, the preview will disappear. However, on clicking it again the preview section will reappear. This is the Detail button. The detail section shows the details for the selected item in the tree (page hierarchy). On clicking this button the detail section will disappear. On clicking it again the section will reappear. Page data model which is equivalent to the UI5 Model in the view. On clicking this button the section will disappear. The Where Used list can be accessed from the context menu of the following elements: Page Page Area Section Transnode To open the Where Used dialog: Right-click on the required element (Page, Page Area, Section, or Transnode). The context menu is displayed. Select Show Where Used from the menu. The Where Used dialog opens, displaying all references for the selected element. When clicking on Show Where Used from the context menu, a Where Used dialog box opens. This dialog displays all references to the selected item within the current application. Dialog Layout​ The Where Used dialog is divided into two sections: **Left Panel (Tree View) ** Displays a hierarchical list of all references for the selected item. **Right Panel (Details View) ** Shows detailed information for the reference selected in the left panel. Selecting an entry in the tree view updates the details shown in the right panel. Supported Elements​ The Where Used feature is available for the following elements: Pages Page Areas Sections Transnodes Reference Checks by Element Type​ **Pages ** The system checks for references in: Application menus Home pages Other pages (including embedded sections and tags) Associated files (controllers, utils) Navigation events within the current page (for example, navTo events) **Page Areas ** The system checks for references in: Associated files(controllers, utils) NavTo Events, layouts in other pages and the current page **Transnodes ** The system checks for references in: Binded data paths Associated files(controllers, utils)

The Where Used dialog allows direct navigation to referenced application objects. In the left tree section, a Navigate button is displayed for application-level objects. When you click this button: A new tab opens automatically. The relevant tool or editor is loaded. The referenced object is preselected and highlighted in the opened tool.

Enable permissions for all entities of the application and provide only necessary permissions for the users. Avoid providing all permissions, even if it is an admin user. Only provide permissions which should be intended for that particular user. If permission is used for restricting an action, always make sure the prevention is done also from the server-side. Any client side i.e. screen / controller / client callbacks. restrictions are not considered secure. When adding a server side validation, make to add in both D2K_SERVER (ONLINE save) and D2K_MSG (OFFLINE save).

documents.t: When an entity is created, CRUD permissions are enabled by default. These permissions are available to the TESTER role by default. The permissions are grouped under the default flavor-level permission group: flv_master_grp. Whenever a new flavor is created, the flv_master_grp group is automatically created for that flavor. You can verify these settings under Page Builder → Permission Designer → Permission Groups tab. Select flv_master_grp, then open the Entity Permissions tab to view all CRUD permissions. Refer Permissions - User Guide for detailed explanations. 11.2. Flavor Master Permission(Permissions by default) When a new flavor is created, a master permission group named flv_master_grp is generated by default. This group initially contains only the “TESTER” role by default. To assign default permissions to any additional roles, add them to the flv_master_grp. Within this group, there is a custom permission called flv_master_perm. Any group having the flv_master_perm permission automatically inherits all permissions, regardless of what is configured in the Entity Permissions tab. The flv_master_perm is not exclusive to the flv_master_grp; it can be used in other groups as well, and the behaviour will be the same. Upon entity creation, permissions are automatically assigned to the flv_master_grp for that entity. To disable the impact of flv_master_grp permissions, simply remove all roles from that group. 11.3. Developer permissions Users with the “DEVELOPER” system role have all permissions by default, irrespective of entity-specific configurations.

documents.t: When an entity is created, CRUD permissions are enabled by default. These permissions are available to the TESTER role by default. The permissions are grouped under the default flavor-level permission group: flv_master_grp. Whenever a new flavor is created, the flv_master_grp group is automatically created for that flavor. You can verify these settings under Page Builder → Permission Designer → Permission Groups tab. Select flv_master_grp, then open the Entity Permissions tab to view all CRUD permissions. Refer Permissions - User Guide for detailed explanations.

documents.t: When a new flavor is created, a master permission group named flv_master_grp is generated by default. This group initially contains only the “TESTER” role by default. To assign default permissions to any additional roles, add them to the flv_master_grp. Within this group, there is a custom permission called flv_master_perm. Any group having the flv_master_perm permission automatically inherits all permissions, regardless of what is configured in the Entity Permissions tab. The flv_master_perm is not exclusive to the flv_master_grp; it can be used in other groups as well, and the behaviour will be the same. Upon entity creation, permissions are automatically assigned to the flv_master_grp for that entity. To disable the impact of flv_master_grp permissions, simply remove all roles from that group.

documents.t: By default, all roles assigned under Flavor Master Permission have full access to all entities and menus within a flavor. If you need to override the default permissions or implement custom Access Management, follow one of the approaches below. Option 1: Modify Permissions for an Existing Role​ Remove the role from default permissions (permission group) for whom permission changes are required. Create a new permission group with: Entity-specific access (e.g., restrict Create, Update, or Delete) Menu-specific access (e.g., hide or allow certain menus) Assign the newly created permission to the role. Option 2: Create New Roles and Permissions​ Create a new role based on your access requirements. Define a new permission group with limited or customized access. Assign the newly created permission to the role. Remove the role from the old permission group (default permissions) and assign the new permission group. Note: Flavor Master Permission provides full CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) access to all entities by default when assigned. Custom permissions are required to restrict or control access.

documents.t: When a CRUD operation is performed on an entity and access restriction is enabled on that operation, the system checks if the user has permission to perform that operation. If the user doesn’t have permission, the request will be rejected before executing any server side callbacks. If the user has permission, then the request will be processed further. In the DEV landscapes the permission can be assigned via the Permission Designer screen in Page Builder & Controlled in QA / PROD system via Role Permissions screen in Security & Permissions. Explain further below in the document. Each CRUD permission allows performing a specific operation, Read - Read permission allows the user to fire a query to that entity. This is validated on the server side. Create - Create permission provides the assigned access user to create entries in that entity. This is validated on the server side. Update - Update permission provides the assigned user access to update existing entries in that entity. This is validated on the server side. Delete - Delete permission provides the assigned user access to delete existing entries in that entity. This is validated on the server side. Download - Download permission is a template permission and doesn’t come with any validation by default. It controls the download excel button visibility in wizard created screens. Similarly in case of online query fired from client also, the query will be rejected if sufficient permissions are not found. Incase a query from entity A inner joins entity B. The user executing the query is expected to have permissions for both entity A & entity B. Consider a modelled query belongs to entity A, and it has inner join to entity B.The cases are as follows, The user has permission to A & B - The query will be executed and the result set will be returned as usual. The user doesn’t have permission to A / B - The query will be rejected at entry point and no server side query callbacks will be executed. The user has permission to read B, but not A - The query will be rejected at entry point and no server side query callbacks will be executed. The user has permission to read A, but not B - The query will be rejected while parsing the query, but before query callback will get executed. Middleware messages are also validated against the permission of the user who created the message. If the user who generated that message doesn’t have required permissions, the message will fail to process and will be moved to error q. This is not applicable for CRUD operation performed inside the server. Once the request reaches the server, and is validated, any further CRUD operations performed in the rules are not validated. Similarly for any server side triggered activities i.e. CRUD performed in the scheduler, appservices will not be restricted.

documents.t: Permission groups, their permissions and assigned roles can be changed in the ongoing versions. When the newer version is transported. During the transport, the permission groups & permissions in the groups of the newer version will be copied to runtime, overriding the older version configuration. All the users who got upgraded to the new version will get permission groups assigned based on their application role and the users permissions will be adjusted based on their new permission groups. In case of minor version deployment, where there are users who are running on older versions, Permission groups assignment will not be changed for those users. Permission adjustments will not be triggered for those users i.e. If new permissions were added to an existing group / removed from the existing group in dev, will not reflect. Permissions will be adjusted when there is a change detected in the application assignment that is relevant to permissions i.e. version upgrade, role changes, application assignment removal, admin changing assignment / permission group permissions ..etc.

documents.t: To check whether a user has specific permissions (CRUD or custom) in code, use the permission APIs available on the KloTransaction object. 1. Checking CRUD Permissions​ Use the following method to check if a user has permission to perform a Create, Read, Update, or Delete operation on an entity: hasCRUDPermission( entityName: string, crudAccessType: ENTITY_OPR_TYPE, r_user_id?: string, r_flavor?: string ): Promise<boolean> entityName: Name of the entity. crudAccessType: The operation to check. r_user_id (optional): The user ID to check permission for. Defaults to the user of the current transaction. r_flavor (optional): Flavor context, if applicable. Defaults to the flavor of the current transaction. Note : If permission is not enabled in that entity, but checked via the API, it will return true. 2. Checking Custom Permissions​ Use the following method to check a specific custom permission by its ID: hasPermission( permissionId: string, r_user_id?: string, r_flavor?: string ): Promise<boolean> permissionId: The ID of the custom permission to check. Other parameters are the same as in hasCRUDPermission. Environment Support​ Both APIs can be used in client-side and server-side environments. If r_user_id or r_flavor is not provided, they default to the user and flavor of the current transaction. Note : Performing any validation on the client side doesn’t provide protection against requests directly made to the server. For any security validation, make sure to add the validation on the server side.

Permissions is a feature provided to control the access to application resources. By default an application user can access any entity of the application and perform CRUD operation if enabled. To control the access, CRUD permissions can be enabled at entity level and appropriate permissions can be granted to selected users.

The "Permission Designer" screen has been added under the Page Builder menu. This screen lets you create and manage permissions, permission groups, and assign roles and permissions to each group while developing an app. Permissions are used to permit access to contents of the Application. Permissions can only be created/Generated in the DEV environment The permissions are owning app specific and will inherit to child Apps. There are two types of permissions, CRUD Permissions: Entity permissions are used to restrict CRUD operations by users for an entity. CUSTOM Permissions: Developers can maintain the custom permissions using the permission master screen and use it for controlling menu and home page visibility. Permissions can also be used in application logic to make decisions based on whether the current user has the particular permissions or not.
Entity CRUD : Basics understanding of CRUD activities performed on entities. Application roles : Roles which are used for vieniable.

Picture-in-Picture (PiP) shrinks a screen into a small player so that you can keep watching while using other apps on your mobile device. You can move the small player around your device's home screen and position it over other apps.

Select the screen for which the developer wants pip mode and in the properties section mark pip_enabled as true. Now, for this screen, PiP mode will be available on mobile. The developer needs to make sure that the PictureInPicture plugin is added.
For using PiP mode the developer needs to mark the pip_mode property as true in the properties section of the screen.

Two actions are required to be added in the KloSectionToolbar (showViewSelection and pivotModellerButton). Once the above actions are added during the design time, the modeller button and view selection will appear in the toolbar of the table during runtime. In Runtime, on click of the modeller button, as shown in the above screenshot, Pivot Modeller opens. If the report is selected from the selection view of the modeller, it will be available and selected automatically. The details can be seen in the left section. If no report is selected when the modeller has opened, it will look like the following image: Pivot Modeller Sections - In the left section, respective report details are shown: During design time, only one report can be modelled in a single instance whereas during runtime, users can work on multiple reports in a single instance. Report listed above the properties are shown only in runtime. On the right side, two list is available i.e Report List and Properties List

It contains the reports created by the user during runtime i.e. Transactional Reports, as well as the reports created during design time i.e. Metadata reports. Metadata reports are locked, users can not modify them. They can only select the report to see the output on their pivot table. This list has four actions i.e. Create, Delete, Copy, Rename on a report. Create - On click of the create button, a blank report gets created with a default name as GUID (GUID, in general, signifies a unique ID). Copy - On click of copy, it copies the selected report with a default name as GUID. Delete - On clicking the delete button, the selected report gets deleted. Rename - This can be achieved by opening the right-click context menu over a report item. On the right click, the report also will be selected and details will be reflected on the left section. All those actions of reports will be saved on close of the modeller.

This list is visible at both runtime and design time. It contains all the properties of the entity in the transnode which is bound with the table/grid. There is a fuzzy search provided in the toolbar of the property list. Here the properties have a drag and drop option. They can be dragged and dropped to the following lists - Rows, Columns, Preprocessors, Chart (Series and Category dropdowns only).

This is the left section of the modeller. It contains five panels : Preprocessor Rows Columns Chart Setting Preprocessors -​ To add preprocessors, properties can either be dragged/dropped from the Property list, Rows, Columns list or the add button itself. Properties can be dragged and dropped in the preprocessor list. Selecting a function will show data showing that kind of value, YEAR: will show values in each Year.(2023,2024) MONTH: will show value in each Month(Jan, Feb,.., Dec) MONTH_YEAR : will show value in each Month with Year (Jan 2023, feb 2023, Jan 2024,feb 2024). DATE: will show value in each Date(1 to 31) DAY: will show value in each Day.(Monday - Sunday) DD_MM_YYYY: will show value in the DD-MM-YYYY format (24-05-2024) ROUNDOFF: will show rounded values such as, if 24.5- value will be shown as 25 CUSTOM: isn’t working Currently Mapping: Mapping can be used to show a different value for a particular value. Rows -​ To add rows, properties can either be dragged/dropped from the Property list, Pre-processor, Columns list or the add button itself. Rows Details - It contains three icons for sorting i.e. No Sort, Ascending, Descending. There is a button - to show more/less, to expand and collapse the advanced fields. The user can paste the icon uri from the sapIcons in the rows section as shown below:(Currently value help is not shown.) Style doesn’t work as for now Columns -​ To add columns, properties can either be dragged/dropped from Property list, Preprocessor, Rows list or the add button itself. Column Details - It contains three icons for sorting i.e. No Sort, Ascending, Descending and two icons for showing Total and Total Percentage. There is a button - to show more/less, to expand and collapse the advanced fields. The figure above shows advanced column options. The column header title is the grouped pivot columns title. The pivot property is the entity property on which the data is pivoted. The aggregate function is the aggregate function of the columns. The default value is count. The aggregate position is the position of the Total column. The possible values are Show Explicit, Show in Tree, Don’t Show. The above figure show the aggregate position: Show Explicit The above figure shows the aggregate position: Show In Tree Chart -​ The chart panel itself contains a switch button, which defines where the Chart is required for the selected report that you are working on. Chart Details - In the chart section, two dropdowns are droppable i.e. Series and Category. Category (x-axis) - Properties which are added in the Rows, among them one can be added in category by either drag/drop or by selecting from the dropdown. Series - Properties which are added in the Columns, can be added in Series multi-dropdown, either by drag/drop or by selecting from the multi-dropdown. There is a toggle button in the header of the chart section. It Enables the Chart view in the view selection field of the KloSectionToolbar. An entry with a label of the report with __chart is made in the viewSelectionDield. Once you select the chart we get the view as shown below: You can further configure the chart with the help of options available in the chart section of the KloPivotModeller. Options are available to enable the zoom of the chart. To enable micro charts there is an option zoom. Colors of the chart can be changed by using the Colors property Colors e.g: {"type":"ColorSet", "list": ["#FF5733", "#33FF57", "#3357FF", "#FF33FF"]} Or {"type":"ColorSet", "step": 5 } Fore more detail check KloChart User Guide Setting -​ Setting Detail - There is a settings section at the bottom of the left container of KloPivotModeller. The toggle button shown above enables the grand total row for the report. The other options rename the grandTotal row and column title. Section Toolbar Properties Three new bindable properties are available on Section Toolbar. They control pivot execution behaviour and link or text rendering — set them in the Properties panel during design time. Property Type Default Description PivotExecutionMode string "client" Controls where pivot aggregation runs. "client" — computed in the browser. "server" — SQL generated by PivotQueryGenerator and run on the database. Switch to "server" for large datasets to avoid browser memory pressure. PivotValuesAsLinks boolean true When true, pivot cell values are rendered as clickable links. The destination of each link is determined by the application's navigation configuration. Set to false to render plain text values. PivotValuesAsLinksScope string "both" Limits where the link rendering is active. "designTime" — links appear only in the designer. "runTime" — links appear only at runtime. "both" — links appear in both contexts. Only takes effect when PivotValuesAsLinks is true.

documents.t: Write the app with its app version and then select the action to either Publish or Validate app. Dropdown will be shown when the page is opened from the menu. On pressing enter or comma it takes the string as an entry. Even if enter or comma is not pressed, on submit it will take the string as an entry. For Publish​ Choose the Build Type from the given option to Publish the App. Publish action will show the response for that flavor as shown below. And status can be checked using the Refresh button provided below App details. Dependencies changes Suggestion​ On click of submit option for publishing a suggestion popup will be shown to the users in case there are any changes detected in the provided apps dependencies. The popup will not be shown incase of no changes detected. These suggestions are determined based upon calculating the time difference between the last metadata save and the last publish time, if the last metadata save time is latest then the dependent app will be considered for suggestions. Actions Apply suggestions - will include the suggestion apps to the publish list Continue with selected apps - will skip the suggestions and continue with the user provided apps list Cancel - will close the popup & publish will not be triggered. The Build History screen allows users to view and filter logs related to various app builds.Refer for more details-Build History Screen ** ** Single or multiple apps can be published. Before Publish, it will validate all the selected apps. If validation fails for any of the flavors, no apps will be published. Selected apps will be published only when all the apps will be validated and there will be no errors. If some of the apps are already IN-QUEUE and Publish is triggered for the same apps again. The completed apps will go to publish again but for IN-QUEUE apps one message will be shown that some of the apps are already IN-QUEUE. Validation failed scenario during publish​ Before initiating the build, all flavors are validated. If any application has a validation error, the build will be blocked and an error list will be displayed, as shown in the screenshot below: However, if a flavor contains only warnings or informational messages, a dialog box will appear, allowing the user to choose whether to view the messages or proceed with the build as shown in the screenshot below: If the user selects Show Logs, it will show all the info as: Else if user selects Proceed with build, the flavor will be published. For Validate​ Choose the validate option in order to validate the flavor. Press Submit, It will show if there is any error. Validation for multiple flavors is possible. documents.t: In order to build the application using the URL directly (in case login is not working), the URL should be as below. Replace the placeholders with values as per your requirement. https://<your_domain>/p6/<your_landscape>/closedmodules/<app_util_ver>/buildandvalidate.html?appName=<AppNames>&action=<Action>&environment=<Environment> Place holder Description your_domain E.g.: dev.procify31.com your_landscape E.g.: CTOOLS_DEV app_util_ver E.g.: app_util_6-0-13 AppNames E.g: sample_app7637_2-0-1 Action Following actions are possible“publish” Use this action if you want to Build the application“validate” Use this action if you want to validate the application and see the errors. Environment: dev OR prod.(if action is publish) Note: In case you want to build multiple applications, specify the same separated by comma ‘,’ Example: https://dev.procify31.com/p6/CTOOLS_DEV/closedmodules/app_util_6-0-13/buildandvalidate.html?appName=sample_app7637_2-0-1,bol_test_1,tpr_test_6-0-3&action=publish&environment=dev It will ask for credentials if the url is directly entered. Note: During the build process, it is mandatory for the parent app to be built first, followed by the child app. However, if the users do not follow this build sequence, the app sequence will be automatically corrected during the build even if the user uses the app utility screen or build url.

This document helps the Application Team find the exact source of a query fired from a Procify application, optimize that query, trace the generated SQL, and use the relevant framework (FW) APIs efficiently. Details about Covers: locating the query source, query optimization techniques, enabling sufficient logging to inspect the generated query, and using FW APIs (e.g. addEndpoint) optimally.

Access to Procify Data Studio for the app/flavor under investigation. A working Private Node checkout of the application source (see the Private Node Setup guide). Access to Design Studio → Query Console (formerly SQL Executor). Access to Google Cloud Logging for the environment under investigation.

Not Applicable — the methods in this guide (Where Used List, Network Initiator, Private Node search, query logging) are built-in platform capabilities and do not require separate enablement. The optional logging flags are listed under Configurations below and Google Cloud Logging guide.
documents.s: Query Analysis — How to enable the feature
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/Query Analysis - 4. How to enable the feature

documents.t: Open Procify Data Studio and select the App/Flavor that owns the entity or query in question. In the entity/query tree, locate the Entity, Query, Property, Value Help, or Event Exit you want to trace. Open the “Where Used List” option for that object. It lists every screen, query, rule, or event exit that references it, along with the property type / value help used where applicable. Use this list to narrow down which module(s)/screen(s) could be responsible for firing the query, before checking Network calls or code.
documents.s: A. Finding the source of a query — Where Used List (Procify Data Studio)
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/Query Analysis - 4. How to enable the feature

documents.t: Open the application in Chrome and press F12 (or right-click → Inspect) to open DevTools. Switch to the Network tab, make sure recording is on, and clear existing entries for a clean trace. Reproduce the action in the application so the request fires. Find the relevant XHR/Fetch request (filter by “Fetch/XHR”). Click the request, then open the “Initiator” tab — it shows the call stack (exact file and line) that issued the request. Click any frame in the Initiator stack to jump to that source line in the Sources panel.
documents.s: B. Finding the source of a query — Chrome Network Initiator
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/Query Analysis - 4. How to enable the feature

documents.t: Set up / start your Private Node for the flavor in question. Open the application’s source checkout in VS Code, e.g. the src folder under the flavor’s workspace. In the Explorer, right-click the src folder → Find in Folder. Search for the query ID / entity ID / property name. Use “Match Whole Word” to avoid false positives. Review every places where this query/entity is used
documents.s: C. Finding the source of a query — Private Node (Find in Folder)
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/Query Analysis - 4. How to enable the feature

documents.t: Paste the query definition and surrounding code into an AI assistant (Recommended : Claude AI with Procify Knowledge Assistant) and ask for unnecessary joins, unused columns, and missing filters/indexes. Never paste real customer data or credentials. Apply setPartialSelect([...]) to return only the needed entity properties. Set setLoadAll(false) unless full-row data is genuinely required. Apply setLimit(n) Push filters into the query (setColumnFilter) instead of filtering in code afterward. Important: Expand All and an INNER JOIN on the same relation are not supported together — confirm which is configured before removing either. Re-run the optimized query in the Query Console and compare row counts / execution time. Query Console- User Guide Re-run the screen end-to-end on Private Node and capture a before/after timing as evidence.
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/Query Analysis - 4. How to enable the feature

documents.t: SN Steps 1 Call addEndpoint once per Business Object, not once per child entity — it already sends the full BO tree by default. 2 Leave onlydirtyobject at its default (true) to send only changed children; set false only when every child must be included. 3 Leave onlyRootEntity at its default (false) so children are included automatically. 4 Consolidate repeated addEndpoint calls against the same BO’s children into one call.
documents.s: E. Using addEndpoint and other apis efficiently
documents.u: /Procify_Documentation/docs/Docs/User Guide/Query Analysis - 4. How to enable the feature

documents.t: The following flags and settings control how much query/transaction detail is captured for debugging, without needing extra code. Parameter Description txn.enableStackTrace Boolean on the transaction (default false). Set true to record a stack trace of all activities of the transaction, including queries executed. Switch off again once captured. enableQueryStats Framework-internal flag (default true) driving query statistics collection. Do not disable unless instructed by platform engineering. "enableReqDump": true (klarion.json) Captures full incoming request payloads into the req_dump folder. Disabled by default. Turn off again after the investigation — req_dump folders have previously grown to multiple GB when left on. Select Distinct (Query → Detail) Set loadAll = true only when true column-level distinctness is required; otherwise leave Select Distinct off.

setPartialSelect(entityPropertyNames: string[]): KloQueryForRule Parameter Description entityPropertyNames Array of return-entity property IDs to select, instead of every property on the return entity.
setLoadAll(val: boolean): KloQueryForRule Parameter Description val Whether to load all fields of the return entity at execution time. Set false to skip properties/relations not required.
setLimit(limitValue: number): KloQueryForRule Parameter Description limitValue Maximum number of records to fetch — use for pagination on list/search screens.
setExpandAll(relations: string): string Parameter Description relations Comma-separated relation IDs to expand. Not supported together with an INNER JOIN on the same relation.

addEndpoint(endpoint, type, channel, object?, onlydirtyobject?, onlyRootEntity?): EndPointBean Parameter Description endpoint Endpoint ID(s) to notify — meaning depends on type (BP_USER, ENDPOINT, USER). type EndpointType — determines how endpoint is interpreted. channel ChannelType filter on qualifying endpoints (default DEVICE). object The KloEntity whose full BO tree is sent. Defaults to the event object. onlydirtyobject Default true — only dirty child entities are included. Set false to force all children. onlyRootEntity Default false — children already included. Set true to send the root entity alone. Note: A single addEndpoint call already messages the root entity and its (dirty) children — avoid a separate call per child entity.

getExecutedQuery(queryid, saveQueryObj, flavor?): Promise<KloEntitySet<KloEntity>> Parameter Description queryid Query name or entity name. saveQueryObj Saved query parameters to apply. flavor Optional — flavor to resolve the query/entity from.

The sql_executor_6-0-1 or later versions of the App should be assigned to the user to access the Query Console. Note: Query Console can only be run in Public Node and is available in the Development environment only.

The Query Console tool enables users to validate and run complex SQL SELECT queries, displaying the results in an organized table format. It also supports the use of EXPLAIN and EXPLAIN ANALYZE for query analysis and optimization insights. Output records are listed immediately after execution. Results can be downloaded as an Excel file with a single click for easy sharing or further analysis. Only SELECT-style queries are permitted. Note: DML/DDL keywords (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, DROP, etc.) are automatically blocked and will be cleared from the screen.

1. Select Page Builder header from the menu 2. Select "Query Console" menu item to navigate to the SQL Executer application 3. Use the app selection dropdown to select your application 4. From the apps dropdown select your application 5. Use the SQL Editor section to write the SQL statements 6. Auto complete suggestions will also be shown based upon the selected application 7. Click "Execute" to execute the query 8. Use the splitter to expand the result section 9. Use the horizontal scrollbar to navigate through all the table columns 10. Click "Download" to download the results in a xlsx file

In the Data Studio, when a user is working on any particular entity/query/value help then that object will be locked. Hence, other users will be restricted to modify the locked objects. Those objects will be unlocked as soon as the user clicks on the save button. If the user forgets to click on save and log off, in the meantime if someone wants to modify that object, then they can use the Unlock entity page to unlock the locked object.
Step 1: Select the Design Studio menu header. Step 2: Click the Record Lock Manager menu item.
Users can search for any particular object with the object name (Example: d_no_items, q_notifications) in that particular app.
Assigned apps for the users will be listed in the dropdown, users can select the app in which they want to unlock an entity.
With a click of the unlock button, the selected objects from the list will be unlocked.
With a click of the Refresh button, the list of entities of selected apps is refreshed.

Columns Description Object Name It will list the names of the objects(entity, query, value help) that have been locked for the selected app. Object Type It will display the type of the objects(Entity / Query / Value Help). Lock State It will show the current state of the object. Locked By It will show the user ID by whom the object has been locked. Locked On It will show the entity-locked date and time

To unlock an object follow the below steps: Step 1: Select the app from the dropdown. Step 2: Select the objects Step 3: Click on the unlock button. On clicking on unlock the selected objects will be unlocked and a success message toast will be shown.
The cockpit app is required to be assigned to the user to get access to this feature.

When using getResult / setResult on the server side for row wise authorized entities, make sure not to send back non authorized data. The data set on to the query using setResults are directly returned as query results, no more filtration is applied. When changing callback from client side to server side always consider row wise authorization if involved. Avoid logging sensitive data. Native query doesn’t support row wise authorization, so don’t select sensitive data via native query. Use “me” token only if all users of applications can access the data, else don’t use me token, use a different access key and add User Access Keys in callback. ValueHelp where row wise authorization is turned off should not have any sensitive data as key or description. The data based on which User Access Keys are generated, should be protected. For example : If Access to issues is based on projects assigned, then, only authorized users should be able to assign or un-assign projects. Query fired on server side will not have row wise authorization / permission applied on it. To apply row wise authorization on server side queries, use applyRowWiseAuthorization.

The feature is for restricting unauthorized access. Only implement on entities with sensitive data. For non-sensitive data, consider using query filtrations. In the User Access Keys callback, make sure to batch queries based on user, as it can be called for 1 - many users.

In the Data Studio, open the Access Management tab. Turn on the row-wise authorization flag for the entity, then click ‘+’ to add a token template. Developers can add more than one template if needed. Tokens are generated based on the application's code in the entity.ts file and the data available in that entity. Property Stores the property ID used to create tokens based on those properties. Access Token Navigation Navigates to the Data Access Rules screen to display the generated tokens.

documents.t: How does Row-wise authorization work ? Row wise authorization works by filtering records on the server level by matching tokens (strings that are used to create a mapping) between user and data. A simple illustration like: Entity Data: data1 -> [token1, token2] data2 -> [token2, token3] data3 -> [token4, token5] User tokens: user1 -> [token1] -> [data1] user2 -> [token1, token2] -> [data1, data2] user3 -> [token3, token4] -> [data2, data3] user4 -> [] -> [] Consider an entity ENT_A, where row wise authorization is enabled, and each record in ENT_A has a set of tokens assigned to it. Consider user USER_A, who has a set of tokens for that entity assigned to him. When USER_A fires a query, he will get only the records in the entity ENT_A which have at least of the tokens that USER_A has. Eg : Consider entity d_no_hdr S.no k_notif_id work_center plant Access Tokens 1 10005154 ELEC 2000 wc=elec pl=2000 2 M10236914 CIVIL 2000 wc=civil pl=2000 3 M10236913 AIW 2000 wc=aiw pl=2000 4 10005141 AIW 2000 wc=aiw pl=2000 5 10005140 CIVIL 2000 wc=civil pl=2000 6 10005142 CIVIL 2002 wc=civil pl=2002 In the above example we have two tokens assigned for each record of data, as listed in the access token column. Now consider a set of users and the token assigned to the users as listed below. User Id Access Tokens asset_manager_01 wc=aiw elec_manager_01 wc=elec plant_head_01 pl=2000 elec_civil_user_01 wc=elec wc=civil Now when query is fired by, asset_manager_01, record 3rd & 4th will be returned as the user has only wc=aiw token assigned to him and only the 3rd & 4th record have the wc=aiw tokens. elec_manager_01, has token wc=elec, so records 1st will be returned as that is the only record with token wc=elec. plant_head_01, has token pl=2000, so all records from 1-5 will be returned as all those records have token pl=2000. elec_civil_user_01, has tokens wc=elec, wc=civil, so, records 1,2,5,6 will be returned. As record 1 has token wc=elec and record 2,5,6 has token wc=civil.

documents.t: Step 1 : Enable row wise authorization on the entity via Data Studio. Step 2 : Create an access token template, enter a readable ID and Key (can be the same). Step 3 : Click on the property expand icon, click on + - add property, and select the property with which you want to control data access. Step 4 : Save the entity. You will see a dialog asking to recalculate the access token. (This dialog won’t be shown if the entity was newly created). Click OK. Step 5 : After recalculation is done, another dialog will appear to build the flavor (This dialog won’t be shown if the entity was newly created). Build the flavor. Step 6 : Add some data in the Data Studio. And make sure to fill the property used for row wise authorization. (Optional if data is already present.) Step 7 : Click on the navigate icon in the access token. It will navigate to the Data Access Rules screen in the Workspace Hub (Workspace Hub should be assigned to the user). In the Data Access Rules screen, check the generated Data Access Keys. For each record where the access token property is not null, a token should be generated. Now we have successfully generated the Data Access Keys. Now, we have to generate matching User Access Keys to provide access. Step 8 : Now we have to add access tokens to users based on what data they should have access to. Go to the Workspace Hub and create some roles in the application. Step 9 : Create entity.ts file for the row wise authorized entity. And add a method as shown below and correct the logic to match your application requirement. Fire query to application entities, if access is dependent upon application data. Copy this code to a temporary file for clearer view. import { d_invoice as d_invoice_gen } from "invoice_management/entity_gen/d_invoice"; import { KloTransaction } from "kloBo/KloTransaction"; import { AccessTokenHelper, EntityAccessTokenCallbackReturnType } from "kloBo/KloEntity"; export class d_invoice extends d_invoice_gen { static async getAccessTokensForUsers(txn: KloTransaction, flavor: string, version: string, userAppRoleMap: { [user_id: string]: string }, accessTokenHelper: AccessTokenHelper): Promise<EntityAccessTokenCallbackReturnType> { let userIdList = Object.keys(userAppRoleMap); let accessTokensMap: EntityAccessTokenCallbackReturnType = {}; debugger; for (let user_id of userIdList) { /** * Building the EntityAccessTokenCallbackReturnType map. * { * user_id1 : { * access_token: [ token1, token2 ] * }, * user_id2 : { * access_token: [ token3, token4 ] * } * } */ if (!accessTokensMap[user_id]) accessTokensMap[user_id] = { access_tokens: [] }; if (userAppRoleMap[user_id] == "FINANCE_VIEWER") { accessTokensMap[user_id].access_tokens.push( await accessTokenHelper.getAccessToken( "status" /** ID from access token screen - not the property*/, { status: "approved", } /** Object with property : value for properties used in access token.*/ ) ); } else if (userAppRoleMap[user_id] == "CREATOR") { accessTokensMap[user_id].access_tokens.push(await accessTokenHelper.getAccessToken("status", { status: "draft" })); } else if (userAppRoleMap[user_id] == "APPROVER") { accessTokensMap[user_id].access_tokens.push(await accessTokenHelper.getAccessToken("status", { status: "pending" })); } else if (userAppRoleMap[user_id] == "AUDITOR") { accessTokensMap[user_id].access_tokens.push(await accessTokenHelper.getAccessToken("status", { status: "paid" }), await accessTokenHelper.getAccessToken("status", { status: "approved" })); } } return accessTokensMap; } } Note : This example considers a use where each role has access to a set of data, but cases where the User Access Keys should be generated based on application data are also possible. Step 10 : Go to the User Data Access in the Security & Permissions and click on re-calculate, select flavor, entity name and click recalculate. Once done, it should generate access tokens for all the users who the application is assigned, based on the logic. (No token will be generated if the application is not assigned with an Application Role). This method can be debugged by triggering re-calculate from private node registration. Step 11 : Now assign the application to some user, and configure based on the logic written in the getAccessTokensForUsers callback. After assigning the flavor, a token should be generated for the user based on the callback logic. Step 12 : Create a screen with the entity and add it to the menu, and build the flavor. Step 13 : Register with the assigned user. Only the data that has access to should be listed. Thus row wise authorization can be configured.

documents.t: Access token is a string, which acts as a link between the data and user to define which data set the user has access to. Consider the above example. There are access tokens for each record of data (Data Access Keys), and below that there is a set of access token(s) assigned to each user (User Access Keys).

documents.t: Row wise authorization can be enabled only in root entities. Not on child entities. If BO is row wise authorized, all the child entities will also follow the same authorization. If a user has access to the root object, then the user can access all the child objects belonging to that root object.

documents.t: Data Access Keys can be added in two ways. By adding an access token template in the entity. Via callback.
