documents.t: Workspace Hub menu will be visible for Users who are assigned as TESTER or DEVELOPER or SUPERADMIN. Step 1: Go to the menu options and select Workspace Hub. Step 2: The Workspace Hub contains the following screens. Under the menu header, App Lifecycle users who are assigned as TESTER or DEVELOPER or SUPERADMIN wIll find Auth Configuration and Custom Domains menus. Under the menu header,App Lifecycle users who are assigned SUPERADMIN and not as any application role wIll find the App Authorisation menu. First, we will look into the menus under the menu header Workspace Hub. AccountDetails - For overviewing the account details of the user and modifying it. Account Name : Account Name are the basic details of the customer for which the account is created. Account Type: Account Type are the basic details of the customer for which the account is created. Valid Till: Valid till are the subscription period of the account which has been created for the customer. Valid From: Valid from are the subscription period of the account which has been created for the customer. User Management - The User screen lists the users who are filtered based on logged in user’s Auth Configuration whose accounts have been created under current landscape.We can check the details of the users, the User Collections one is assigned , the endpoints and apps assigned. Need help?: Need help is the help and support section in an Workspace Hub that includes options for contacting customer support, such as phone numbers or email details, and links to important documents like Terms and Conditions, Privacy Policy, and Logo sections. You can also find details on sales inquiries or account management contacts. App Management - The Apps screen lists the Apps that are created in the current landscape for which logged in user has MANAGER access . Apps help create new apps, assign users based on roles to the app, and add language and FAQ Keys. use show External checkbox to show/hide external apps (default hide). Use ShowExternal to see external apps assigned to the user as manager. User ShowAll to see all the versions of apps assigned to the user as manager. User Collections - The User Group screen lists the User Collections who are filtered based on logged in user’s Auth Configuration and have been created under the current landscape. A User Group is the section where a group of users using the same application are listed. User Collections are of two types : 1. Individual user group which is created by default for every user. By default individual User Collections are hidden, use show Individual checkbox if needed. Individual User Collections are needed to automatically assign newly created apps to the logged in user. 2. Group user group which was manually created. These groups of users can be assigned to an app group. App Collections - The App Group screen lists the App Collections which are filtered based on logged in user’s Auth Configuration and have been created under the current landscape. The App Group is used to create groups that will consist of apps which fall under a particular project or that fall under a particular user. App Collections are of two types: 1. Individual App group which is created by default during every new , major and minor App creation. By default individual App Collections are hidden, use show Individual checkbox if needed. Individual App Collections are used to assign newly created apps to the logged in user. 2. Group App group which was manually created. One can also add User Collections to the App Collections. Login Sessions - Whenever any account is registered in the application, a new endpoint ID gets created against that account. It can be checked in the endpoint section. Now, we have three menus under the menu header App Lifecycle. Let us delve in to know what each does. Auth Configuration - Here we will find the available Auth Configuration that are available in this tool and under this we can add or remove users according to our requirements. Auth Configuration are used to segregate users, apps , User Collections ,App Collections. It works as authorisation to particular users for apps, users, App Collections and User Collections. Custom Domains - Custom Domains is a URL Development for redirecting a short url to its long url version. This process is done to make the URLs convenient for the end user's understanding. Short URLs improve the user experience by being easier to type out. AI User Quota - AI User quota is a screen that will store the AI seat allocation details for the users. It consists of seat id clicking on which it will navigate to the AI conversation history screen. This screen is only visible to app admins. AI Conversation History - AI conversation history is a screen that has detailed information about the prompts and the corresponding responses that are given by user/’s using particular seats. This screen is only visible to app admins. Now, we have a menu under the menu header App Lifecycle**.** Let us delve in to know what each does. App Authorisation - In this section, the accounts of the current or existing users will be shown and the users can assign or remove apps as and when required. Note:​ After saving in the Users, User Collections and App Collections screen a popup will be shown indicating that Permission has been triggered and can be checked in the Permission Logs screen. User can go to Permission Logs screen in App Lifecycle

1.15.1.1. Business Requirement​ Application configuration wizard is to create a new application in the system by taking the necessary information, an application can also be created by taking a reference of an existing application. 1.15.1.2. Prerequisites​ All configuration tables in the system. The Application wizard and its components in the system. 1.15.1.3.Process Flow​ Path : Wizards → Application Wizard Tcode : /MVN/APP_WIZARD Report : /MVN/RP_APP_WIZARD Execute the Tcode or use Menu to open the wizard. It enters the start page of the wizard as shown below. Wizard steps​ Please read the guidelines provided in each step of the wizard carefully before proceeding with the execution of that step. Name and Integration parameters​ This step is for setting up the application configuration. Input Purpose Possible values Application-Version App and version of the newly created app. Eg:eam-1 Integration Mode Integration mode of app Online/ Offline Integration Type Integration type of app File/Gateway/PI or PO Reference From All Informations will be copied from the reference app to the newly creating app Existing App name and version Enter all the required input as shown above and click continue to proceed to the next step. Connection parameter​ This step is to provide the Connection parameters of the application. Input Purpose Possible values Gateway/PI URL URL of gateway or PI Gateway RFC Gateway RFC name Inbound folder Inbound folder path Outbound folder Outbound folder path Enter all the required input as shown above and click continue to proceed to the next step. Token parameter​ This step is to configure the token parameter of the application for the provided gateway information. Input Purpose Possible values Token URL Token url Username User name of the URL access Password Password of the URL access SSL ID SSL ID of the connection Proxy Proxy RFC: Gateway to SAP Gateway to SAP RFC Once all token parameters are provided, click the ‘TEST’ icon to verify the connection. This will display the connection status as shown below. Click on continue to move to the next step. Middleware parameter​ Modify the default middleware parameter values in this step according to the requirements, then click continue to proceed to the next page. Click the ‘Del’ icon in the table to remove parameters. Message parameter​ Edit the default message parameters in this step based on the requirement and click on continue to move on to the next page. Copy other configurations​ This step involves selecting the configurations to be copied to the new app if a reference app is available. Input Purpose Possible Values Profile determination To copy the profile determination configurations BO Handler To copy the BO Handler configurations Klo Model To copy the Klo Model configurations F4 Mappings To copy the F4 Mappings configurations Select the checkbox if the specified configurations should be copied. This applies only if a reference app is provided in the Name and Integration parameters section. Wizard Finish​ Review the provided details in the wizard summary and click the Complete button to finalize the application creation. 1.15.1.4. Wizard Results​ An application is created with the provided details as below, Connection Parameters:​ Path: Klobase Configuration cockpit -> Application configuration -> Application Configuration T-code : /MVN/KB_VC_APP_CONF Middleware Parameters:​ Path: Klobase Configuration cockpit -> Application configuration -> Application Configuration T-code : /MVN/KB_VC_APP_CONF Message Parameters​ Path: Klobase Configuration cockpit -> Application configuration -> Application Configuration T-code : /MVN/KB_VC_APP_CONF Other Configurations​ If the reference app is provided, the Properties selected in the ‘’Copy Other configuration’’ sections such as Profile Determination, Bo Handler, Klo model and F4 mapping will be copied.

kloBroker is a broker between tenants, clients, and external systems. It enables communication via messaging and queues. kloBroker runs on the master node in the kloSystem. There can be multiple instances, one per kloLandscape. This dialog allows the user to modify klobroker fields such as mw_msg_pick, mw required, notif required, bol enabled, fcm server key, base path, external file size, holding time, notif interval, notif threshold, interval, queue size, threshold, queue creation class, max message per file, SQL batch size, notif pick size and file parallel count. This dialog also allows CRUD on klobroker external fields which contain endpointid, type, destination host, destination port, destination protocol, user ID, password, and destination path. Description for the above fields are as follows: Fields Description MW Msg Pick This implies the number of messages middleware can pick from the tenant_q table. MW Required This implies whether middleware is required or not. Notif Required Server will send push notifications to the device. It will push all notifications to one table(ma_notification_queue). FCM Server Key To sync the message from the server to the device, fcm_server_key is mandatory. Base Path SAP will put files in this folder and the server will pick files. External File Size Size of the external files Notif Interval It will check in the queue at intervals whether the messages are present or not. Notif threshold The Maximum number of notifications the server will pick. Interval For how much time the DB needs to be checked, the Server will check whether the file is available or not in the sap in the folder and if the file is available then it will process or it will not. Threshold The number of messages the server will hold at a time. Notif pick size The number of notifications it can pick at a time

This will only consider SAP_LOCAL or SAP_ONLINE. It will not consider if it has any extra symbols or any extensions like SAP_LOCAL_ or SAP_LOCAL. Description for the above fields are as follows: Fields Description SAP_LOCAL If something is being saved in the DB, then it will go to tenant_q and save in the klarion db, then we need to push to SAP as a JSON message. SAP_ONLINE When we are directly accessing the SAP server without saving in our db, in this case, we use SAP_ONLINE. TYPE Destination Host Here we are maintaining the url provided by SAP. User Id User Id provided by SAP for the url. Password Password provided by SAP for the url. Destination Path When the type is a folder, then we specify a path here. Note :​ File processing. When processing SAP messages by file, txn_user_id has to be maintained in KloBroker configuration, or else, the generated messages will go to error q without user in transaction. The user ID maintained should have required application, row wise authorization(If required), permissions assigned.

A calendar is a set of working and non-working days specified for a particular time interval. This includes holidays and special periods underlying the organisation’s calendar. We have two types of calendars: 1. Calendar 2. Team Calendar
Displays a calendar of a single entity (such as a person, or resource) for the selected time interval.

NAME TYPE DEFAULT VALUE DESCRIPTION appointmentCreate boolean false Determines either user can create appointments on hold and drag. calendarView string week Defines the type of calendar view based on time. In config, users need to bind the appointmentStartDate : js date object, appointmentEndDate: js date object, appointmentTitle: string, appointmentIcon: sap icon URL or image path and appointmentText: string properties of calendar control to the properties of the entity set. Bind the properties of calendar control to the properties of the entity set. After following the above-mentioned steps, a preview of the calendar screen will look like below: There are 4 types of views in the calendar: Day Week Work Week Month By default, the calendar will be displayed in the weekly view. If the developer wants to use a different view then add the calendarView property in the config and select the desired view type. Select the desired view type. Calendar will also provide drag and drop, create and resize of appointments. To use these features developers need to add enableAppointmentsCreate and enableAppointmentsResize, properties in the config of the calendar control. Note: For screen types like Calendar, Team Calendar, Timeline, and kloMap, their respective aggregations—such as appointments or map markers—can be modeled in the same way as card content. KloAttach control is used to capture, record, upload and display the media.
Properties Type Doc

For using the KloAttach control using Page Builder, developers need to have a qualifier of type attachment. Then developers need to select the section in which KloAttach is needed. After selecting the section click and then new -> Controls. Provide the ID to the control and type KloAttach in the control field. Bind the value property of the control with the attachment qualifier type property of your entity. Developers also can drag the qualifier property from the trans node and drop over the section in which they want to use KloAttach control; the control generator will automatically predict the KloAttach control. NOTE: Please note that video recording in IQOO doesn’t work for unsupported codec with the Blob generated from MediaRecorder API. There are 4 modes in KloAttach control: Preview: In this mode Image control will be there with camera control. Users can capture and upload attachments. This mode will also display the captured and uploaded attachment. This is also the default mode of the KloAttach control. w/o preview: In this mode, users can capture and upload all the valid types of media but a preview will not be available. Compact fileUpload: In this mode file upload icon will be there. Users can upload all valid media. fileUpload: In this mode upload icon with the input field will be there. Users can upload all valid media. If developers want to change the mode of the control then add the mode property in control and choose the mode from the f4 of the mode property.Two new properties, `maxFileSizeAttachment` and `showFileSizeRestriction`, along with their validations, have been added for all four modes in the KloAttach control. A text display shows users the file size limit and supported file types (if enabled). Preview mode: If the enabled property of control is false then the camera button will be hidden. The image of the attachment is clickable. On click, it will open in full size in a dialog. With the click of the camera button, a dialog will appear with a live stream. By default, captured image/video will be of quality SD. But this can be configured using control’s property quality This button is used to open the flashlight of the camera. This button will close the camera. This button will open the file uploader. With the click of this button, the image will get captured. This button will switch the mode of the camera. On clicking the icon the camera & video buttons will get switched. Like On a click of this button video recording will start. With the click of this button video recording will stop. After capturing the image the dialog will look like below: On click, the image editing dialog will open with editing options. For knowing more about editing options see the KloFeedBack control. On click, the captured photo will be saved. On click, the dialog will get closed without saving the image. W/O Preview mode: In this mode, only the camera button will be visible. The only difference between review and w/o preview mode is that in w/o preview mode attachments will not be displayed. File upload mode: In this mode file upload button with a text field will be displayed. On click of the file upload button, the system's file explorer will open and the user can select the attachment and upload. The name of the selected attachment will be shown in the text field. Preview of the attachment is not available in this mode. Compact file upload mode: In this mode, only the file upload button will be visible. On click of the file upload button, the system's file explorer will open and the user can select the attachment and upload. Preview of the attachment is not available in this mode.

Developers are also able to change the preview preference of the KloAttach control. For using thumbnails the developer needs to enable the isThumbnailEnabled property in the IAttachment qualifier from the Data Studio. By default, KloAttach will display the original images and videos. Developers can change the preview preference by using the previewPreference property of the KloAttach control. There are 3 types of preview preference are available: Only Thumbnail 2. Only Real 3. On clicking Real This property is applicable only in preview mode. If "Only Thumbnail" then always the thumbnail will be displayed. If 'Only Real' then always a real image will be displayed. If 'On click Real' then a thumbnail will be displayed and on click of an image real image will come into frame. The difference between thumbnails and real images is their size & quality. Thumbnails will have low-quality images & smaller in size as compared to the original images. Developers are also able to change the WaterMark of the KloAttach control. By default, waterMark will not be displayed in the original images and videos. The developer has to mark the watermark property as true to enable that. There are a total of 5 watermark properties: - waterMark Watermark Position Watermark Size Watermark Type Watermark Config The developer can use these properties to change the size, position and type of watermark. If the developer wants to customize the watermark according to his preference, they should use the Watermark config:- In waterMarkConfig, add json Like:- { waterMarkPosition: "top_left", waterMarkColor: 'white', waterMarkSize: 'M', waterMarkType: ['geolocation', 'user', 'Text','Logo'], waterMarkText: 'Solution', waterMarkLogo: 'closedmodules/kloTouch_5/media/logo.png' } if you want to test the logo, the logo should be present in the location specified or you should change it to the current location Default watermark w/o any configuration. Note:- The watermark will only appear on the captured images/videos, it will not appear on uploaded images/videos.

A media type (also known as a Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions or MIME type) indicates the nature and format of a document, file, or assortment of bytes. Mode should be file_upload. mimeType can be an array of strings containing the required mime types . For specific file types(“file_upload”, “compact_file_upload” mode) pass the MIME type array. MIME types are listed in Mime Type Data. Note: There is another property fileType that will accept the file extensions in the format [“pdf”, “xlsx”, “txt”]. This property handles the mimetype of the control automatically. If fileType is provided, then the mimeType property will be ignored. For filetypes “vsd” and “vsdx”, some browser do not have the internal mimetypes maintained. You can use [“vsd”, “*”] in the fileType property for these files.

Extended from sap.m.DynamicDateRange KloDateRange control is extended from sap.m.DynamicDateRange, it is customised to support the date range selection and search in the FrameWork. If a value is binded to the dsrc field of the control in the UIEditor, the control will be binded to <property_id>_LEQ and <property_id>_GEQ, these values will be set on the Query and whenever query is executed, the tokens will be generated for <= and >= values in the query. It also supports dateFormat property that will display the selected date values based on the given dateFormat value. KloDateRange control is only supported in the search section.

Property name Type Default value Description endDate any null Binding for value set in the model, whenever value is selected from the control, the date object is updated to the path where endDate is binded in the model startDate any null Binding for value set in the model, whenever value is selected from the control, the date object is updated to the path where startDate is binded in the model displayFormat string undefined Based on the displayFormat provided, the datevalue is shown in the control after selecting a value. defaultRangeOperator string DATETIMERANGE Specifies the default operator to be used when reconstructing the date range value after a reset. If the control's current value does not contain an operator (e.g. after a reset clears the value), this property is used as the fallback. If not specified, DATETIMERANGE is used. Accepted values are valid DynamicDateRange operator keys such as DATETIMERANGE, DATERANGE, THISWEEK, etc.

Whenever a screen is created with wizard, fields that have datatype timestamp, are rendered as KloDateRange with default property standardOptions: [“DateTimeRange”]. In the list/detail section, the control class will be sap.m.DateTimePicker with show as label enabled. When a property is manually dropped from the search transnode to the search section, the control class will be KloDateRange for the properties of datatype timestamp. Note: When the application font size is increased, certain standard controls such as m.dateRange may not re-render all UI elements consistently. This can lead to layout issues where text is reflowed but action buttons are not, resulting in overlapping content and non-actionable buttons. To avoid this behavior, it is recommended to use kloDateRange instead of m.dateRange. The kloDateRange control handles dynamic font scaling and UI re-rendering correctly, ensuring proper popup alignment, button accessibility, and consistent user interaction across different display and accessibility settings.

Class: KloGuid
Extended from KloLink which is extended sap.m.Link. KloGuid allows developers to display GUID property data in a shortened format.

KloGuid allows displaying GUID property data in a shortened format,showing the first four characters, followed by four dots, and then the last four characters (e.g., abcd....lmno). When the user hovers over it, a copy icon appears, enabling them to easily copy the full GUID. The GUID, which is 32 characters in length, is formatted by displaying the first four characters, followed by '....', and then the last four characters, making it more concise and visually suitable for display on the screen. When you hover over the link, an icon will appear. Upon clicking the icon, the entire 32-character GUID will be copied to the clipboard, allowing it to be used as needed. Additionally, clicking the link will navigate you to the detailed page.

The KloMultiCombo box control is commonly used to enable users to select one or more options from a predefined list. The control provides an editable input field to filter the list, and a dropdown arrow to open the list of available options. The select options in the list have checkboxes that permit multi-selection.

Use the kloMultiCombo box if​ The user needs to select one or more options from a long list of options (maximum of approximately 200). The values of the option list contain secondary information that does not need to be displayed right away. Do not use the kloMultiCombo box if​ The user needs to choose between two options, such as ON or OFF and YES or NO. In this case, consider using a switch control instead. You need to display more than one attribute. In this case, consider using the kloInput instead. The user needs to search on multiple attributes. In this case, consider using the kloInput instead. Your use case requires all available options to be displayed right away, without any user interaction. In this case, consider using checkboxes instead. You want to enable users to add custom values. In this case, consider using the multi-input field. Your use case requires more options to choose from. In this case, consider using the multi-input field, either with the select dialog or value help dialog (for more than 1000 items).
The kloMultiCombo box is optimized for keyboard and mouse interaction. Size S​ Size M​ Size L​

Input Field​ The input field (2) can display a placeholder text (6) when it’s empty, or a token (1) if a value is selected. Components of the kloMultiCombo box Dropdown Trigger​ The dropdown button (3) collapses and expands the dropdown list. Option List​ The option list (7) contains a list of selectable options (5). Clicking the label of an entry closes the option list and creates a token for the selected option. To enable multi-selection, every entry also has a checkbox (4). Clicking a checkbox creates a token. The option list remains open.

Select a Value​ There are three ways to select an item from the list: Tick the checkbox (option list remains open). Click the label of a select option (option list is closed). Use the keyboard (spacebar or Enter). The user clicks the input field to place the cursor in the field (1). Clicking the down arrow displays the list (2). As the user types into the input field, the list is filtered accordingly (3). The arrow up and arrow down keys move the focus within the list (4), while the typed text remains in the input field. Selected options are automatically entered into the input field as tokens (5). If the user selects items from the filtered option list (3) by clicking the checkbox or by pressing the space bar on the keyboard, the text entered in the input field remains. The option list stays open. If the user selects items by clicking the label or by pressing Enter, the entered text is cleared and the option list is closed. The shift key can be used to select a range of items (shift+click marks the end of the range, shift+arrow up / shift+arrow down extends or narrows the selection range in the corresponding direction. Ctrl+A selects or deselects all items. If selecting all items is a common use case, you can also show a Select All checkbox at the top of the list (property: showSelectAll). Reviewing Tokens​ If tokens have been selected, and the multi-combo box is not in focus, the input field displays as many tokens as possible in the available space. If more tokens have been selected, an [n] More label indicates the number of hidden tokens. The tokens in the input field appear in the order in which they were selected. Clicking the [n] More label opens a popover below the input field, in which all selected items are shown. The user can deselect an item by clicking its checkbox or label. If the length of the last selected token exceeds the width of the input field, a label [n] Item/s is shown when the field is not in focus. Clicking the [n] Item/s label opens a popover below the input field, in which all selected items are shown. The user can deselect an item by clicking its checkbox or label. If there is only one token in the input field and its length exceeds the width of the input field, the text is truncated. Clicking the token opens a popover below the input field, in which the full text of the token is shown. Multi-combo box - '1 Item' case (desktop) Filtering the Option List​ When the user starts typing in the input field, the option list is filtered. Only items that match the characters entered are shown in the dropdown list. The default filtering method is “starts with per term”, which matches the beginning of each word in an item’s text. If the filtered option list contains items that start with the characters entered by the user, the first matching, unselected item is auto-completed in the input field.

Placeholder​ Don’t use the placeholder attribute as an alternative to a label. This is important because the placeholder text will be overwritten as soon as the form is filled out. Labels are necessary because they indicate the meaning of the form fields if the placeholders are no longer visible. Show a placeholder only if the user needs a hint about what data to enter. Don’t repeat the content of the label. A hint could be a sample value or a brief description of the expected format. For more information about how to use the placeholder, see input field. Option List​ Keep the label of an entry in the select option list as short as possible because the list uses single lines only. Values that are too long may be truncated. If you need to indicate that none of the selection options are selected, show a blank input field. Define a default selection whenever possible. The kloMultiCombo box cannot display columns. If you want to show two values in the option list, show the leading information first, followed by the secondary information in parentheses, such as Walldorf (Germany). Don’t disable items in the option list. If an item can’t be selected, hide it. Width​ You can adjust the width of the option list to some extent. The multi-combo box control is usually used in forms, where the width is determined by the form element or container in which it is embedded. Therefore, we don’t recommend defining a fixed width, but rather working with proper layout containers such as the form, simple form, or responsive grid layout, and with the layout data property, where the width is defined. If you need to restrict the width to a defined value, set the width accordingly. Keep in mind that there’s no horizontal scrolling in the option list. Entries that are too long are truncated and users won’t be able to read them. To avoid this, you can enable wrapping (property: wrapping). additionalTextList, textList and keyList: keyList accepts the value which is the property in the value help suggestionItems. When provided property goes as relative binding to the suggestionItems aggregation. And the value is the key for the suggestion items. textList accepts the value which is the property in the value help suggestionItems. When provided property goes as relative binding to the suggestionItems aggregation. And the value is the text for the suggestion items. additionalTextList accepts the value which is the property in the value help suggestionItems. When provided property goes as relative binding to the suggestionItems aggregation. And the value is the additional for the suggestion items. showSecondaryValues property needs to be set to true so that the additionalText is shown in the suggestionItems. Note: For binding properties, we follow the predefined sequence: ["geoLocation", "avatarTitle", "src", "dateValue", "selected", "selectedKey", "selectedKeys", "value", "guid", "text", "state"]. Accordingly, for kloMultiComboBox, the binding should be implemented using the selectedKey property Note: For more information please refer to this sap.m.MultiComboBox.

Extended from sap.ui.core.Control. KloShape lets the developer include the shape controls in the UI (rectangle and oval). The developer can control properties like height, width, fill, border, opacity, etc., KloShape can also be used in the form subscreen.

NAME TYPE DEFAULT VALUE DESCRIPTION width sap.ui.core.CSSSize 100% Specifies the width of the control. height sap.ui.core.CSSSize 100% Specifies the height of the control. shape string rectangle Specifies the required shape. Supported Shapes include rectangle and oval. If a square and circle are specified then the dimensions are equal to the width of the control. fill sap.ui.core.CSSColor black Specifies the background fill of the control. opacity string 1 Specifies the opacity of the control. borderColor sap.ui.core.CSSColor #fff Specifies the border colour of the control. borderThickness sap.ui.core.CSSSize 0px Specifies the thickness of the control. borderRadius sap.ui.core.CSSSize 0px Specifies the border radius of the control. image string “” Specifies the background image of the control.
KloShape control can be used if the developer requires a shape of suitable dimensions and style. The dimensions and styles can be controlled via the properties of the control.
NAME TYPE DESCRIPTION press - Triggered whenever the control is clicked. hover - Triggered whenever the user hovers over the control.

Class: KloSignature

Extended from sap.m.Input. It renders a KloSignature control based on its mode. There are 3 modes of kloSignature control ( inline, popup, w/o preview ). Value property is mandatory for KloSignature. The signature will be saved as an attachment.
Version 5.7 and 6.0

NAME TYPE DEFAULT VALUE DESCRIPTION value object {} Value property must be an attachment property. height sap.ui.core.CSSSize 150px Height property is only applied to the signature image. In inline mode, height must be in px. width sap.ui.core.CSSSize 250px The width property is only applied to the signature image. In inline mode, the width must be in px. title string Signature Pad This property will be used as a title for the header of the dialog icon sap.ui.core.URI sap-icon://kloFontg/edit Icon to be displayed for the signature control button. mode string popup There are 3 modes for kloSignature. Inline:- In this mode, the signature can be done at the same place where it's displayed.Popup:- In this mode on click of the signature button, the signature pad will open where the user can sign.w/o preview:- In this mode, signature image will not be displayed. With the click of the sign button, the signature pad will open. pen boolean true whether you want to use a pen or not. penSize int 4 Thickness of the pen. penColor sap.ui.core.CSSColor blue The colour of the pen in which the user will do the signature. palette boolean true Whether to display a palette or not. Not applicable for inline mode. crop boolean true Whether to display a crop button or not. Not applicable for inline mode. enabled boolean true Indicates whether the user can interact with the control or not. visible boolean true Indicates whether this control is visible to the user or not.

For using the KloSignature control using Page Builder, developers need to have a qualifier of type signature. Then developers need to select the section in which KloSignature is needed. After selecting the section, right-click and then new -> control. Provide the ID to the control and type KloSignature in the control field. Bind the value property of the control with the signature qualifier type property of your entity. Developers also can drag the qualifier property from the trans node and drop over the section in which they want to use kloSignature control; the control generator will automatically predict the KloSignature control. There are 3 modes in KloSignature control: Inline: In this mode, the signature can be done at the same place where it's displayed. Popup:- In this mode on click of the signature button, the signature pad will open where the user can sign. This is also the default mode of KloSignature control. w/o preview:- In this mode, signature image will not be displayed. With a click on the sign button, the signature pad will open. If developers want to change the mode of the control then add the mode property in control and choose the mode from the f4 of the mode property. Inline mode: With a click of this button, this button will get replaced with the save, reset and cancel button. Now the users can do signatures with a mouse or touch. With a click of this button, the signature will get saved. On click, the signature pad will get cleaned. On click, the save, reset and cancel will get replaced with the edit button and now the pad becomes non-editable. If the enabled property of the control is false then the footer of the control will be blank (no action button). Popup mode: If the enabled property of control is false then the edit button will be hidden. With a click of this button, the signature pad will open in a dialog and the user can do a signature with a mouse or touch on the pad. With a click of this button, a signature will be saved. On click, the dialog will get closed. With the click of this button, more editing options will open. After selecting the options, this button’s icon will change based on the selected option. This button is to select the pen. This button's task is to clean the signature pad. This button is for cropping the signature. This button is a colour palette. The selected colour will be used for signature. W/o Preview mode: In w/o preview mode, only the pen button will be displayed. The Only difference between popup & and w/o preview mode is that in w/o preview mode signature will not be displayed. With a click of this button, the signature pad will open in a dialog and the user can do a signature with a mouse or touch on the pad. With a click of this button, the signature will get saved. On click, the dialog will get closed. With the click of this button, more editing options will open. After selecting the options, this button’s icon will change based on the selected option. This button is to select the pen. This button's task is to clean the signature pad. This button is for cropping the signature. This button is a colour palette. The selected colour will be used for signature.
NAME DESCRIPTION onCancel Fired when the close button is clicked in the KloSignature dialog box.

Map control (KloConfigMap) is used to display the locations on the map. Configuration : To use the map, google_maps_api_key should be maintained in the config.json(mm_klobroker)

NAME TYPE DEFAULT VALUE DESCRIPTION lat float 1 It will set the position of the map latitude-wise. lng float 1 It will set the position of the map longitude-wise. width sap.ui.core.CSSSize auto It will set the width of the map. height sap.ui.core.CSSSize 25em It will set the height of the map. mapTypeId string terrain mapTypeId will be used to show a map in [terrain, satellite] view. zoom int 16 It will set the zoom level of the map. centre boolean true If the true recenter button comes at the right-hand side of the map. navigation boolean true If the true recenter button comes at the right top of the map. mapType boolean false If the true recenter button will come at the left top on the map. fitToMarkers boolean true If true, the map will be focused on the markers. language string English To select the language for the map. Ex. for Hindi it’s ‘hi’, for arabic it’s ‘ar’, for english ‘en’.(First two letter of the language) showMyLoc boolean FALSE It will show the pin for the current location. myLocIcon G-Icons It will set the icon inside the pin. myLocPin boolean FALSE It will hide the pin and show only the icon for the current location myLocIconColor sap.ui.core.CSSColor It will set the colour of the icon. myLocPinColor sap.ui.core.CSSColor It will set the colour of the pin.

This control will be used as a screen type. A preview of the section where this control is added will display the map with the added pins. For using this control first select the screen type of the section as map. Then for using the map's properties, add config to the respective section. In config, you can use the properties of kloConfigMap. KloConfigMap has markers as a hidden aggregation. For adding markers drag a property ( which has a geoLocation qualifier) from the trans node and drop over configMap. The map has only 2 views [terrain, satellite]. Demonstration of the kloConfigMap control’s implementation using Page Builder,. Preview of map: By default map will be shown in terrain view. For changing the default view of the map developers need to add the mapTypeId property in the config of the map, then select the desired mapTypeId from the property’s f4. Preview of map control in satellite view. If the developer wants to provide the control to the user for changing the view of the map then enable the mapType property in the config. Preview after enabling the mapType. For displaying the pin on the map, drag the property of type geolocation from the trans node (entity or entityset) and drop it on the config of the map. Preview after adding geolocation qualifier. In the above preview, default markers are displayed. Developers can customise the markers by selecting the class name as KloMapMarker and changing the pin, pinColor, size, icon and iconColor properties. If developers want to change the size of the pin then assign the size in px in the size property of KloMapMarker. If developers want to display only icons then they can mark the pin property as false and select the icon from f4 of icon properties, change the colour using the iconColor property. If developers want to change the size of the icon then assign the size in px in the size property of KloMapMarker. Over the map pins/ icons are clickable, on click of the pins/ icons popover will open in which the card will be displayed. That card will display the content which is added in the same section whose screen type is a map. Action button on the map: On click of this button, the info event of KloMapMarker will be fired. Developers need to define the info event. With a click of this button, Google Maps will open and display the path between the clicked pin and the current location. With the click of this button, Google Maps will open and display the path between the first pin rendered on a map and the current location. With a click of the button, it will recenter the map to the current location of the device/system.

documents.t: This is an implementation of drag and drop from grid list to multi calendar. A multicalendar section and a grid section is required for this integration. In controller onSectionEnter(eg. onMulticaEnter) method of multicalendar is added. There the control instance is stored with the “getActiveControlById” method of the controller. This is required because while creating the drag and drop config of the grid the target element Id should be provided which in this case will be the multi calendar’s internal table. With this setup the drag and drop should work. To create an appointment in the multi calendar on drop check out the “onDrop” method in the below given code example. For more info check out this link. Note: For safari or iOS cordova the ‘event.dataTransfer.setData('text/plain', "")’ is required in onDragStart event otherwise the drag and drop won’t work.

documents.t: public onMulticaEnter() { const oGrid = this.getActiveControlById('','section01'); const oMultica = this.getActiveControlById('','s_people__list02'); const oDND = new sap.ui.core.dnd.DragDropInfo({ sourceAggregation: "rows", targetAggregation:"items", targetElement: oMultica.getId() + "-Table", dragEnter: (oEvent) => { event.dataTransfer.setData('text/plain', ""); //Safari Specific **IMPORTANT: Here event is browser event not oEvent. this.onDragEnter(oEvent); }, dragStart: (oEvent) => { this.onDragStart(oEvent) }, drop: (oEvent) => { this.onDrop(oEvent) } }); oGrid.addDragDropConfig(oDND); } public async onDrop(oEvent){ let oDroppedControl = oEvent.getParameter("droppedControl"); let cliId = oDroppedControl.getId(); let rowId = cliId.replace("-CLI", ""); let calRow = (<sap.ui.core.Control>sap.ui.getCore().byId(rowId)); let sPath = this.getPathFromControl(calRow); const iIndex = sPath.split("/").pop(); const oChildEnt = (this.tm.getTN('r_appoint').getData())[iIndex]; let calendarRow = ""; let rowStartDate = ""; let targetObj = oEvent.getParameter("droppedControl") let browserEvent = oEvent.mParameters.browserEvent let browserTarget = ""; let intervalNumber = ""; if (browserEvent.target) { browserTarget = browserEvent.target; //@ts-ignore if (browserTarget?.id) {//@ts-ignore if (browserTarget?.id.indexOf("CalRow-AppsInt") !== -1) {//@ts-ignore intervalNumber = browserTarget?.id?.split("CalRow-AppsInt")[1] || 0; } } } if (targetObj.getAggregation("cells").length > 1) { calendarRow = targetObj.getAggregation("cells")[1]; if (calendarRow) {//@ts-ignore rowStartDate = calendarRow?.getStartDate(); } } let iIntervalNumber = isNaN(+intervalNumber) ? 0 : +intervalNumber; let startdate = new Date(new Date(rowStartDate).getTime() + iIntervalNumber * 60 * 60000); let enddate = new Date(startdate.getTime() + 60 * 60000); await oChildEnt['r_appoint'].newEntityP().then(ent => { ent['startdate'] = startdate; ent['enddate'] = enddate; ent['title'] = "Drop Appointment" ent['text'] = "Created by drop from list" ent['icon'] = "sap-icon://background" }); }

documents.t: The Tree Screen Type is designed to represent hierarchical data in a structured manner. It allows users to visualize relationships between parent and child nodes, making it ideal for displaying nested information such as organizational charts, file systems, or any other hierarchical datasets.

To prepare the data for a Tree Screen Type, we will use a JSON format that represents the hierarchical structure (If your Entityset has such structured data, you can use your entityset for the tree). Here’s a sample JSON array: [{ "key_01": "value_1", "key_02": "value_2", "key_03": "value_3", "child": [{ "key_01": "value_11", "key_02": "value_22", "key_03": "value_33", "child": [{ "key_01": "value_111", "key_02": "value_222", "key_03": "value_333", "child": [{ "key_01": "value_1111", "key_02": "value_2222", "key_03": "value_3333", }] }] }] }]

Each object represents a node in the tree. The child array holds nested objects, representing the child nodes. Key names for child nodes are consistent with parent nodes, ensuring a clear relationship. We will store the data in other type of transnode.

Create one pageArea with screentype, fit_to_area and a section with screentype, tree. In the section layout, add one property autoHeight as true. This ensures that the section dynamically adjusts its height based on the content displayed.
Create other type of transnode (If you are using entityset, then you can use that transnode).

Add Controls for Data Binding Create controls within the section for each key in your JSON data (key_01, key_02, key_03). Bind the section to the other type of transnode that contains the hierarchical JSON data. Ensure that each control is correctly bound to the corresponding key in the JSON structure.
